british-virgin-islands.text: The foreign relations of the British Virgin Islands are largely conducted on behalf of the British Virgin Islands Government by the United Kingdom through the Foreign and Commonwealth Office as a result of the Territory's status as a British Overseas Territory.
british-virgin-islands.title: Foreign relations of the British Virgin Islands

british-virgin-islands.text: The colony of the British Virgin Islands has issued its own stamps since 1866. The first Post Office was opened in Tortola in 1787.
british-virgin-islands.title: Postage stamps and postal history of the British Virgin Islands

british-virgin-islands.text: Holidays in the British Virgin Islands are predominantly religious holidays, with a number of additional national holidays.
british-virgin-islands.title: Public holidays in the British Virgin Islands

british-virgin-islands.text: The systems of transport in the British Virgin Islands include 113 kilometres of highway and a harbour at Road Town.
british-virgin-islands.title: Transport in the British Virgin Islands

british-virgin-islands.text: Country Code: +1284 International Call Prefix: 011 Calls from the British Virgin Islands to the US, Canada, and other NANP Caribbean nations, are dialled as 1 + NANP area code + 7-digit number.
british-virgin-islands.title: Telecommunications in the British Virgin Islands

brunei.text: The politics of Brunei take place in a framework of an absolute monarchy, whereby the Sultan of Brunei is both head of state and head of government. Brunei is the only ruling state with an absolute monarchy in Southeast Asia. As of 2023, Brunei is one of seven absolute monarchies in the world.
brunei.title: Politics of Brunei

brunei.text: The demographic features of Brunei include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population. Like neighbouring countries, Brunei is a Malay-majority country.
brunei.title: Demographics of Brunei

brunei.text: Education in Brunei is provided or regulated by the Government of Brunei through the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
brunei.title: Education in Brunei

brunei.text: Brunei's healthcare system is managed by the Brunei Ministry of Health and funded by the General Treasury. It consists of around 15 health centers, ten clinics and 22 maternal facilities, considered to be of reasonable standard. There are also two private hospitals.
brunei.title: Health in Brunei

brunei.text: This is a list of rivers in Brunei.
brunei.title: List of rivers of Brunei

brunei.text: The geology of Brunei is primarily made up of Cenozoic rocks overlying deeper rock units on the island of Borneo. Rocks from the Oligocene through the Holocene are up to 15 kilometers thick.
brunei.title: Geology of Brunei

brunei.text: The wildlife of Brunei is one of its primary attractions. Tropical evergreen rainforest makes up the majority of the country's natural vegetation. 81% of the land is covered by forests, with 59% being primary forests and 22% being secondary forests and plantations.
brunei.title: Wildlife of Brunei

brunei.text: Brunei maintains diplomatic relations with 171 out of 193 countries, joined ASEAN on 7 January 1984, one week after resuming full independence, and gives its ASEAN membership the highest priority in its foreign relations. Brunei joined the United Nations in September 1984.
brunei.title: Foreign relations of Brunei

brunei.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Brunei. Brunei is located on the north coast of the island of Borneo, in Southeast Asia.
brunei.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Brunei

brunei.text: Brunei is a southeast Asian country located on Borneo between the states of Sabah and Sarawak which are part of Malaysia. There is a wide array of native folk music, and dance.
brunei.title: Music of Brunei

brunei.text: Bruneian cuisine concerns the cuisine of Brunei. It is similar to, and heavily influenced by the cuisine of neighbouring Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia, with additional influences from India, China, Thailand, and the Middle East.
brunei.title: Bruneian cuisine

brunei.text: This is a list of holidays in Brunei.
brunei.title: Public holidays in Brunei

picture.credit: sam garza from Los Angeles, USA

brunei.text: Among religions in Brunei, Sunni Islam is predominant. In 2021, the government census showed that 82.1% of Brunei's population is Muslim. However, other religions also have a considerable foothold in Brunei: 6.7% of the population is Christian and another 6.3% is Buddhist.
brunei.title: Religion in Brunei

brunei.text: There are a number of languages spoken in Brunei. The official language of the state of Brunei is Standard Malay, the same Malaccan dialect that is the basis for the standards in Malaysia and Indonesia. This came into force on 29 September 1959, with the signing of Brunei 1959 Constitution.
brunei.title: Languages of Brunei

brunei.text: Sport in Brunei covers the variety of sports that are played, from amateur to professional levels, across the sultanate of Brunei Darussalam, in addition to individuals and teams who are sent to compete in tournaments both home and abroad.
brunei.title: Sport in Brunei

brunei.text: Transport in Brunei consists of air, land, and sea transport. Previously there was some rail transport in Brunei, but eventually most of it was closed down. Several public and commercial sector organizations are in charge of creating and overseeing these networks and infrastructures.
brunei.title: Transport in Brunei

brunei.text: Tourism in Brunei is governed by the Ministry of Primary Resources and Tourism, which is planning to diversify Brunei's tourism to include adventure tourism, ecotourism and Islamic tourism.
brunei.title: Tourism in Brunei

brunei.text: Brunei possesses an extensive system of telecommunications, including telephone and mobile phone service, internet service, television and radio.
brunei.title: Telecommunications in Brunei

brunei.text: Energy in Brunei is related to all of the type of energy and its related infrastructure used in Brunei. Natural gas and diesel are used significantly in Brunei to generate domestic electricity, as well as gasoline and diesel to power its roads.
brunei.title: Energy in Brunei

bulgaria.text: Bulgaria is a parliamentary representative democratic republic, whereby the prime minister is the head of government, and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government. Legislative power is vested in both the government and the National Assembly.
bulgaria.title: Politics of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: The demography of the Republic of Bulgaria is monitored by the National Statistical Institute of Bulgaria. Demographic features of the population of Bulgaria include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and others.
bulgaria.title: Demographics of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Education in Bulgaria is guided and overseen by Bulgarian Ministry of Education and Science. Compulsory education includes three years of pre-primary education, primary education, and secondary education. The schools start by age of seven and end the age of 18.
bulgaria.title: Education in Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Bulgaria had the third highest mortality in Europe, at 708 per 100,000 population in 2015. The four European regions with the highest death rates from diseases of the circulatory system were all in Bulgaria.
bulgaria.title: Health in Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: This is a list of rivers in Bulgaria, organised geographically, taken clockwise from the westernmost tributaries of the Danube drainage.
bulgaria.title: List of rivers of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: The geology of Bulgaria consists of two major structural features. The Rhodope Massif in southern Bulgaria is made up of Archean, Proterozoic and Cambrian rocks and is a sub-province of the Thracian-Anatolian polymetallic province.
bulgaria.title: Geology of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Mountains constitute a significant part of Bulgaria and are dominant in the southwest and central parts. Bulgaria's highest mountains are Rila and Pirin.
bulgaria.title: List of mountains in Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: The foreign relations of Bulgaria are overseen by the Ministry of Foreign Relations headed by the Minister of Foreign Affairs. Situated in Southeast Europe, Bulgaria is a member of both NATO and the European Union. It maintains diplomatic relations with 187 countries.
bulgaria.title: Foreign relations of Bulgaria

picture.credit: Original uploader was Мико at bg.wikipedia

bulgaria.text: Bulgaria liberated itself from the Ottoman Empire in 1878 and, although it remained de jure autonomous until the proclamation of full independence in 1908, it acted as a de facto independent country.
bulgaria.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: The music of Bulgaria refers to all forms of music associated with the country of Bulgaria, including classical, folk, popular music, and other forms.
bulgaria.title: Music of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Bulgarian cuisine is part of the cuisine of Eastern Europe, sharing characteristics with other Balkan cuisines. Bulgarian cooking traditions are diverse because of geographical factors such as climatic conditions suitable for a variety of vegetables, herbs, and fruit.
bulgaria.title: Bulgarian cuisine

bulgaria.text: The official public holidays in Bulgaria are listed in the table below.
bulgaria.title: Public holidays in Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Religion in Bulgaria has been dominated by Christianity since its adoption as the state religion in 864. The dominant form of the religion is Eastern Orthodox Christianity within the fold of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church.
bulgaria.title: Religion in Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: The official language of Bulgaria is Bulgarian, which is spoken natively by 86.2% of the country's population. Other major languages are Turkish, and Romani according to 2021 census. Two main varieties of Romani language spoken in the country are Balkan Romani and Vlax Romani.
bulgaria.title: Languages of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Bulgaria has been producing films since 1915. Bulgarian cinema is known for the pioneering work of directors like Donyo Donev in the field of animation. The filming and screening of Vasil Gendov's film Bulgaran is Gallant is considered to be the beginning of Bulgarian cinematography.
bulgaria.title: Cinema of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Bulgaria has established traditions in a great variety of sports.
bulgaria.title: Sport in Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Bulgarian literature is literature written by Bulgarians or residents of Bulgaria, or written in the Bulgarian language; usually the latter is the defining feature.
bulgaria.title: Bulgarian literature

bulgaria.text: Transport in Bulgaria is dominated by road transport. As of 2024, the country had 879 kilometers of highways and another 117 km under construction. The total length of the network is almost 40,000 km, divided nearly in half between the national and the municipal road network.
bulgaria.title: Transport in Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Tourism in Bulgaria is a significant contributor to the country's economy. Situated at the crossroads of the East and West, Bulgaria has been home to many civilizations: Thracians, Greeks, Romans, Eastern Romans or Byzantines, Slavs, Bulgars, and Ottomans.
bulgaria.title: Tourism in Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Telecommunications in Bulgaria include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
bulgaria.title: Telecommunications in Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Prior to World War II, agriculture in Bulgaria was the leading sector in the Bulgarian economy. In 1939, agriculture contributed 65 percent of Net material product, and four out of every five Bulgarians were employed in agriculture.
bulgaria.title: Agriculture in Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Energy in Bulgaria is among the most important sectors of the national economy and encompasses energy and electricity production, consumption and transportation in Bulgaria.
bulgaria.title: Energy in Bulgaria

burkina-faso.text: According to the 1991 Constitution of Burkina Faso, the politics of Burkina Faso take place in the form of a semi-presidential republic, with powers separated between the executive, legislative, and judicial branches.
burkina-faso.title: Politics of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Burkina Faso's 22 million people belong to two major West African cultural groups: the Gur and the Mandé. The Voltaic are far more numerous and include the Mossi, who make up about one-half of the population.
burkina-faso.title: Demographics of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Education in Burkina Faso is structured in much the same way as in the rest of the world: primary, secondary, and higher education. As of 2008, despite efforts to improve education, the country had the lowest adult literacy rate in the world.
burkina-faso.title: Education in Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: A landlocked sub-Saharan country, Burkina Faso is among the poorest countries in the world—44 percent of its population lives below the international poverty line of US$1.90 per day—and it ranks 185th out of 188 countries on UNDP's 2016 Human Development Index.
burkina-faso.title: Health in Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: This is a list of streams and rivers in Burkina Faso. Burkina Faso has three main rivers — the Black Volta, the Red Volta and the White Volta. Areas near rivers are affected by tsetse flies and simulium flies.
burkina-faso.title: List of rivers of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: The geology of Burkina Faso is dominated by Precambrian rocks of the Guinea Rise, a dome of Archaean rocks, composed largely of migmatites, gneisses and amphibolites, over which lie the greenstone belts of the early Proterozoic age.
burkina-faso.title: Geology of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Burkina Faso is largely wild bush country with a mixture of grass and small trees in varying proportions. The savanna region is mainly grassland in the rainy season and semi desert during the harmattan period.
burkina-faso.title: Wildlife of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Burkina Faso has good relations with the European Union, African and certain Asian countries. According to the U.S.
burkina-faso.title: Foreign relations of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Burkina Faso, known as Upper Volta until July 1984. The story of the posts in Burkina Faso begins in the 1890s, with French penetration into the area and the establishment of military posts.
burkina-faso.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: The music of Burkina Faso includes the folk music of 60 different ethnic groups.
burkina-faso.title: Music of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Burkinabe cuisine, the cuisine of Burkina Faso, is similar to the cuisines in many parts of West Africa, and is based on staple foods of sorghum, millet, rice, fonio, maize, peanuts, potatoes, beans, yams and okra. Rice, maize and millet are the most commonly eaten grains.
burkina-faso.title: Burkinabe cuisine

burkina-faso.text: This is a list of holidays in Burkina Faso.
burkina-faso.title: Public holidays in Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Burkina Faso is a religiously diverse society, with Islam being the dominant religion. According to the latest 2019 census, 63.8% of the population adheres to Islam.
burkina-faso.title: Religion in Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Burkina Faso is a multilingual country. An estimated 70 languages are spoken there, of which about 66 are indigenous. Mooré or the Mossi language is spoken by about 52.5% of the population, mainly in the central region around the capital, Ouagadougou.
burkina-faso.title: Languages of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: The cinema of Burkina Faso is one of the more significant in Africa, with a history that spans several decades and includes the production of many award-winning films.
burkina-faso.title: Cinema of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Sport in Burkina Faso is widespread and includes football, basketball, baseball, cycling, rugby union, handball, tennis, athletics, boxing, and martial arts.
burkina-faso.title: Sport in Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Burkinabé literature grew out of oral tradition, which remains important. In 1934, during French occupation, Dim-Dolobsom Ouedraogo published his Maximes, pensées et devinettes mossi, a record of the oral history of the Mossi people.
burkina-faso.title: Burkinabe literature

burkina-faso.text: The art of Burkina Faso is the product of a rich cultural history. Many of the ancient artistic traditions for which Africa is so well known have been preserved in Burkina Faso because so many people continue to honor the ancestral spirits, and the spirits of nature.
burkina-faso.title: Art of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Transport in Burkina Faso consists primarily of road, air and rail transportation. The World Bank classified country's transportation as underdeveloped but noted that Burkina Faso is a natural geographic transportation hub for West Africa.
burkina-faso.title: Transport in Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Burkina Faso has many interesting locations for tourists. However, the country annually receives less tourism than most African countries.
burkina-faso.title: Tourism in Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Telecommunications in Burkina Faso include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet. The telephony market in Burkina Faso is still relatively underdeveloped. Although mobile penetration is just over 100%, it is still below the African average.
burkina-faso.title: Telecommunications in Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Agriculture in Burkina Faso has tremendous potential.
burkina-faso.title: Agriculture in Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Energy in Burkina Faso is sourced primarily from diesel and heavy fuel, with some access to hydropower and solar. Burkina Faso produced 69 kilotonnes of oil equivalent of energy in 2015, 89.8% of which was generated from fossil fuels. Final consumption of electricity was 86 ktoe.
burkina-faso.title: Energy in Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Gold mining often plays a significant role in Burkina Faso’s economy. Burkina Faso has become Africa's 4th biggest producer of gold in 2012. Production of mineral commodities is limited to cement, dolomite, gold, granite, marble, phosphate rock, pumice, other volcanic materials, and salt.
burkina-faso.title: Mining industry of Burkina Faso

burundi.text: The politics of Burundi take place in a framework of a transitional presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the president of Burundi is both head of state and head of government, and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government.
burundi.title: Politics of Burundi

burundi.text: Demographic features of the population of Burundi include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects. At 206.1 persons per km2, Burundi has the second-largest population density in Sub-Saharan Africa.
burundi.title: Demographics of Burundi

burundi.text: Education is compulsory in Burundi for six years between the ages of seven and 13. Theoretically, primary education is free at the point of use. Primary education in Burundi spans six grades between the ages of 7 and 13.
burundi.title: Education in Burundi

burundi.text: Burundi is one of the poorest countries in the world, with a population of 14.4 million people as of 2025. Generally, there have been some improvements in the key health indicators such as life expectancy, child mortality and maternal mortality over the last fifty years.
burundi.title: Health in Burundi

burundi.text: This list of rivers in Burundi is a partial list of the larger rivers, arranged by drainage basin, with tributaries indented under each parent stream's name.
burundi.title: List of rivers of Burundi

burundi.text: The geology of Burundi consists largely of metamorphic rocks of Proterozoic age with inliers of basement rocks of Archaean age. The former are metasediments of the Burundian and Malagaarasian Supergroups which are of Meso- and Neoproterozoic age, respectively.
burundi.title: Geology of Burundi

burundi.text: The wildlife of Burundi is composed of its flora and fauna. The small, landlocked country is home to 2,950 species of plants, 596 birds, 163 species of mammals, 52 species of reptiles, 56 species of amphibians, and 215 fish species.
burundi.title: Wildlife of Burundi

burundi.text: The climate of Burundi is equatorial in nature, and is marked by high mean annual temperatures, small temperature ranges, and rainfall throughout the year. Despite this, there is still considerable daily variation in temperature and rainfall across the country, depending on altitude.
burundi.title: Climate of Burundi

burundi.text: Burundi's relations with its neighbours have often been affected by security concerns. During the Burundian Civil War, hundreds of thousands of Burundian refugees have at various times crossed to neighboring Rwanda, Tanzania, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
burundi.title: Foreign relations of Burundi

picture.credit: Postal administration of the Kingdom of Burundi

burundi.text: Burundi has issued postage stamps for national use since achieving independence on 1 July 1962. The country was formerly a part of the Belgian territory of Ruanda-Urundi and before 1962 used those postage stamps.
burundi.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Burundi

burundi.text: Burundi is a Central African nation that is closely linked with Rwanda, geographically, historically and culturally. The drum such as the karyenda is one of central importance. Internationally, the country has produced the music group Royal Drummers of Burundi.
burundi.title: Music of Burundi

burundi.text: Burundi is situated in East Africa and has a territory full of mountains, savannas and agricultural fields, with forests in the surrounding rivers and waters. Agriculture is spread on 80% of the country's surface and it mainly includes coffee, tea, maize, beans and manioc.
burundi.title: Burundian cuisine

burundi.text: This is a list of public holidays in Burundi.
burundi.title: Public holidays in Burundi

burundi.text: Religion in Burundi is diverse, with Christianity being the predominant faith. Catholicism is the largest Christian denomination in the country, followed by Protestantism. Islam is the second largest religion, though its demographic share of the population has been subject to dispute.
burundi.title: Religion in Burundi

burundi.text: The three official languages of Burundi are Kirundi, French, and English. Of these, Kirundi is the only one spoken by the vast majority of the country's population. It is recognised as the national language by the Burundian constitution of 2005. English received official status only in 2014.
burundi.title: Languages of Burundi

burundi.text: The Cinema of Burundi is the filmmaking and film industry in Burundi.
burundi.title: Cinema of Burundi

burundi.text: There are a number of systems of transport in Burundi, including road and water-based infrastructure, the latter of which makes use of Lake Tanganyika. Furthermore, there are also some airports in Burundi.
burundi.title: Transport in Burundi

burundi.text: Tourism in Burundi refers to tourism in Burundi. Bujumbura, the largest city and former capital of Burundi, is a major tourist attraction of the country. In addition to this, Lake Tanganyika is a popular tourist attraction.
burundi.title: Tourism in Burundi

burundi.text: Communications in Burundi include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, the Internet, and the postal service in Burundi.
burundi.title: Communications in Burundi

burundi.text: Energy in Burundi is a growing industry. As of 2020, Burundi consumes a total of 382.70 million kilowatt hours of electric energy per year. The country produces locally 69% of the electricity it consumes, with the rest imported from other countries.
burundi.title: Energy in Burundi

burundi.text: Burundi is a producer of columbium and tantalum ore, tin ore, and tungsten ore, and some deposits of gold which are designated for export. Burundi has resources of copper, cobalt, nickel, feldspar, phosphate rock, quartzite, and rare reserves of uranium, and vanadium.
burundi.title: Mining industry of Burundi

cambodia.text: The politics of Cambodia are defined within the framework of a constitutional monarchy, in which the king serves as the head of state, and the prime minister is the head of government.
cambodia.title: Politics of Cambodia

cambodia.text: Demographic features of the population of Cambodia include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
cambodia.title: Demographics of Cambodia

cambodia.text: Education in Cambodia is controlled by the state through the Ministry of Education in a national level and by the Department of Education at the provincial level. The Cambodian education system includes pre-school, primary, secondary education, higher education and non-formal education.
cambodia.title: Education in Cambodia

cambodia.text: The quality of health in Cambodia is rising along with its growing economy.
cambodia.title: Health in Cambodia

picture.credit: Juan Manuel Garcia from Mexico City, Mexico

cambodia.text: This is a list of rivers in Cambodia.
cambodia.title: List of rivers of Cambodia

cambodia.text: The geology of Cambodia is the study of the nation's rocks, minerals, water and landforms. Cambodia's ancient geologic history in the Precambrian is poorly understood.
cambodia.title: Geology of Cambodia

cambodia.text: The wildlife of Cambodia is very diverse with at least 162 mammal species, 600 bird species, 176 reptile species, 900 freshwater fish species, 670 invertebrate species, and more than 3000 plant species.
cambodia.title: Wildlife of Cambodia

cambodia.text: The Cambodian government has diplomatic relations with most countries. The government is a member of most major international organizations, including the United Nations and its specialized agencies such as the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
cambodia.title: Foreign relations of Cambodia

cambodia.text: The earliest traces of armed conflict in the territory that constitutes modern Cambodia date to the Iron Age settlement of Phum Snay in north-western Cambodia. Sources on Funan's military structure are rare.
cambodia.title: Military history of Cambodia

cambodia.text: Cambodia used the postage stamps of Indochina until the early 1950s. In 1949 Cambodia became an associated state of the French Union but gained independence in 1953 and left the Union in 1955.
cambodia.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Cambodia

cambodia.text: The music of Cambodia is derived from a mesh of cultural traditions dating back to the ancient Khmer Empire, India, China and the original indigenous tribes living in the area before the arrival of Indian and Chinese travelers.
cambodia.title: Music of Cambodia

cambodia.text: Cambodian cuisine is the national cuisine of Cambodia. It reflects the varied culinary traditions of different ethnic groups in Cambodia, central of which is Khmer cuisine, the nearly-two-thousand-year-old culinary tradition of the Khmer people.
cambodia.title: Cambodian cuisine

cambodia.text: Cambodia has numerous public holidays, including memorial holidays and religious holidays of Buddhist origin. The Khmer traditional calendar, known as ចន្ទគតិ Chănteăkeătĕ, is a lunisolar calendar although the word itself means lunar calendar.
cambodia.title: Public holidays in Cambodia

cambodia.text: Buddhism is the state religion of Cambodia. Approximately 97% of Cambodia's population follows Theravada Buddhism, with Islam, Christianity, and tribal animism as well as Baha’i faith making up the bulk of the small remainder.
cambodia.title: Religion in Cambodia

cambodia.text: Cinema in Cambodia began in the 1950s, and many films were being screened in theaters throughout the country by the 1960s, which were regarded as the "golden age".
cambodia.title: Cinema of Cambodia

cambodia.text: Cambodia has increasingly become involved in sports over the last 30 years.
cambodia.title: Sport in Cambodia

cambodia.text: Cambodian literature, also Khmer literature, has a very ancient origin. Like most Southeast Asian national literatures its traditional corpus has two distinct aspects or levels: The written literature, mostly restricted to the royal courts or the Buddhist monasteries.
cambodia.title: Cambodian literature

cambodia.text: The history of Cambodian art stretches back centuries to ancient times, with the most widely recognized period being the art of the Khmer Empire, especially in the area around Angkor and the 12th-century temple-complex of Angkor Wat, initially Hindu and subsequently Buddhist.
cambodia.title: Cambodian art

cambodia.text: The system of transport in Cambodia, was rudimentary in the past, severely damaged in the chaos that engulfed the nation in the latter half of the 20th century.
cambodia.title: Transport in Cambodia

cambodia.text: The tourism industry in Cambodia is one of the most important sectors in the country's economy. In 2013, tourism arrivals increased by 17.5 percent year on year, with business travelers increasing 47 percent.
cambodia.title: Tourism in Cambodia

cambodia.text: Telecommunications in Cambodia include telephone, radio, television, and Internet services, which are regulated by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications.
cambodia.title: Telecommunications in Cambodia

cambodia.text: Agriculture accounts for 22 percent of Cambodia’s GDP, and employs about 3 million people.
cambodia.title: Agriculture in Cambodia

cambodia.text: Energy in Cambodia covers the energy sources used in the country including renewables, fossil fuels, biomass, and hydro-power. Cambodia had, in 2024, 5044 MW of electricity capacity installed. According to the IEA, Cambodia is the second least electrified country in the region.
cambodia.title: Energy in Cambodia

cambodia.text: In 2006, Cambodia's mineral resources remained, to a large extent, unexplored.
cambodia.title: Mineral industry of Cambodia

cameroon.text: The politics of Cameroon takes place in the context of an electoral autocracy where multi-party elections have been held since 1992, the ruling party wins every election, and Paul Biya has been president since 1982.
cameroon.title: Politics of Cameroon

cameroon.text: The demographic profile of Cameroon is complex for a country of its population.
cameroon.title: Demographics of Cameroon

cameroon.text: Cameroon is a Central African nation on the Gulf of Guinea. Bantu speakers were among the first groups to settle Cameroon, followed by the Muslim Fulani until German domination in 1884. After World War I, the French took over 80% of the area, and the British 20%.
cameroon.title: Education in Cameroon

cameroon.text: The Human Rights Measurement Initiative finds that Cameroon is fulfilling 61.0% of what it should be fulfilling for the right to health based on its level of income. When looking at the right to health with respect to children, Cameroon achieves 81.7% of what is expected based on its current income.
cameroon.title: Health in Cameroon

cameroon.text: This is a list of rivers in Cameroon. This list is arranged by drainage basin, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
cameroon.title: List of rivers of Cameroon

cameroon.text: The geology of Cameroon is almost universally Precambrian metamorphic and igneous basement rock, formed in the Archean as part of the Congo Craton and the Central African Mobile Zone and covered in laterite, recent sediments and soils.
cameroon.title: Geology of Cameroon

cameroon.text: The wildlife of Cameroon is composed of its flora and fauna. Bordering Nigeria, it is considered one of the wettest parts of Africa and records Africa's second highest concentration of biodiversity.
cameroon.title: Wildlife of Cameroon

cameroon.text: The climate of Cameroon is very diverse. Cameroon is generally referred to as the Africa in miniature because it has the major climates and vegetation of the continent.
cameroon.title: Climate of Cameroon

cameroon.text: Cameroon's noncontentious, low-profile approach to foreign relations puts it squarely in the middle of other African and developing country states on major issues.
cameroon.title: Foreign relations of Cameroon

cameroon.text: Postage stamps have been used in Cameroon or Cameroun since the nineteenth century.
cameroon.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Cameroon

cameroon.text: The music of the Cameroon includes diverse traditional and modern musical genres. The best-known contemporary genre is makossa, a popular style that has gained fans across Africa, and its related dance craze bikutsi.
cameroon.title: Music of Cameroon

cameroon.text: Cameroonian cuisine is one of the most varied in Africa due to Cameroon's location on the crossroads between the north, west, and center of the continent; the diversity in ethnicity with mixture ranging from Bantus, Bamileke people, Bamoun, Bamenda people and Shuwa Arabs, as well as the influence of German, French and British colonization.
cameroon.title: Cameroonian cuisine

cameroon.text: This is a list of holidays in Cameroon
cameroon.title: Public holidays in Cameroon

cameroon.text: Christianity is the majority religion in Cameroon, with significant minorities of Islam and traditional faiths. Cameroon is officially a secular country.
cameroon.title: Religion in Cameroon

cameroon.text: Cameroon is home to at least 250 languages, with some accounts reporting around 600. These include 55 Afro-Asiatic languages, two Nilo-Saharan languages, four Ubangian languages, and 169 Niger–Congo languages.
cameroon.title: Languages of Cameroon

cameroon.text: The cinema of Cameroon includes French and English-language filmmaking. The Anglophone film industry is sometimes known as Collywood.
cameroon.title: Cinema of Cameroon

cameroon.text: Sports in Cameroon is practiced widely by the population and advocated by the national government. Cameroonians take pride in victories at international competitions, making sport an important source of national unity.
cameroon.title: Sport in Cameroon

cameroon.text: Cameroonian literature includes literature in French, English and indigenous languages.
cameroon.title: Literature of Cameroon

cameroon.text: Different transportation options available in Cameroon. These options are available to citizens and tourists such as railways, roadways, waterways, pipelines, and airlines.
cameroon.title: Transport in Cameroon

cameroon.text: Tourism in Cameroon is a growing but relatively minor industry. Since the 1970s, the government of Cameroon has cultivated the industry by creating a ministry of tourism and by encouraging investment by airlines, hotels, and travel agencies.
cameroon.title: Tourism in Cameroon

cameroon.text: Telecommunications in Cameroon include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
cameroon.title: Telecommunications in Cameroon

cameroon.text: Agriculture in Cameroon is an important part of the Economy of Cameroon. It is one of the largest producers of Taro, cocoa bean, Palm oil and Cooking banana in the world.
cameroon.title: Agriculture in Cameroon

cameroon.text: Energy in Cameroon is a growing industry with tremendous potential, especially with the hydroelectric industry.
cameroon.title: Energy in Cameroon

cameroon.text: Despite being a mineral rich country, Cameroon has only recently begun to investigate mining on an industrial scale. Strong metal and industrial mineral prices since 2003 have encouraged companies to develop mines here.
cameroon.title: Mining industry of Cameroon

canada.text: The politics of Canada functions within a framework of parliamentary democracy and a federal system with strong democratic traditions. Canada is a constitutional monarchy where the monarch is the ceremonial head of state.
canada.title: Politics of Canada

canada.text: Statistics Canada conducts a country-wide census that collects demographic data every five years in the first and sixth year of each decade. The 2021 Canadian census enumerated a total population of 36,991,981, an increase of around 5.2 percent over the 2016 figure.
canada.title: Demographics of Canada

canada.text: Education in Canada is for the most part provided publicly, funded and overseen by federal, provincial, and local governments. Education is within provincial jurisdiction and the curriculum is overseen by the province.
canada.title: Education in Canada

canada.text: Healthcare in Canada is delivered through the provincial and territorial systems of publicly funded single-payer healthcare, informally called Medicare. It is guided by the provisions of the Canada Health Act, adopted during 1984, and is universal.
canada.title: Healthcare in Canada

canada.text: The list of rivers of Canada is organized by drainage basin and province.
canada.title: List of rivers of Canada

canada.text: The geology of Canada is a subject of regional geology and covers the country of Canada, which is the second-largest country in the world. Geologic units and processes are investigated on a large scale to reach a synthesized picture of the geological development of the country.
canada.title: Geology of Canada

canada.text: The wildlife of Canada or biodiversity of Canada consist of over 80,000 classified species, and an equal number thought yet to be recognized. Known fauna and flora have been identified from five kingdoms: protozoa represent approximately 1% of recorded species; chromist; fungi; plants; and animals.
canada.title: Wildlife of Canada

canada.text: Most mountain peaks of Canada lie in the west, specifically in British Columbia, Alberta, and the Yukon. Mountains can be found all over British Columbia while those in Alberta are mainly situated on the eastern side of the Canadian Rockies.
canada.title: List of mountains of Canada

canada.text: Canada is recognized as a middle power for its role in global affairs with a tendency to pursue multilateral and international solutions.
canada.title: Foreign relations of Canada

canada.text: The military history of Canada spans centuries of conflicts within the country, as well as international engagements involving the Canadian military. The Indigenous nations of Canada engaged in conflicts with one another for millennia.
canada.title: Military history of Canada

canada.text: The postal and philatelic history of Canada concerns postage of the territories which have formed Canada. Before Canadian Confederation, the colonies of British Columbia and Vancouver Island, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Newfoundland issued stamps in their own names.
canada.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Canada

canada.text: The music of Canada reflects the diverse influences that have shaped the country. Indigenous peoples, the British, and the French have all made unique contributions to the musical heritage of Canada.
canada.title: Music of Canada

canada.text: Canadian cuisine consists of the cooking traditions and practices of Canada, with regional variances around the country. First Nations and Inuit have practiced their culinary traditions in what is now Canada for at least 15,000 years.
canada.title: Canadian cuisine

canada.text: Public holidays in Canada known as statutory holidays, stat holidays, or simply stats, consist of a variety of cultural, nationalistic, and religious holidays that are legislated in Canada at the federal or provincial and territorial levels.
canada.title: Public holidays in Canada

canada.text: Religion in Canada encompasses a wide range of beliefs and customs that historically has been dominated by Christianity. The constitution of Canada refers to 'God'; however Canada has no official church and the government is officially committed to religious pluralism.
canada.title: Religion in Canada

canada.text: A multitude of languages have always been spoken in Canada. Prior to Confederation, the territories that would become Canada were home to over 70 distinct languages across 12 or so language families.
canada.title: Languages of Canada

canada.text: The cinema of Canada dates back to the earliest known display of film in Saint-Laurent, Quebec, in 1896. The film industry in Canada has been dominated by the United States, which has utilized Canada as a shooting location and to bypass British film quota laws.
canada.title: Cinema of Canada

canada.text: Sports in Canada consist of a wide variety of games. The roots of organized sports in Canada date back to the 1770s. Canada's official national sports are ice hockey and lacrosse. Other major professional games include curling, basketball, baseball, soccer, and football.
canada.title: Sports in Canada

canada.text: The architecture of Canada is, with the exception of that of Canadian First Nations, closely linked to the techniques and styles developed in Canada, Europe and the United States.
canada.title: Architecture of Canada

canada.text: Canadian literature is often divided into French- and English-language literatures, which are rooted in the literary traditions of France and Britain, respectively. The earliest Canadian narratives were of travel and exploration.
canada.title: Canadian literature

canada.text: Canadian art refers to the visual as well as plastic arts originating from the geographical area of contemporary Canada.
canada.title: Canadian art

canada.text: Canada, the world's second-largest country in total area, is dedicated to having efficient, high-capacity multimodal transportation spanning often vast distances between natural resource extraction sites, agricultural and urban areas.
canada.title: Transportation in Canada

canada.text: Tourism in Canada is a major economic driver in the service sector, attracting millions of visitors and supporting approximately 10% of the national labor force. In recent years, statistics show that Canada has received over 20 million international tourists annually.
canada.title: Tourism in Canada

canada.text: Present-day telecommunications in Canada include telephone, radio, television, and internet usage. In the past, telecommunications included telegraphy available through Canadian Pacific and Canadian National.
canada.title: Telecommunications in Canada

canada.text: Canada is one of the largest agricultural producers and exporters in the world.
canada.title: Agriculture in Canada

canada.text: Canada has access to all main sources of energy including oil and gas, coal, hydropower, biomass, solar, geothermal, wind, marine and nuclear.
canada.title: Energy policy of Canada

canada.text: Mining has been conducted on an industrial scale in present-day Canada since the late 18th century. The industry remains an important aspect of the economy of Canada to this day, particularly in the North, and Canadian-domiciled mining companies have increasingly expanded their operations globally.
canada.title: Mining in Canada

cape-verde.text: Politics of Cape Verde takes place in a framework of a semi-presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the Prime Minister of Cape Verde is the head of government and the President of the Republic of Cape Verde is the head of state, and of a multi-party system.
cape-verde.title: Politics of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Demographic features of the population of Cape Verde include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population. Cape Verde has about 540,000 inhabitants.
cape-verde.title: Demographics of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Primary school education in Cape Verde is mandatory between the ages of 6–18 and free for children ages 6–18. In 1997, the gross primary enrollment rate was 148.8%. Primary school attendance rates were unavailable for Cape Verde as of 2001.
cape-verde.title: Education in Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Health in Cape Verde is limited due to limited health care in Cape Verde. Gains since 2000 have led to improvements.
cape-verde.title: Health in Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: This is a partial list of streams of Cape Verde, sorted by island.
cape-verde.title: List of streams of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Cape Verde is a volcanic archipelago situated above an oceanic rise that puts the base of the islands 2 kilometers above the rest of the seafloor.
cape-verde.title: Geology of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: The wildlife of Cape Verde is found across its archipelago of ten islands and three islets, albeit in smaller numbers of species than mainland Africa.
cape-verde.title: Wildlife of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: This is a list of mountains in Cabo Verde:
cape-verde.title: List of mountains in Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Cape Verde follows a policy of nonalignment and seeks cooperative relations with all friendly states. Angola, Brazil, the People's Republic of China, Cuba, France, Germany, Portugal, Senegal, Russia, and the United States maintain embassies in Praia.
cape-verde.title: Foreign relations of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: The Cape Verdean Armed Forces or Cabo Verdean Armed Forces are the military of Cape Verde. They include two branches, the National Guard and the Coast Guard.
cape-verde.title: Cape Verdean Armed Forces

cape-verde.text: Cape Verde is known internationally for morna, a form of folk music usually sung in the Cape Verdean Creole, accompanied by clarinet, violin, guitar and cavaquinho. Funaná, Coladeira, Batuque and Cabo love are other musical forms.
cape-verde.title: Music of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: The cuisine of Cape Verde is a West African cuisine largely influenced by Portuguese, Southern and Western European and West African cuisine. Cape Verde was a colony of Portugal from its colonization until 1975.
cape-verde.title: Cape Verdean cuisine

cape-verde.text: This is a list of holidays in Cape Verde.
cape-verde.title: Public holidays in Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Christianity is the largest religion in Cape Verde, with Roman Catholics having the most adherents. Different sources give varying estimates on the relative sizes of various Christian denominations.
cape-verde.title: Religion in Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: The history of the cinema of Cape Verde dates back to the arrival of filmmakers in the early twentieth century. The first picture house was established in Mindelo around 1922, called Eden Park. The nation has two film festivals that occur annually.
cape-verde.title: Cinema of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Cape Verde has risen to prominence in a number of sporting areas in recent decades.
cape-verde.title: Sport in Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: The Architecture of Cape Verde has different architectural styles. Unlike the African mainland, Cape Verde was uninhabited until 1461 when the Portuguese arrived, whereas most of the other islands were first inhabited after the end of the 15th century.
cape-verde.title: Architecture of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: The Literature of Cape Verde is among the most important in West Africa. It is the second richest in West Africa after Mali and modern-day Mauritania. It is also the richest in the Lusophone portion of Africa.
cape-verde.title: Literature of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Most transportation in Cape Verde is done by air. There are regular flights between the major islands, with less frequent flights to the other islands. Boat transportation is available, though not widely used nor dependable.
cape-verde.title: Transport in Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Tourism in Cape Verde, a group of islands off the coast of Senegal, West Africa, started in the 1970s on the island of Sal and increased slowly in the 1980s and 1990s.
cape-verde.title: Tourism in Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Telecommunications in Cape Verde include fixed-line and mobile telephone services, radio and television broadcasting, and Internet access. The country's telecommunications system underwent extensive modernization from 1996 to 2000 following partial privatization in 1995.
cape-verde.title: Telecommunications in Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Cape Verde is a net importer of energy, with no significant fossil energy resources. As of 2016, 176,743 tonnes of fuel were sold on the internal market. Electricity production was 443 GWh in 2016, of which 81% from thermal power, 17% from wind power and 1.4% from solar power.
cape-verde.title: Energy in Cape Verde

cayman-islands.text: The politics of the Cayman Islands takes place within a framework of parliamentary democracy, within the confines of the Government of the Cayman Islands.
cayman-islands.title: Politics of the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: This is a demography of the population of the Cayman Islands including population density, ethnicity, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
cayman-islands.title: Demographics of the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: Education in the Cayman Islands is compulsory for those aged 4 to 16 and is free to all Caymanian children. The literacy rate for residents over age 15 is 98%. Public schools follow a British-style educational system.
cayman-islands.title: Education in the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: In 2003, the Cayman Islands became the first country in the world to mandate health insurance for all residents. There are four hospitals in the Cayman Islands. Grand Cayman is home to the private Health City Cayman Islands, as well as the Chrissie Tomlinson Memorial Hospital.
cayman-islands.title: Health in the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: The geology of the Cayman Islands includes carbonates deposited and periodically eroded over the last 30 million years. The underlying Cayman Ridge is proposed as an uplifted fault block. The oldest rocks are believed to be granodiorite, followed by a cap of basalt.
cayman-islands.title: Geology of the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: The foreign relations of the Cayman Islands are largely managed from the United Kingdom, as the islands remains one of 14 overseas territories under British jurisdiction and sovereignty.
cayman-islands.title: Foreign relations of the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: The defence of the Cayman Islands has been and currently remains the responsibility of the United Kingdom. Before the independence of Jamaica in 1962, the Cayman Islands were under the same administration as Jamaica.
cayman-islands.title: Military history of the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: The Cayman Islands, a British Overseas Territory located in the western Caribbean Sea, came under British control in 1670, as a dependency of Jamaica, continuing in that status until 1962.
cayman-islands.title: Postage stamps and postal history of the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: The music of the Cayman Islands, a Caribbean island chain, includes a wide selection of international pop music as well as unique folk styles.
cayman-islands.title: Music of the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: The Cayman Islands are a group of islands situated in the Caribbean Sea just between Cuba and Honduras. After being colonized first by Jamaica and then by the British, Cayman Islands remained under British dependency since 1962.
cayman-islands.title: Cuisine of the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: This is a list of public holidays in Cayman Islands. Additionally the General elections at least since 2009 have also been a public holiday.
cayman-islands.title: Public holidays in the Cayman Islands

cayman-islands.text: The transport infrastructure of the Cayman Islands includes a 785 kilometre long public road network with seven active bus routes. There are three airports on the islands.
cayman-islands.title: Transport in the Cayman Islands

central-african-republic.text: The politics of the Central African Republic formally take place in a framework of a semi-presidential republic. In this system, the President is the head of state, with a Prime Minister as head of government. Executive power is exercised by the government.
central-african-republic.title: Politics of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: Demographic features of the population of the Central African Republic include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
central-african-republic.title: Demographics of the Central African Republic

picture.credit: hdptcar from Bangui, Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: Public education in the Central African Republic is free, and education is compulsory from ages 6 to 14. AIDS-related deaths have taken a heavy toll on teachers, contributing to the closure of more than 100 primary schools between 1996 and 1998.
central-african-republic.title: Education in the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: Health in the Central African Republic has been degraded by years of internal conflict and economic turmoil since independence from France in 1960. One sixth of the country's population is in need of acute medical care.
central-african-republic.title: Health in the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: This is a list of rivers in Central African Republic. This list is arranged by drainage basin, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
central-african-republic.title: List of rivers of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The geology of Central African Republic is part of the broader geology of Africa. CAR occupies a swath of ancient rocks, dating back billions of years that record significant aspects of Earth history and yield minerals vital to the country's small economy.
central-african-republic.title: Geology of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The wildlife of the Central African Republic is in the vast natural habitat in the Central African Republic located between the Congo Basin's rain forests and large savannas, where the human density was smaller than 0.5 per km2 prior to 1850.
central-african-republic.title: Wildlife of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: Mountains of the Central African Republic.
central-african-republic.title: List of mountains of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The Central African Republic has diplomatic relations with 119 out of the 193 United Nations member states.
central-african-republic.title: Foreign relations of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The Central African Republic has been issuing stamps since 1959. Before this, it was called Ubangi-Shari. Ubangi-Shari became an autonomous state within the French Community and was renamed the Central African Republic on 1 December 1958. The Republic became fully independent on 13 August 1960.
central-african-republic.title: Postage stamps and postal history of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: Music of the Central African Republic includes many different forms. Western rock and pop music, as well as Afrobeat, soukous and other genres have become popular nationwide. The sanza is a popular instrument. The Pygmies have a complex folk music tradition.
central-african-republic.title: Music of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: Central African cuisine includes the cuisines, cooking traditions, practices, ingredients and foods of the Central African Republic. Indigenous agriculture in the country includes millet, sorghum, banana, yam, okra, yellow onion, garlic, spinach, rice and palm oil.
central-african-republic.title: Cuisine of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: This is a list of public holidays in the Central African Republic
central-african-republic.title: Public holidays in the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: Christianity is the predominant religion in the Central African Republic, with significant minorities adhering to Islam and traditional African religions. The country is officially secular and freedom of religion is enshrined in its constitution.
central-african-republic.title: Religion in the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The official languages of the Central African Republic are French and Sango. In total there are about 73 languages in the country; 67 living indigenous languages and 6 commonly spoken foreign languages.
central-african-republic.title: Languages of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The cinema of the Central African Republic refers to the films and the film industry of Central African Republic. The country is one of the world's poorest countries and the film industry is correspondingly small.
central-african-republic.title: Cinema of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: Modes of transport in the Central African Republic include road, water, and air. Most of the country is connected to the road network, but not all of it. Some roads in the country do not connect to the rest of the national road network and may become impassable, especially during heavy monsoon rain.
central-african-republic.title: Transport in the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The Central African Republic has seen little international tourism due to its recent history of conflict, an ongoing civil war, and resulting insecurity in certain areas of the country, particularly the north and northwest.
central-african-republic.title: Tourism in the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: Telecommunications in the Central African Republic includes radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet as well as the postal system. Persistent conflict has hampered telecommunication and media development in the Central African Republic.
central-african-republic.title: Telecommunications in the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The Central African Republic's mineral resource endowment includes copper, diamond, gold, graphite, ilmenite, iron ore, kaolin, kyanite, lignite, limestone, manganese, monazite, quartz, rutile, salt, tin, and uranium.
central-african-republic.title: Mining industry of the Central African Republic

chad.text: The politics of Chad take place in a framework of a semi-presidential republic, whereby the President of Chad is the head of state and the prime minister is the head of government. Executive power is exercised by the government. Legislative power is vested in both the government and parliament.
chad.title: Politics of Chad

chad.text: The people of Chad speak more than 100 languages and divide themselves into many ethnic groups. However, language and ethnicity are not the same. Moreover, neither element can be tied to a particular physical type.
chad.title: Demographics of Chad

picture.credit: US Army Africa from Vicenza, Italy

chad.text: Education in Chad is challenging due to the nation's dispersed population and a certain degree of reluctance on the part of parents to send their children to school.
chad.title: Education in Chad

chad.text: Health in Chad is suffering due to the country's weak healthcare system. Access to medical services is very limited and the health system struggles with shortage of medical staff, medicines and equipment.
chad.title: Health in Chad

chad.text: This is a list of rivers in Chad. This list is arranged by drainage basin, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
chad.title: List of rivers of Chad

chad.text: The terrain of Chad in central Africa is dominated by the low-lying Chad Basin, which rises gradually to mountains and plateaus on the north, east, and south. In the east heights of more than 900 metres are attained in the Ennedi and Ouaddaï plateaus.
chad.title: Geology of Chad

chad.text: The wildlife of Chad is composed of its flora and fauna.
chad.title: Wildlife of Chad

chad.text: The foreign relations of Chad are significantly influenced by the desire for oil revenue and investment in Chadian oil industry and support for former Chadian President Idriss Déby. Chad is officially non-aligned but maintains close relations with France, its former colonial power.
chad.title: Foreign relations of Chad

chad.text: The military history of Chad was closely tied to the French military during World War I and World War II, when many Chadians served in French forces. Chad achieved independence in 1960 without national armed forces of its own.
chad.title: Military history of Chad

chad.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Chad. Chad is a landlocked country in central Africa bordered by Libya to the north, Sudan to the east, the Central African Republic to the south, Cameroon and Nigeria to the southwest, and Niger to the west.
chad.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Chad

chad.text: Chad is an ethnically diverse Central African country. Each of its regions has its own unique varieties of music and dance.
chad.title: Music of Chad

chad.text: Chadian cuisine is the cooking traditions, practices, foods and dishes associated with the Republic of Chad. Chadians use a medium variety of grains, vegetables, fruits and meats. Commonly consumed grains include millet, sorghum, and rice as staple foods.
chad.title: Chadian cuisine

chad.text: This is a list of public holidays in Chad. December 1, "Freedom and Democracy Day", remembers December 1, 1990 and celebrates the ascent of President Idriss Déby to power.
chad.title: Public holidays in Chad

chad.text: Islam and Christianity are the most widely professed religions in Chad. A smaller share of Chadians adhere to other faiths, including traditional religions, or profess no religion.
chad.title: Religion in Chad

chad.text: Chad has two official languages, French and Arabic. Ethnologue reports over 120 indigenous languages in the country. Nevertheless, French remains the primary language of government and education and is predominant for inter-ethnic communication.
chad.title: Languages of Chad

chad.text: The film industry of Chad is small but growing. The first film made in the country was the 1958 John Huston adventure film The Roots of Heaven, filmed when the country was still a part of French Equatorial Africa.
chad.title: Cinema of Chad

chad.text: The principal sports of Chad are football, basketball, athletics, boxing, martial arts and fishing, which is mostly known in Lake Chad. The national stadium is the Stade Nacional in the capital, N'Djamena.
chad.title: Sports in Chad

chad.text: Chadian literature has suffered greatly from the turmoil which has engulfed the country, economical and political. As with many cultures, literature in Chad began with folk tales and legends. While French is the dominant language, Arabic is also used by some Chadian writers.
chad.title: Chadian literature

chad.text: Transport infrastructure within Chad is generally poor, especially in the north and east of the country. River transport is limited to the south-west corner.
chad.title: Transport in Chad

chad.text: Tourism in Chad is a relatively minor industry. Most travellers are attracted by Chad's hunting capabilities and its Zakouma National Park. Tourists must have valid passports and visas, as well as evidence of yellow fever immunization.
chad.title: Tourism in Chad

chad.text: Telecommunications in Chad include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
chad.title: Telecommunications in Chad

chad.text: In 2020, approximately 80% of Chad's labor force was employed in the agricultural sector. This sector of the economy accounts for 52.3% of the GDP, as of 2017.
chad.title: Agriculture in Chad

chad.text: The total energy consumption in Chad is of 200.00 million kWh of electric energy per year. Per capita, this is an average of 13 kWh. Chad can provide for itself completely with self-produced energy.
chad.title: Energy in Chad

chad.text: In the late 1980s, the only mineral exploited in Chad was sodium carbonate, or natron.
chad.title: Mining industry of Chad

chile.text: Chile's government is a representative democratic republic, in which the President of Chile serves as both head of state and head of government, within a formal multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the president and their cabinet.
chile.title: Politics of Chile

chile.text: Chile's 2017 census reported a population of 17,574,003 people. Its rate of population growth has been decreasing since 1990, due to a declining birth rate.
chile.title: Demographics of Chile

chile.text: Education in Chile is divided in preschool, primary school, secondary school, and technical or higher education.The levels of education in Chile are: Pre-school: For children up to 5 years old. Primary school: for children aged 6–13 years old, divided into 8 grades.
chile.title: Education in Chile

chile.text: The healthcare system in Chile operates as a mixed system, combining both public and private provision of health services. The public system, known as Fondo Nacional de Salud, is funded through taxes and provides free or subsidized care to those who cannot afford private health insurance.
chile.title: Healthcare in Chile

chile.text: This list of rivers of Chile includes all the major rivers of Chile. See each article for their tributaries, drainage areas, etc. Usually significant tributaries appear in this list, under the river into which they drain.
chile.title: List of rivers of Chile

chile.text: The geology of Chile is a characterized by processes linked to subduction, such as volcanism, earthquakes, and orogeny. The building blocks of Chile's geology were assembled during the Paleozoic Era when Chile was the southwestern margin of the supercontinent Gondwana.
chile.title: Geology of Chile

chile.text: The wildlife of Chile is very diverse because of the country's slender and elongated shape, which spans a wide range of latitude, and altitude, ranging from the windswept coastline of the Pacific coast on the west to northern Andes to the sub-Antarctic, high Andes mountains in the east.
chile.title: Wildlife of Chile

chile.text: The climate of Chile comprises a wide range of weather conditions across a large geographic scale, extending across 38 degrees in latitude, making generalizations difficult.
chile.title: Climate of Chile

chile.text: Since its return to democracy in 1990, Chile has been an active participant in the regional and international arena. Chile assumed a two-year non-permanent position on the UN Security Council in January 2003 and was re-elected to the council in October 2013.
chile.title: Foreign relations of Chile

chile.text: Chile has produced stamps for national use since 1853. The first stamps of Chile were inscribed Colon Chile. In 1894, Chile was one of the few countries to issue a stamp for the Avis de réception service.
chile.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Chile

chile.text: Chilean music refers to all kinds of music developed in Chile, or by Chileans in other countries, from the arrival of the Spanish conquistadors to the modern day. It also includes the native pre-Columbian music from what is today Chilean territory.
chile.title: Music of Chile

chile.text: Chilean cuisine stems mainly from the combination of traditional Spanish cuisine, Chilean Mapuche culture and local ingredients, with later important influences from other European cuisines, particularly from Germany, the United Kingdom and France.
chile.title: Chilean cuisine

chile.text: This is a list of public holidays in Chile; about half of them are Christian holidays.
chile.title: Public holidays in Chile

chile.text: Christianity is the most widely professed religion in Chile, with Catholicism being its largest denomination. The country is secular and the freedom of religion is established under its Constitution.
chile.title: Religion in Chile

chile.text: Spanish is the de facto official and administrative language of Chile. It is spoken by 99.3% of the population in the form of Chilean Spanish, as well as Andean Spanish. Spanish in Chile is also referred to as "castellano".
chile.title: Languages of Chile

chile.text: Chilean cinema refers to all films produced in Chile or made by Chileans. It had its origins at the start of the 20th century with the first Chilean film screening in 1902 and the first Chilean feature film appearing in 1910.
chile.title: Cinema of Chile

chile.text: Sports in Chile are performed at both amateur and professional levels, practiced both at home and abroad to develop and improve, or simply represent the country. Association football is the most popular sport in Chile, and is played for a range of reasons.
chile.title: Sport in Chile

chile.text: Chilean architecture is influenced by the country's history, religious culture and unique climate. Chile was a former Spanish colony and its architectural style was therefore strongly influenced by Spanish design.
chile.title: Architecture of Chile

chile.text: Chilean literature refers to all written or literary work produced in Chile or by Chilean writers. The literature of Chile is usually written in Spanish. Chile has a rich literary tradition and has been home to two Nobel prize winners, the poets Gabriela Mistral and Pablo Neruda.
chile.title: Chilean literature

chile.text: Chilean art refers to all kinds of visual art developed in Chile, or by Chileans, from the arrival of the Spanish conquerors to the modern day. It also includes the native pre-Columbian pictorial expression on modern Chilean territory.
chile.title: Chilean art

chile.text: Transport in Chile is mostly by road. The far south of the country is not directly connected to central Chile by road without travelling through Argentina, and water transport also plays a part there.
chile.title: Transport in Chile

chile.text: Since the mid-1990s, tourism in Chile has become one of the main sources of income for the country, especially in its most extreme areas. In 2005, this sector grew by 13.6%, generating more than US$500 million, equivalent to 1.33% of the national GDP.
chile.title: Tourism in Chile

chile.text: The technical regulator of communications in Chile is the Ministry of Transportation and Telecommunications, through the Undersecretariat of Telecommunications.
chile.title: Telecommunications in Chile

chile.text: Agriculture in Chile encompasses a wide range of different activities due to the country's particular geography, climate, geology and human factors.
chile.title: Agriculture in Chile

chile.text: Chile's total primary energy supply was 36.10 Mtoe in 2014. Energy in Chile is dominated by fossil fuels, with coal, oil and gas accounting for 73.4% of the total primary energy.
chile.title: Energy in Chile

chile.text: The mining sector in Chile has historically been and continues to be one of the pillars of the Chilean economy. Mining in Chile is concentrated in 14 mining districts, all of them in the northern half of the country and in particular in the Norte Grande region spanning most of the Atacama Desert.
chile.title: Mining in Chile

colombia.text: Colombia is a presidential representative democratic republic with a multi-party system, where the President of Colombia is both head of state and head of government. The national government has separate executive, legislative, and judicial branches.
colombia.title: Politics of Colombia

colombia.text: The demographics of Colombia consist of statistics regarding Colombians' health, economic status, religious affiliations, ethnicity, population density, and other aspects of the population.
colombia.title: Demographics of Colombia

colombia.text: Education in Colombia includes nursery school, elementary school, high school, technical instruction and university education.
colombia.title: Education in Colombia

colombia.text: Health care in Colombia is offered by the medical, nursing, and allied health professions in the Republic of Colombia. The Human Rights Measurement Initiative finds that Colombia is fulfilling 94.0% of what it should be fulfilling for the right to health based on its level of income.
colombia.title: Health care in Colombia

colombia.text: Geology of Colombia refers to the geological composition of the Republic of Colombia that determines its geography. Most of the emerged territory of Colombia covers vast areas within the South American Plate, whereas much submerged territory lies within the Caribbean Plate and the Nazca Plate.
colombia.title: Geology of Colombia

colombia.text: The biodiversity of Colombia is the variety of indigenous organisms in the country with the second-highest biodiversity in the world. As of 2021, around 63,000 species are registered in Colombia, of which 14% are endemic.
colombia.title: Biodiversity of Colombia

colombia.text: The climate of Colombia is characterized for being tropical and isothermal as a result of its geographical location near the Equator presenting variations within five natural regions and depending on the altitude, temperature, humidity, winds and rainfall.
colombia.title: Climate of Colombia

colombia.text: Colombia seeks diplomatic and commercial relations with all countries, regardless of their ideologies or political or economic systems. For this reason, the Colombian economy is quite open, relying on international trade and following guidelines given by international law.
colombia.title: Foreign relations of Colombia

colombia.text: Colombia is a country in north-western South America. Colombia is bordered by Venezuela, Brazil, Ecuador, Peru, Panama and the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean. With a population of over 45 million people, Colombia has the second largest population in South America, after Brazil.
colombia.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Colombia

colombia.text: The music of Colombia is an expression of Colombian culture, music genres, both traditional and modern, according with the features of each geographic region, although it is not uncommon to find different musical styles in the same region.
colombia.title: Music of Colombia

colombia.text: Colombian cuisine is a culinary tradition of six main regions within Colombia: Insular, Caribbean, Pacific, Andean, Orinoco, and Amazonian. Colombian cuisine varies regionally and is influenced by Indigenous Colombian, Spanish, and African cuisines, with a slight Arab influence in some regions.
colombia.title: Colombian cuisine

colombia.text: There are 19 public holidays in Colombia, plus Palm and Easter Sunday. The city of Barranquilla has 2 extra holidays, celebrating Monday and Tuesday of Carnival. The city of Cartagena has a week of holiday, the week of November 11, celebrating The Independence of Cartagena.
colombia.title: Public holidays in Colombia

colombia.text: Religion in Colombia is dominated by various branches of Christianity and is an expression of the different influences in Colombian culture including that of the Spanish, the Indigenous peoples and the Afro-Colombians.
colombia.title: Religion in Colombia

colombia.text: Around 99.2% of Colombians speak the Spanish language. Sixty-five Amerindian languages, two Creole languages, the Portuguese language and the Roma language are also spoken in the country. English has official status in the San Andrés, Providencia and Santa Catalina Islands.
colombia.title: Languages of Colombia

colombia.text: Cinema of Colombia refers to film productions made in Colombia, or considered Colombian for other reasons. Colombian cinema, like any national cinema, is a historical process with industrial and artistic aspects.
colombia.title: Cinema of Colombia

colombia.text: Sports in Colombia includes professional sports leagues, as well as amateur leagues for numerous sports. Football, cycling, baseball, and roller skating are the most popular sports in Colombia.
colombia.title: Sport in Colombia

colombia.text: Colombia's architectural heritage includes Spanish colonial architecture, such as Catholic churches. Its modern architecture represents various International Style architecture. In the postmodern architecture era, a wave of innovate and striking buildings have been designed.
colombia.title: Architecture of Colombia

colombia.text: Colombian literature, as an expression of the culture of Colombia, is heterogeneous due to the coexistence of Spanish, African and Native American heritages in an extremely diverse geography.
colombia.title: Colombian literature

colombia.text: Colombian art has 3,500 years of history and covers a wide range of media and styles ranging from Spanish Baroque devotional painting to Quimbaya gold craftwork to the "lyrical americanism" of painter Alejandro Obregón.
colombia.title: Colombian art

colombia.text: Transport in Colombia is regulated by the Ministry of Transport. Road travel is the main means of transport; 69 percent of cargo is transported by road, as compared with 27 percent by railroad, 3 percent by internal waterways, and 1 percent by air.
colombia.title: Transport in Colombia

colombia.text: Tourism in Colombia contributed to 2% of the country's GDP and 2.5% of total employment in 2016. Foreign tourist visits were predicted to have risen from 0.6 million in 2007 to 4 million in 2017.
colombia.title: Tourism in Colombia

colombia.text: Since being liberalized in 1991, the Colombian telecommunications sector has added new services, expanded coverage, improved efficiency, and lowered costs. The sector has had the second largest investment in infrastructure since 1997.
colombia.title: Communications in Colombia

colombia.text: Agriculture in Colombia refers to all agricultural activities, essential to food, feed, and fiber production, including all techniques for raising and processing livestock within the Republic of Colombia.
colombia.title: Agriculture in Colombia

colombia.text: The electricity sector in Colombia is dominated by large hydropower generation and thermal generation. Despite the country's large potential for new renewable energy technologies, this potential has been barely tapped.
colombia.title: Electricity sector in Colombia

colombia.text: Mineral industry of Colombia refers to the extraction of valuable minerals or other geological materials in Colombia. Colombia is well-endowed with minerals and energy resources. It has the largest coal reserves in Latin America, and is second to Brazil in hydroelectric potential.
colombia.title: Mineral industry of Colombia

comoros.text: The politics of the Union of the Comoros take place in a framework of a federal presidential republic, whereby the President of the Comoros is both head of state and head of government, and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government.
comoros.title: Politics of the Comoros

comoros.text: The Comorians inhabiting Grande Comore, Anjouan, and Mohéli share African-Arab origins. Islam is the dominant religion, and Quranic schools for children reinforce its influence. Although Islamic culture is firmly established throughout, a small minority are Christian.
comoros.title: Demographics of the Comoros

comoros.text: Practically all children attend Quranic school for two or three years, starting around age five; there they learn the rudiments of the Islamic faith and some classical Arabic.
