Some holidays are religious and others are secular, while some can be fixed holidays on the calendar while others are movable. There are four Islamic holidays and two Christian holidays.
egypt.title: Public holidays in Egypt

egypt.text: Religion in Egypt controls many aspects of social life and is endorsed by law. The state religion of Egypt is Islam, although estimates vary greatly in the absence of official statistics.
egypt.title: Religion in Egypt

egypt.text: Literary Arabic is the official language and the most widely written. Egyptians speak a continuum of dialects. The predominant dialect in Egypt is Egyptian Colloquial Arabic or Masri/Masry, which is the vernacular language.
egypt.title: Languages of Egypt

egypt.text: The Egyptian film industry is today based mainly in Cairo, which is sometimes referred to as Hollywood on the Nile, Hollywood of the Middle East or Hollywood of the East, despite having its beginnings in the city of Alexandria in the early 20th century.
egypt.title: Cinema of Egypt

egypt.text: Football is the most popular national sport of Egypt. The Cairo Derby is one of the fiercest derbies in Africa, and the BBC picked it as one of the 7 toughest derbies in the world.
egypt.title: Sport in Egypt

egypt.text: There have been many architectural styles used in Egyptian buildings over the centuries, including Ancient Egyptian architecture, Greco-Roman architecture, Islamic architecture, and modern architecture.
egypt.title: Architecture of Egypt

egypt.text: Egyptian literature traces its beginnings to ancient Egypt and is some of the earliest known literature. Ancient Egyptians were the first to develop written literature, as inscriptions or in collections of papyrus, precursors to the modern book.
egypt.title: Egyptian literature

egypt.text: Transport in Egypt is centered in Cairo and largely follows the pattern of settlement along the Nile. The Ministry of Transportation and other government bodies are responsible for transportation in Egypt, whether by sea, river, land or air.
egypt.title: Transport in Egypt

egypt.text: Tourism in Egypt is one of the leading sources of income, a vital component of the national economy.
egypt.title: Tourism in Egypt

egypt.text: Telecommunications in Egypt began in 1854 with the inauguration of the first telegraph lines between the governorates of Cairo and Alexandria under the Egyptian Telegraph and Telephone Authority, while 1881 saw the installation of the first telephone line between the two governorates.
egypt.title: Telecommunications in Egypt

egypt.text: Energy in Egypt is an important sector of the Egyptian national economy. This article describes the energy and electricity production, consumption, export, and import in Egypt.
egypt.title: Energy in Egypt

egypt.text: Mining in Egypt has had a long history that dates back to predynastic times. Active mining began in Egypt around 3000 BCE. Egypt has substantial mineral resources, including 48 million tons of tantalite, 50 million tons of coal, and an estimated 6.7 million ounces of gold in the Eastern Desert.
egypt.title: Mining industry of Egypt

el-salvador.text: Politics of El Salvador takes place in a framework of a presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the President of El Salvador is both head of state and head of government, and of an executive power is exercised by the government.
el-salvador.title: Politics of El Salvador

el-salvador.text: This is a demography of the population of El Salvador including population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population. El Salvador's population numbers 6.03 million.
el-salvador.title: Demographics of El Salvador

el-salvador.text: Education in El Salvador is regulated by the country's Ministry of Education.
el-salvador.title: Education in El Salvador

el-salvador.text: For the period between 2005 and 2010, El Salvador had the third-lowest birth rate in Central America, with 57 births per 2500. However, during the same period, it had the highest death rate in Central America, 59 deaths per 10000.
el-salvador.title: Health in El Salvador

el-salvador.text: This is a list of rivers in El Salvador. El Salvador has 58 river basins which all drain to the Pacific Ocean. The total amount of water discharged into the Pacific is 19 million m3 in a normal year. Additionally, there are several endorheic basins linked to a lake.
el-salvador.title: List of rivers of El Salvador

el-salvador.text: The geology of El Salvador is underlain by rocks dating to the Paleozoic. Prior to the Pennsylvanian, sediments deposited and were intensely deformed, intruded by granite rocks and metamorphosed.
el-salvador.title: Geology of El Salvador

el-salvador.text: El Salvador is a member of the United Nations and several of its specialized agencies, the Organization of American States, the Central American Common Market, the Central American Parliament, and the Central American Integration System.
el-salvador.title: Foreign relations of El Salvador

el-salvador.text: El Salvador became independent from Spain in 1821. It has produced its own stamps since 1867. The earliest known postal marking for El Salvador has been found on an entire letter from Santa Ana to Guatemala, July 30, 1780. It bears a pre-philatelic postmark from Santa Ana.
el-salvador.title: Postage stamps and postal history of El Salvador

picture.credit: Presidencia El Salvador from San Salvador, El Sa

el-salvador.text: The music of El Salvador refers to the Music of the Republic of El Salvador and is encompassed in the wider Latin American musical traditions. During the colonial period, El Salvador's music began to be influenced by various ethnic groups involved in the colonization process.
el-salvador.title: Music of El Salvador

el-salvador.text: Salvadoran cuisine is a style of cooking derived from the nation of El Salvador. The indigenous foods consist of a mix of Amerindian cuisine from groups such as the Lenca, Pipil, Maya Poqomam, Maya Chʼortiʼ, Alaguilac and Cacaopera peoples and some African influences.
el-salvador.title: Salvadoran cuisine

el-salvador.text: This is a list of public holidays in El Salvador.
el-salvador.title: Public holidays in El Salvador

el-salvador.text: Christianity is the predominant religion in El Salvador, with Catholicism and Evangelicalism being its main denominations. The Catholic share of the population is on decline while Protestants are experiencing rapid growth in recent decades.
el-salvador.title: Religion in El Salvador

el-salvador.text: The Languages of El Salvador is what the country has been influenced throughout its history from the roots of the indigenous languages. Spanish is the official language of El Salvador, plus the indigenous as recognized languages: El idioma oficial de El Salvador es el castellano.
el-salvador.title: Languages of El Salvador

el-salvador.text: Salvadoran literature is primary literature written in El Salvador. Salvadoran literature is primary written in Spanish and in other languages like English.
el-salvador.title: Salvadoran literature

el-salvador.text: El Salvador has transport links by road, rail, sea and air. El Salvador has over 10,000 km of roads, and one passenger rail service. There are several seaports on the Pacific Ocean, and two international airports.
el-salvador.title: Transport in El Salvador

el-salvador.text: Tourism accounts for a large part of El Salvador's economy. El Salvador has many natural attractions including beaches. El Salvador offers many lush forests shrouded in cool temperatures with abundant wildlife and scenic mountain-top vistas.
el-salvador.title: Tourism in El Salvador

el-salvador.text: Telecommunications in El Salvador include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet, centered primarily around the capital, San Salvador.
el-salvador.title: Telecommunications in El Salvador

el-salvador.text: Mining in El Salvador to extract gold and other minerals from beneath the surface can be traced back to the beginning of the twentieth century but has generally been halted due to policy changes in the last two decades.
el-salvador.title: Mining in El Salvador

equatorial-guinea.text: The politics of Equatorial Guinea take place under an authoritarian regime where power has been centralized under President Teodoro Obiang Nguema since he seized power in a 1979 coup against his uncle, Francisco Macías Nguema.
equatorial-guinea.title: Politics of Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: Demographic features of the population of Equatorial Guinea include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
equatorial-guinea.title: Demographics of Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: There have been major strides with Education in Equatorial Guinea over the past ten years, although there is still room for improvement. Among sub-Saharan African countries, Equatorial Guinea has one of the highest literacy rates.
equatorial-guinea.title: Education in Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: The Human Rights Measurement Initiative finds that Equatorial Guinea is fulfilling 43.5% of what it should be fulfilling for the right to health based on its level of income.
equatorial-guinea.title: Health in Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: This is a list of rivers in Equatorial Guinea. This list is arranged by drainage basin, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
equatorial-guinea.title: List of rivers of Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: The geological basement of the central and eastern regions Equatorial Guinea is composed of Precambrian rocks which form a part of the Congo craton. They include gneiss, greenstone, schist-amphibolite and granitoids.
equatorial-guinea.title: Geology of Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: The wildlife of Equatorial Guinea is composed of its flora and fauna.
equatorial-guinea.title: Wildlife of Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: The government's official policy is one of nonalignment. In its search for assistance to meet the goal of national reconstruction, the government of Equatorial Guinea has established diplomatic relations with numerous European and Third World countries.
equatorial-guinea.title: Foreign relations of Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Equatorial Guinea, formerly known as Spanish Guinea.
equatorial-guinea.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: Equatorial Guinea's culture has been less documented than most African countries, and commercial recordings remain scarce.
equatorial-guinea.title: Music of Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: The cuisine of Equatorial Guinea is a blend of the cuisines of the native peoples of this African country, including the Annobonese, the Bubi, the Fang, and the Kombe.
equatorial-guinea.title: Cuisine of Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: This is a list of holidays in Equatorial Guinea. January 1: New Year's Day April 7: Good Friday May 1: Labour Day June 5: President's Day, birthday of President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo.
equatorial-guinea.title: Public holidays in Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: Christianity is the dominant religion in Equatorial Guinea, with the Catholic Church having the most members. There are also substantial minorities of the adherents of traditional faiths and Islam.
equatorial-guinea.title: Religion in Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: Equatorial Guinea was the only Spanish colony in Sub-Saharan Africa. During its colonial history between 1778 and 1968, it developed a tradition of literature in Spanish, unique among the countries of Africa, that persists to the present day.
equatorial-guinea.title: Equatoguinean literature

equatorial-guinea.text: This article lists transport in Equatorial Guinea.
equatorial-guinea.title: Transport in Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: Telecommunications in Equatorial Guinea include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
equatorial-guinea.title: Telecommunications in Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: Agriculture is a major sector of the economy in Equatorial Guinea. Farming accounts for approximately 2% of GDP as it contributes little to the export earnings of the country. In 2022, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations held its Africa regional conference in Malabo.
equatorial-guinea.title: Agriculture in Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: Energy in Equatorial Guinea is an industry with plenty of potential, especially in the fields of oil and natural gas. However, production has been declining in recent years due to under-investment and a lack of new discoveries.
equatorial-guinea.title: Energy in Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: The regulation of mining in Equatorial Guinea is handled by the Ministry of Mines, Industry, and Energy, which oversees activities in the mining and petroleum industries.
equatorial-guinea.title: Mining industry of Equatorial Guinea

eritrea.text: The politics of Eritrea and the government of Eritrea take place in the framework of a single-party presidential republic currently under a totalitarian dictatorship. The President officially serves as both head of state and head of government.
eritrea.title: Politics of Eritrea

eritrea.text: Sources disagree as to the current population of Eritrea, with some proposing numbers as low as 3.6 million and others as high as 6.7 million. Eritrea has never conducted an official government census. The nation has nine recognized ethnic groups.
eritrea.title: Demographics of Eritrea

eritrea.text: Education in Eritrea is officially compulsory between 7 and 13 years of age.
eritrea.title: Education in Eritrea

eritrea.text: The Health in Eritrea has been poor on a world scale. Nevertheless, Eritrea is one of the few countries to be on target to meet its Millennium Development Goal targets for health.
eritrea.title: Health in Eritrea

eritrea.text: This is a list of streams and rivers in Eritrea, arranged geographically by drainage basin. This is a list of rivers in Eritrea, organized by drainage basin. Generally, rivers in Eritrea drain into 3 different basins: those that drain into Sudan, towards the Red Sea and towards the Afar Depression.
eritrea.title: List of rivers of Eritrea

eritrea.text: The geology of Eritrea in east Africa broadly consists of Precambrian rocks in the west, Paleozoic glacial sedimentary rocks in the South and Cenozoic sediments and volcanics along the coastal zone adjoining the Red Sea.
eritrea.title: Geology of Eritrea

eritrea.text: The wildlife of Eritrea is composed of its flora and fauna. Eritrea has 96 species of mammals and a rich avifauna of 566 species of birds.
eritrea.title: Wildlife of Eritrea

eritrea.text: The foreign relations of Eritrea are the policies of the Eritrean government by which it administers its external relations with other nations. Since its independence, Eritrea's foreign relations have been dominated by conflict and confrontation, both in the regional and international arenas.
eritrea.title: Foreign relations of Eritrea

eritrea.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Eritrea. Eritrea is a country in the North East of Africa. The capital is Asmara. It is bordered by Sudan in the west, Ethiopia in the south, and Djibouti in the southeast.
eritrea.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Eritrea

eritrea.text: The music of Eritrea, is a diverse mix of traditional and popular styles originating from ancient to modern times.
eritrea.title: Music of Eritrea

eritrea.text: Eritrean cuisine is based on Eritrea's native culinary traditions, but also arises from social interchanges with other regions.
eritrea.title: Eritrean cuisine

eritrea.text: There are approximately sixteen nationally recognized public holidays in Eritrea. The most important national holidays are Independence Day, Martyrs' Day, and Revolution Day.
eritrea.title: Public holidays in Eritrea

eritrea.text: The two main religions in Eritrea are Christianity and Islam. However, the number of adherents of each faith is subject to debate. Estimates of the Christian share of the population range from 47% to 53%, while estimates of the Muslim share of the population range from 37% to 52%.
eritrea.title: Religion in Eritrea

eritrea.text: The main languages spoken in Eritrea are Tigrinya, Tigre, Kunama, Bilen, Nara, Saho, Afar, and Beja. The country's working languages are Tigrinya, Arabic, English, and formerly Italian.
eritrea.title: Languages of Eritrea

eritrea.text: The history of cinema in Eritrea dates back to the country's colonial rule under the Kingdom of Italy.
eritrea.title: Cinema of Eritrea

eritrea.text: Sports in Eritrea primarily consist of football, cycling, and long-distance running. Football is a popular recreational sport, and at a professional level it is played under the authority of the Eritrean National Football Federation.
eritrea.title: Sport in Eritrea

eritrea.text: Eritrean literature in the Tigrinya language dates, as far as is known, from the late 19th century but Ge'ez writings have been found in the 4th century BC.
eritrea.title: Eritrean literature

eritrea.text: Transport in Eritrea includes highways, airports and seaports, in addition to various forms of public and private vehicular, maritime and aerial transportation.
eritrea.title: Transport in Eritrea

eritrea.text: Telecommunications in Eritrea are regulated and operated primarily by Eritrea Telecommunication Services Corporation, a Government of Eritrea organization. The country's telecommunications infrastructure includes fixed-line telephone, mobile telephone, and Internet services.
eritrea.title: Telecommunications in Eritrea

eritrea.text: Agriculture is one of the main economic activities in Eritrea. Agriculture made up 20% of the country its GDP in 2021. Eritrea has 565,000 hectares of arable land and permanent crops. 70% of the Eritrean workforce is employed in agriculture, accounting for roughly one-third of the economy.
eritrea.title: Agriculture in Eritrea

eritrea.text: Energy in Eritrea is an industry lacking in natural resources, though it has plenty of potential. Eritrea's final consumption of electricity is 33 kilotonne of oil equivalent.
eritrea.title: Energy in Eritrea

estonia.text: Politics in Estonia takes place in a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic republic, whereby the Prime Minister of Estonia is the head of government, and of a multi-party system. Legislative power is vested in the Estonian parliament.
estonia.title: Politics of Estonia

estonia.text: The demographics of Estonia in the 21st century result from historical trends over more than a thousand years, as with most European countries, but have been disproportionately influenced by events in the second half of the 20th century.
estonia.title: Demographics of Estonia

picture.credit: Original uploader was Digwuren at en.wikipedia

estonia.text: The history of formal education in Estonia dates back to the 13–14th centuries when the first monastic and cathedral schools were founded. The first primer in the Estonian language was published in 1575.
estonia.title: Education in Estonia

estonia.text: A new measure of expected human capital calculated for 195 countries from 1990 to 2016 and defined for each birth cohort as the expected years lived from age 20 to 64 years and adjusted for educational attainment, learning or education quality, and functional health status was published by The Lancet in September 2018.
estonia.title: Health in Estonia

estonia.text: Rivers of Estonia are short and mostly have a small discharge. Only 10 rivers are longer than 100 km. The largest river is the Narva on the Estonian–Russian border, whose average discharge is larger than that of all other Estonian rivers combined.
estonia.title: List of rivers of Estonia

estonia.text: The geology of Estonia is the study of rocks, minerals, water, landforms and geologic history in Estonia. The crust is part of the East European Craton and formed beginning in the Paleoproterozoic nearly two billion years ago.
estonia.title: Geology of Estonia

estonia.text: Estonia is a small, heavily forested country situated on the Baltic Sea. It is a part of the Euro-Siberian region of terrestrial Palearctic realm, and the Temperate Northern Atlantic marine ecoregion.
estonia.title: Fauna of Estonia

estonia.text: List of hills in Estonia.
estonia.title: List of mountains in Estonia

estonia.text: Estonia lies in the northern part of the temperate climate zone and in the transition zone between maritime and continental climate.
estonia.title: Climate of Estonia

estonia.text: The Republic of Estonia gained its independence from the Russian Empire on 24 February 1918 and established diplomatic relations with many countries via membership of the League of Nations.
estonia.title: Foreign relations of Estonia

estonia.text: Two years after the end of the Estonian War of Independence, the Estonian Army consisted of 3 field divisions and a number of small independent battalions and companies. The Republic of Estonia consisted of 47,750 km2 of territory, with a population of 1,107,000 inhabitants.
estonia.title: Military history of Estonia

estonia.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Estonia. The stamps of Estonia are issued by the postal administration Eesti Post which is the country's only provider of universal postal services. In 1625, mainland Estonia came entirely under Swedish Empire rule.
estonia.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Estonia

estonia.text: The recorded history of music in Estonia dates as far back as the 12th century.
estonia.title: Music of Estonia

estonia.text: Traditional Estonian cuisine has substantially been based on meat and potatoes, and on fish in coastal and lakeside areas. However, it now shows influences from a variety of international cuisines and ingredients, with a number of contributions from the traditions of nearby countries.
estonia.title: Estonian cuisine

estonia.text: All official holidays in Estonia are established by acts of Parliament.
estonia.title: Public holidays in Estonia

estonia.text: Estonia, historically a Lutheran Christian nation, is today one of the least religious countries in the world in terms of declared attitudes, with only 14 percent of the population declaring religion to be an important part of their daily life.
estonia.title: Religion in Estonia

estonia.text: The official language of Estonia is Estonian, a Uralic language of the Finnic branch, which is related to Finnish. It is unrelated to the bordering Russian and Latvian languages, both of which are Indo-European.
estonia.title: Languages of Estonia

estonia.text: Cinema of Estonia is the film industry of the Republic of Estonia. The motion pictures have won international awards and each year new Estonian films are seen at film festivals around the globe.
estonia.title: Cinema of Estonia

estonia.text: Sport plays an important role in Estonian culture. Estonia first competed as a nation at the 1920 Summer Olympics, although the National Olympic Committee was established in 1923. Estonian athletes took part at every Olympic Games until the country was annexed by the Soviet Union in 1940.
estonia.title: Sport in Estonia

estonia.text: This article covers the architecture of Estonia.
estonia.title: Architecture of Estonia

estonia.text: Estonian literature is literature written in the Estonian language The oldest records of written Estonian date from the 13th century. Originates Livoniae in Chronicle of Henry of Livonia contains Estonian place names, words and fragments of sentences.
estonia.title: Estonian literature

estonia.text: Estonian art is art that comes from Estonia, from Estonian artists or art pieces relating to Estonia. Starting from prehistoric art, there are no caves with paintings in Estonia. About 1700 registered cup stones have been found from the Bronze Age and archaeological finds from the Neolithic period.
estonia.title: Estonian art

estonia.text: Transport in Estonia relies mainly on road and rail networks.
estonia.title: Transport in Estonia

estonia.text: Tourism in Estonia refers to the overall state of the tourism industry in the Baltic nation of Estonia. It is a key part of the country's economy, contributing 7.8% to its GDP, and employing 4.3% of its population.
estonia.title: Tourism in Estonia

estonia.text: Telecommunications in Estonia describes the infrastructure, market, and regulatory environment for telecommunication services in the country. Since regaining independence in 1991, Estonia has developed from a poorly connected Soviet republic into one of the world's most advanced digital nations.
estonia.title: Telecommunications in Estonia

estonia.text: Traditionally, agriculture in Estonia has emphasized livestock production, with most crops grown for feed. Farmers also grow potatoes, vegetables, flax and sugar beet. The industry has been in great flux since the degeneration of the collective and state farm systems.
estonia.title: Agriculture in Estonia

estonia.text: Energy in Estonia has heavily depended on fossil fuels. Finland and Estonia are two of the last countries in the world still burning peat. Estonia has set a target of 100% of electricity production from renewable sources by 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050.
estonia.title: Energy in Estonia

eswatini.text: Eswatini is an absolute monarchy with constitutional provisions and Swazi law and Custom. The head of state is the king or Ngwenyama, currently King Mswati III, who ascended to the throne in 1986 after the death of his father King Sobhuza II in 1982 and a period of regency.
eswatini.title: Politics of Eswatini

eswatini.text: Demographic features of the population of Eswatini include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
eswatini.title: Demographics of Eswatini

eswatini.text: Education in Eswatini includes pre-school, primary, secondary and high schools, for general education and training, and universities and colleges at tertiary level. Pre-school education is usually for children five years or younger.
eswatini.title: Education in Eswatini

eswatini.text: The Health Sector in Eswatini is deteriorating and four years into the United Nations sustainable development goals, Eswatini seems unlikely to achieve the goal on good health.
eswatini.title: Health in Eswatini

eswatini.text: This is a list of rivers in Eswatini. This list is arranged by drainage basin, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
eswatini.title: List of rivers of Eswatini

eswatini.text: The geology of Eswatini formed beginning 3.6 billion years ago, in the Archean Eon of the Precambrian.
eswatini.title: Geology of Eswatini

eswatini.text: The wildlife of Eswatini is composed of its flora and fauna. The country has 107 species of mammals and 507 species of birds.
eswatini.title: Wildlife of Eswatini

eswatini.text: Eswatini is a member of the United Nations, the Commonwealth of Nations, the African Union, the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa, and the Southern African Development Community.
eswatini.title: Foreign relations of Eswatini

eswatini.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Eswatini, formerly Swaziland. The first stamps of Swaziland were overprinted stamps of South African Republic issued 18 October 1889.
eswatini.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Eswatini

eswatini.text: The cuisine of Eswatini is largely determined by the seasons and the geographical region. Staple foods in Eswatini include sorghum and maize, often served with goat meat. The farming industry mainly depends on sugarcane, tobacco, rice, maize, peanuts, and the export of goat meat and beef.
eswatini.title: Cuisine of Eswatini

eswatini.text: This is a list of holidays in Eswatini. If a holiday falls on a Sunday, it may be celebrated on the following Monday.
eswatini.title: Public holidays in Eswatini

eswatini.text: Christianity is the predominant religion in Eswatini, with Protestantism being its largest denomination. The royal family of Eswatini is officially Christian. The Constitution of the Kingdom provides for freedom of religion and the government generally respects religious liberty.
eswatini.title: Religion in Eswatini

eswatini.text: Eswatini is home to two official languages. The native language is Siswati. Recent immigrant languages include Chichewa, Tsonga, and Zulu.
eswatini.title: Languages of Eswatini

eswatini.text: Public transport is the main means of transportation in Eswatini. Car ownership is low, at 89 cars per 1,000 people, with a total of 297,000 vehicles on the local roads. The National Road Network has 1500 km of main roads and 2270 km of district roads.
eswatini.title: Transport in Eswatini

eswatini.text: Tourism in Eswatini developed during the apartheid era in South Africa and this shaped many of its distinctive attractions. Since the end of apartheid, Eswatini has emphasized its traditional culture as a tourist attraction. Most of the tourists who visit Eswatini arrive by road from South Africa.
eswatini.title: Tourism in Eswatini

eswatini.text: Telecommunications in Eswatini includes radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
eswatini.title: Telecommunications in Eswatini

eswatini.text: The mining industry of Eswatini vests with the Ngwenyama who authorizes mineral rights after due consultation with the Minerals Committee, which he appoints. Fiscal contribution from mining operations to Eswatini's GDP is 2% and also accounts for 2% of export earnings.
eswatini.title: Mining industry of Eswatini

ethiopia.text: The politics of Ethiopia are the activities associated with the governance of Ethiopia. The government is structured as a federal parliamentary republic with both a President and Prime Minister. The legislature is multicameral, with a house of representatives and a council.
ethiopia.title: Politics of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: The demographics of Ethiopia encompass the demographic features of inhabitants in Ethiopia, including ethnicity, languages, population density, education level, health, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
ethiopia.title: Demographics of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Education in Ethiopia was dominated by the Ethiopian Orthodox Church for many centuries until secular education was adopted in the early 1900s.
ethiopia.title: Education in Ethiopia

picture.credit: Pete Lewis / UK Department for International Dev

ethiopia.text: Health in Ethiopia has improved markedly since the early 2000s, with government leadership playing a key role in mobilizing resources and ensuring that they are used effectively.
ethiopia.title: Health in Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: This is a list of streams and rivers in Ethiopia, arranged geographically by drainage basin. There is an alphabetic list at the end of this article.
ethiopia.title: List of rivers of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: The geology of Ethiopia includes rocks of the Neoproterozoic East African Orogeny, Jurassic marine sediments and Quaternary rift-related volcanism. Events that greatly shaped Ethiopian geology include the assembly and break-up of Gondwana and the present-day rifting of Africa.
ethiopia.title: Geology of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: The richness and variety of the wildlife of Ethiopia is dictated by the great diversity of terrain with wide variations in climate, soils, natural vegetation and settlement patterns.
ethiopia.title: Wildlife of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: This is a list of notable mountains in Ethiopia
ethiopia.title: List of mountains in Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: The Climate of Ethiopia is highly diverse, ranging from equatorial rainforest with high rainfall and humidity in the south and southwest, to Afromontane regions on the summits of Semien and Bale Mountains to desert region in northeast, east and southeast Ethiopia.
ethiopia.title: Climate of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: The foreign relations of Ethiopia refers to overall diplomatic relationship of Ethiopia. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs oversees foreign relations and diplomatic missions of the country.
ethiopia.title: Foreign relations of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: The military history of Ethiopia dates back to the foundation of early Ethiopian Kingdoms in 980 BC.
ethiopia.title: Military history of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Ethiopia. Long an independent state in Africa, messages were originally carried by couriers called méléktegnas, who held the letters attached to a stick.
ethiopia.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Ethiopian music is a term that can mean any music of Ethiopian origin, however, often it is applied to a genre, a distinct modal system that is pentatonic, with characteristically long intervals between some notes.
ethiopia.title: Music of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Ethiopian cuisine characteristically consists of vegetable and often very spicy meat dishes. This is usually in the form of wat, a thick stew, served on top of injera, a large sourdough flatbread, which is about 50 centimeters in diameter and made out of fermented teff flour.
ethiopia.title: Ethiopian cuisine

ethiopia.text: The following lists are public holidays in Ethiopia. Many holidays follow the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church.
ethiopia.title: Public holidays in Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Religion in Ethiopia consists of a number of faiths. Among these mainly Abrahamic religions, the most numerous is Christianity whose adherents collectively form 67.3% of the population, followed by Islam, adhered to by 31.3%. There is also a longstanding but small Ethiopian Jewish community.
ethiopia.title: Religion in Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: The languages of Ethiopia include the official languages of Ethiopia, its national and regional languages, and a large number of minority languages, as well as foreign languages.
ethiopia.title: Languages of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: The Ethiopian film industry is growing significantly marked by a surge in digital, locally produced Amharic-language films since 1990s and 2000s. Historically, live stage theater enjoyed more popularity in Ethiopia, creating a handful of relatively successful stage actors.
ethiopia.title: Cinema of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Sports in Ethiopia include many fields. Association football is the most popular sport in Ethiopia, followed by athletics. Ethiopia is best known internationally for its middle-distance and long-distance runners. Seifu Mekonnen was an Olympic contestant for Ethiopia in boxing.
ethiopia.title: Sport in Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: The architecture of Ethiopia varies greatly from region to region. Over the years, it has incorporated various architectural styles and techniques.
ethiopia.title: Architecture of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Ethiopian literature dates from Ancient Ethiopian literature up until modern Ethiopian literature. Ancient Ethiopian literature starts with Axumite texts written in the Geʽez language using the Geʽez script, indigenous to both Ethiopia and Eritrea.
ethiopia.title: Ethiopian literature

picture.credit: A. Davey from Where I Live Now: Pacific Northwes

ethiopia.text: Ethiopian art is the manifestation in art of the Ethiopian civilization. In a primarily Christian civilization, Ethiopian art traditions have developed for millennia alongside Christian Art the world over, and since the 7th century, the Islamic artistic traditions as well.
ethiopia.title: Ethiopian art

ethiopia.text: Transport in Ethiopia is overseen by the Ministry of Transport and Communications. Over the last years, the Ethiopian federal authorities have significantly increased funding for rail and road construction to build an infrastructure, that allows better economic development.
ethiopia.title: Transport in Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Tourism in Ethiopia accounted for 5.5% of the country's gross domestic product in 2006, having barely increased 2% over the previous year. The government is proving its commitment and willingness to develop tourism through a number of initiatives.
ethiopia.title: Tourism in Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Telecommunications in Ethiopia is a monopoly in the control of Ethio telecom, formerly the Ethiopian Telecommunications Corporation. As of 2012, 20.524 million cellular phones and 797,500 main line phones were in use.
ethiopia.title: Telecommunications in Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Agriculture in Ethiopia is the foundation of the country's economy. According to World Bank, agriculture, forestry, and fishing accounted for approximately 32.8% of Ethiopia’s GDP in 2025, while agriculture employed around 60% of the country’s workforce.
ethiopia.title: Agriculture in Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Energy in Ethiopia includes energy and electricity production, consumption, transport, exportation, and importation in the country of Ethiopia. Ethiopia's energy sector is crucial for its development, with wood being a primary energy source, leading to deforestation challenges.
ethiopia.title: Energy in Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Mining is important to the economy of Ethiopia as a diversification from agriculture. Currently, mining comprises only 1% of GDP. Gold, gemstones, and industrial minerals are important commodities for the country's export-oriented growth strategy.
ethiopia.title: Mining in Ethiopia

falkland-islands.text: The demographics of the Falkland Islands have been measured by census since 1851.
falkland-islands.title: Demographics of the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: Education in the Falkland Islands starts with childcare for babies, all the way to lifelong learning for adults. It broadly follows the English education system with Falklands local content. Most teachers are trained in the UK or other English-speaking countries.
falkland-islands.title: Education in the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: Due its geography and geology, the Falkland Islands has no particularly large rivers. Those of some length tend to be sluggish, often ending in one of the frequent fjords or large inlets surrounding the Islands as creeks.
falkland-islands.title: List of rivers of the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: The geology of the Falkland Islands is described in several publications. The Falkland Islands are located on a projection of the Patagonian continental shelf.
falkland-islands.title: Geology of the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: The wildlife of the Falkland Islands is quite similar to that of Patagonia. The Falkland Islands have no native reptiles or amphibians, and the only native land mammal, the warrah, is now extinct.
falkland-islands.title: Wildlife of the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: The climate of the Falkland Islands is cool and temperate, regulated by the large oceans which surround it.
falkland-islands.title: Climate of the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: The Falkland Islands are a British overseas territory and, as such, rely on the United Kingdom for the guarantee of their security.
falkland-islands.title: Military of the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of the Falkland Islands.
falkland-islands.title: Postage stamps and postal history of the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: "Song of the Falklands" is the Territorial anthem of the Falkland Islands. It was written in the 1930s by Christopher Lanham, a Hampshire schoolteacher, while working on West Falkland.
falkland-islands.title: Song of the Falklands

falkland-islands.text: Public holidays in the Falkland Islands are determined by the Executive Council of the Falkland Islands. There are currently nine annual public holidays in force in the Falklands, with several other observances throughout the year.
falkland-islands.title: Public holidays in the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: Christianity is the most predominant religion in the Falkland Islands; the primary denominations are Church of England, Roman Catholic, United Free Church, Lutheran, Jehovah's Witnesses, Seventh-day Adventists among others.
falkland-islands.title: Religion in the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: The only official language of the Falkland Islands is English, and this is spoken by everyone on a day-to-day basis. Spanish is spoken by 10% of the population, a significant minority. Most of the Spanish speakers are immigrants, foreign workers, and expats, predominantly from Chile.
falkland-islands.title: Languages of the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: Sport in the Falkland Islands is restricted by the islands' low, and generally scattered, population. Nonetheless, it has been able to send teams to the Commonwealth Games, and the Island Games.
falkland-islands.title: Sport in the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: The Falkland Islands currently have three primary means of transport – road, sea and air. However, in 1946, when Sir Miles Clifford arrived as governor, there were no air services, no roads outside Stanley and an indifferent sea service.
falkland-islands.title: Transport in the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: Telecommunications in the Falkland Islands includes radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
falkland-islands.title: Telecommunications in the Falkland Islands

faroe-islands.text: The politics of the Faroe Islands, an autonomous country of the Kingdom of Denmark, function within the framework of a parliamentary, representative democratic dependency, whereby the Prime Minister of the Faroe Islands is the head of government, and of a multi-party system.
faroe-islands.title: Politics of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: Demographic features of the population of the Faroe Islands include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population. The vast majority of the population are ethnic Faroese, of North Germanic descent.
faroe-islands.title: Demographics of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: The levels of education in the Faroe Islands are primary, secondary and higher education. Most institutions are funded by the state; there are few private schools in the country. Education is compulsory for 9 years between the ages of 7 and 16.
faroe-islands.title: Education in the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: The geology of the Faroe Islands shows parallels to the geology of Iceland, although volcanism in the Faroe Islands has ceased. Geologically, the Faroe Islands are around 60 million years old.
faroe-islands.title: Geology of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: The following is a list of mountains of the Faroes. Note, however, that several mountains have more than one peak. However, only the tallest peak is counted in this table.
faroe-islands.title: List of mountains of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: Being part of the Kingdom of Denmark, the foreign relations of the Faroe Islands are handled by the government of the Faroe Islands in conjunction with the Danish government. Unlike Denmark, the Faroe Islands is not a part of the European Union.
faroe-islands.title: Foreign relations of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: The postage stamps and postal history of the Faroe Islands began in the 1860s with a message exchange system called Skjúts, which was before a regular boat service was established between the islands.
faroe-islands.title: Postage stamps and postal history of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: Faroese music is primarily vocal, accompanied by the fiddle and European dances like the minuet and polka.
faroe-islands.title: Music of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: Important parts of Faroese cuisine are lamb and also fish owing to proximity to the sea. Traditional foods from the Faroe Islands include skerpikjøt, seafood, whale meat, blubber, garnatálg, Atlantic puffins, potatoes, and few fresh vegetables.
faroe-islands.title: Faroese cuisine

faroe-islands.text: This is a list of public holidays in the Faroe Islands.
faroe-islands.title: Public holidays in the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: Religion in the Faroe Islands is dominated by the Lutheran Christianity. Historically linked to both Norway and Denmark, the islands' religious evolution reflects a blend of Norse traditions and Danish influences.
faroe-islands.title: Religion in the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: The national language of the Faroe Islands is Faroese. The Faroese language is a Germanic language which is descended from Old Norse. Danish is the official second language. Faroese is similar in grammar to Icelandic and Old Norse, but closer in pronunciation to Norwegian.
faroe-islands.title: Languages of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: Due to its small population size and the high initial cost of filmmaking, the cinema history of the Faroe Islands is modest. The first film director of the Faroe Islands was Katrin Ottarsdóttir. Her first film set in the Faroe Islands was Atlantic Rhapsody.
faroe-islands.title: Cinema of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: Faroese literature, in the traditional sense of the word, has only really developed in the past two hundred years. This is mainly because of the islands' isolation, and also because the Faroese language was not written down in a standardised format until 1890.
faroe-islands.title: Faroese literature

faroe-islands.text: Faroese art is art by artists living in the Faroe Islands and art by Faroese nationals living abroad. In the Faroe Islands, art is an important part of everyday life and in the public debate. It may be the special light in the Faroes which causes so many to express themselves in painting.
faroe-islands.title: Faroese art

faroe-islands.text: The Faroe Islands is served by an internal transport system based on roads, ferries, and helicopters. As of the 1970s, the majority of the population centres of the Faroe Islands have been joined to a single road network, connected by bridges and tunnels.
faroe-islands.title: Transport in the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: Tourism in the Faroe Islands is a growing industry. The official tourist board is Visit Faroe Islands, which is overseen and organized by the Ministry of Environment, Industry and Trade. Tourism in the islands accounted for 1.4% of the total GDP in 2015.
faroe-islands.title: Tourism in the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: Energy in the Faroe Islands is produced primarily from imported fossil fuels, with further contributions from hydro and wind power. Oil products are the main energy source, mainly consumed by fishing vessels and sea transport.
faroe-islands.title: Energy in the Faroe Islands

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: The politics of the Federated States of Micronesia takes place in a framework of a federal assembly-independent representative democratic republic. The President of the Federated States of Micronesia is both head of state and head of government.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Politics of the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: Demographic features of the population of the Federated States of Micronesia include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Demographics of the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: Education in the Federated States of Micronesia is required for citizens aged 6 to 14, and is important to their economy. The literacy rate for citizens aged 15 to 24 is 98.8%. The national education agency is the FSM Department of Education.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Education in the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: The Human Rights Measurement Initiative finds that the Federated States of Micronesia are fulfilling 94.9% of what it should be fulfilling for the right to health based on its level of income.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Health in the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: This is a list of the rivers of the Federated States of Micronesia, arranged by State:
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: List of rivers of the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: The government of the Federated States of Micronesia conducts its own foreign relations. Since independence in 1986, the FSM has established diplomatic relations with 92 countries, including all of its Pacific neighbors.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Foreign relations of the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of the Federated States of Micronesia. The Federated States of Micronesia are located in the Caroline Islands in the western Pacific Ocean and consist of over 600 islands.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Postage stamps and postal history of the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: The traditional music of the Federated States of Micronesia varies widely across the four states, and has, in recent times, evolved into popular music influenced by Europop, country music and reggae.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Music and dances of the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: This is a list of public holidays in the Federated States of Micronesia.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Public holidays in the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: Christianity is the predominant religion in the Federated States of Micronesia and represents an integral part of the nation's identity. The country is secular and its constitution guarantees the freedom of religion.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Religion in the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: Despite its small size, the Federated States of Micronesia is a multilingual country: according to Ethnologue there are 17 living and endemic languages in the country of 115,000 people. 89 % of the population is literate.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Languages of the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: Railways: 0 km Highways: total: 388 kilometers paved: 42 kilometers unpaved: 198 kilometers Ports and harbors: Colonia, Kolonia, Lele, Moen Merchant marine: total: three ships 3,560 GT/2,060 tonnes deadweight by type: cargo one, passenger/cargo two Airports: Six Airports - with paved runways: total: Six 1,524 to 2,437 m: Four 914 to 1,523 m: Two
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Transportation in the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: This article is about communications systems in the Federated States of Micronesia. In 2010, Pohnpei State was connected to the Internet using the HANTRU-1 undersea communications cable to provide high-speed bandwidth.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Telecommunications in the Federated States of Micronesia

fiji.text: The politics of Fiji take place within the framework of a parliamentary representative democratic republic. Fiji has a multiparty system with the Prime Minister of Fiji as head of government. The executive power is exercised by the government.
fiji.title: Politics of Fiji

fiji.text: The demographic characteristics of the population of Fiji are known through censuses, usually conducted in ten-year intervals, and has been analysed by statistical bureaus since the 1880s.
fiji.title: Demographics of Fiji

fiji.text: Primary school education in Fiji is compulsory, and subsidized for eight years. In 1978, the gross primary enrollment ratio was 113.5 percent, and the net primary enrollment rate was 97.7 percent.
fiji.title: Education in Fiji

fiji.text: Life expectancy in Fiji is 66 years for men and 72 years for women. Maternal mortality was 59 per 100 000 live births in 2013. The Human Rights Measurement Initiative finds that Fiji is fulfilling 76.5% of what it should be fulfilling for the right to health based on its level of income.
fiji.title: Health in Fiji

fiji.text: This is a list of the rivers of Fiji. They are listed by island in clockwise order, starting at the north end of each island. Tributaries are listed under the parent stream.
fiji.title: List of rivers of Fiji

fiji.text: Fiji has experienced many coups recently, in 1987, 2000, and 2006. Fiji has been suspended various times from the Commonwealth of Nations, a grouping of mostly former British colonies.
fiji.title: Foreign relations of Fiji

picture.credit: Post Office of Fiji (left); Louis-Henri Mercier

fiji.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Fiji. Fiji is an island nation in Melanesia in the South Pacific Ocean about 2,000 km northeast of New Zealand's North Island. It was a former British colony. A postal system was formally established in Fiji in 1871.
fiji.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Fiji

fiji.text: Fiji is an island nation in the Pacific Ocean. Though geographically Melanesian, the music of Fiji is more Polynesian in character. Nevertheless, Fijian folk styles are distinct in their fusion of Polynesian and Melanesian traditions.
fiji.title: Music of Fiji

fiji.text: Fijian cuisine has long consisted of primarily foraged and farm-grown food. Although rice, wheat, and tea all became staples during Fiji's colonial era, native Fijians still eat primarily tubers and coconuts.
fiji.title: Fijian cuisine

fiji.text: Public holidays in Fiji reflect the country's cultural diversity. Each major religion in Fiji has a public holiday dedicated to it.
fiji.title: List of festivals in Fiji

fiji.text: According to the most recent census in 2017, just under 7 in 10 people in Fiji are Christian, with a sizable Hindu and Muslim minority. Religion tends to split along ethnic lines with most Indigenous Fijians being Christian and most Indo-Fijians being mostly Hindu or in some cases, Muslim.
fiji.title: Religion in Fiji

fiji.text: Fiji has four primary national languages: English, Fijian, Standard Hindi, and Fiji Hindi. While the 1997 constitution declared English, Fijian and Hindustani as official languages of the state, the 2013 constitution does not explicitly establish one.
fiji.title: Languages of Fiji

fiji.text: Fiji only began producing its own feature films in 2004, and has produced just one to date.
fiji.title: Cinema of Fiji

fiji.text: Rugby union is the most popular sport in Fiji; however, rugby league, netball, and association football are also widely played. Various forms of traditional boat racing and wrestling are also popular. Sports culture is unique as different racial fixes and cultures come together in a common interest.
fiji.title: Sport in Fiji

fiji.text: The architecture of Fiji has its own unique style and pattern. While Fiji is a famous travelling destination among tourists for its beaches and beauty, its architecture is unique and particularly attractive.
fiji.title: Architecture of Fiji

fiji.text: Among the first published works of Fijian literature, in the late 1960s and early 1970s, were Vivekanand Sharma, Raymond Pillai's and Subramani's short stories and Pio Manoa's poetry. The emergence of Fiji's written literature coincides with the country's transition to independence in 1970.
fiji.title: Fijian literature

fiji.text: Modes of transport in Fiji include rail, road, water, and air. The rail network is mainly used for movement of sugar cane. Suva and Lautoka are the largest seaports. There are 122 km of navigable inland waterways.
fiji.title: Transport in Fiji

fiji.text: Telecommunications in Fiji include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
fiji.title: Telecommunications in Fiji

finland.text: The politics of Finland take place within the framework of a parliamentary representative democracy. Finland is a republic whose head of state is President Alexander Stubb, who leads the nation's foreign policy and is the supreme commander of the Finnish Defence Forces.
finland.title: Politics of Finland

finland.text: The demographics of Finland is monitored by the Statistics Finland. Finland has a population of almost 5.7 million people, ranking it 19th out of 27 within the European Union.
finland.title: Demographics of Finland

finland.text: The educational system in Finland consists of daycare programmes, a one-year "preschool", and an 11-year compulsory basic comprehensive school. As of 2024, secondary general academic and vocational education, higher education and adult education are compulsory.
finland.title: Education in Finland

finland.text: The major causes of deaths in Finland are cardiovascular diseases, malignant tumors, dementia and Alzheimer's disease, respiratory diseases, alcohol related diseases and accidental poisoning by alcohol.
finland.title: Health in Finland

finland.text: This is a list of rivers of Finland. Listing begins with rivers flowing into the Baltic Sea, from the north, that is from the Swedish border. Tributaries are listed down the page in an upstream direction.
finland.title: List of rivers of Finland

finland.text: The geology of Finland is made up of a mix of geologically very young and very old materials. Common rock types are orthogneiss, granite, metavolcanics and metasedimentary rocks.
finland.title: Geology of Finland

finland.text: The wildlife of Finland is affected by prevailing environmental conditions. The phytogeography of Finland is shared between the Arctic, central European, and northern European provinces of the Circumboreal Region within the Boreal Kingdom.
finland.title: Wildlife of Finland

finland.text: The summit of Halti at 1,365 m is in Norway, which makes Ridnitsohkka the highest summit in Finland.
finland.title: List of mountains in Finland

finland.text: The climate of Finland is influenced most by its latitude: Finland is located between 60 and 70 N. Because of Finland's northern location, winter is the longest season. Only on the south coast and in the southwest is summer as long as winter.
finland.title: Climate of Finland

finland.text: The foreign relations of Finland are the responsibility of the president of Finland, who leads foreign policy in cooperation with the government. Implicitly the government is responsible for internal policy and decision making in the European Union.
finland.title: Foreign relations of Finland

finland.text: The military history of Finland consists of hundreds of years of armed actions in the territory encompassing modern Finland.
finland.title: Military history of Finland

picture.credit: Scanned and processed by Andrei Sdobnikov

finland.text: Finland has produced postage stamps for use since 1856.
finland.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Finland

finland.text: The music of Finland can be roughly divided into folk music, classical and contemporary art music, and contemporary popular music. The folk music of Finland belongs to a broader musical tradition, common amongst Balto-Finnic people, sung in the so-called Kalevala metre.
finland.title: Music of Finland

finland.text: All official holidays in Finland are established by acts of Parliament. The official holidays can be divided into Christian and non-Christian holidays. The main Christian holidays are Christmas, New Year's Day, Epiphany, Easter, Ascension day, Pentecost, Midsummer Day, and All Saints' Day.
finland.title: Public holidays in Finland

finland.text: Finland is a predominantly Christian nation where 61.2% of the Finnish population of 5.7 million are members of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Finland, 35.9% are unaffiliated, 1.0% are Orthodox Christians, and 1.8% follow other religions.
finland.title: Religion in Finland

finland.text: The two main official languages of Finland are Finnish and Swedish. There are also several official minority languages: three Sámi languages, as well as Romani, Finnish Sign Language, Finland-Swedish Sign Language and Karelian.
finland.title: Languages of Finland

finland.text: The Finnish cinema has a long history, with the first public screenings starting almost as early as modern motion picture technology was invented. It took over a decade before the first Finnish film was produced and screened in 1907.
finland.title: Cinema of Finland

finland.text: Sport is considered a national pastime in Finland and many Finns visit different sporting events regularly. Pesäpallo is the national sport of Finland, although the most popular forms of sport in terms of television viewers and media coverage are ice hockey and Formula One.
finland.title: Sport in Finland

finland.text: The architecture of Finland has a history spanning over 800 years, and while up until the modern era the architecture was highly influenced by Sweden, there were also influences from Germany and Russia.
finland.title: Architecture of Finland

finland.text: Finnish literature refers to literature written in Finland. During the European early Middle Ages, the earliest text in a Finnic language is the unique thirteenth-century Birch bark letter no. 292 from Novgorod.
finland.title: Finnish literature

finland.text: Finnish art started to form its individual characteristics in the 19th century when romantic nationalism began to rise in the autonomous Grand Duchy of Finland.
finland.title: Finnish art

finland.text: The transport system of Finland is well-developed. Factors affecting traffic include the sparse population and long distance between towns and cities, and the cold climate with waterways freezing and land covered in snow for winter.
finland.title: Transport in Finland

finland.text: In 2025, Finland was visited by nearly 5.1 million foreign tourists, an increase of four percent compared to the previous year. Tourism generated approximately 3.7€ billion in export revenue for Finland's economy.
finland.title: Tourism in Finland

finland.text: Telecommunications in Finland, as indicated by a 2022 European Commission index, highlight the country's significant role in the EU's digital sector.
finland.title: Telecommunications in Finland

finland.text: Agriculture in Finland is characterized by the northern climate and self-sufficiency in most major agricultural products.
finland.title: Agriculture in Finland

finland.text: Energy in Finland describes energy and electricity production, consumption and import in Finland. Energy policy of Finland describes the politics of Finland related to energy. Electricity sector in Finland is the main article regarding electricity in Finland.
finland.title: Energy in Finland

france.text: France is a semi-presidential system determined by the Constitution of the Fifth Republic. The nation declares itself to be an "indivisible, secular, democratic, and social Republic".
france.title: Politics of France

france.text: The demography of France is monitored by the Institut national d'études démographiques and the Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques.
france.title: Demographics of France

france.text: Education in France is organized in a highly centralized manner, with many subdivisions. It is divided into the three stages of primary education, secondary education, and higher education. Two year olds do not start primary school, they start preschool.
france.title: Education in France

france.text: Life expectancy in France at birth was 81 years in 2008.
france.title: Health in France

picture.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Abrahami as

france.text: This is a list of rivers that are at least partially in France. The rivers are grouped by sea or ocean. The rivers flowing into the sea are sorted along the coast. Rivers flowing into other rivers are listed by the rivers they flow into.
france.title: List of rivers of France

france.text: The regional geology of France is commonly divided into the Paris Basin, the Armorican Massif, the Massif Central, the Aquitaine Basin, the Pyrenees, the Alps, the Côte languedocienne, the Sillon rhodanien, the Massif des Vosges, the Massif Ardennais, the Alsace graben and Flanders Basin.
france.title: Geology of France

france.text: The wildlife of France can be divided into that of Metropolitan France, and that of the French Overseas territories.
france.title: Wildlife of France

france.text: The following is a sortable table of the 37 peaks of continental France with a topographical prominence of at least 1,000 metres. This table includes all ultras with prominence of at least 1,500 m within continental France. Mountains located on islands and overseas departments are not included.
france.title: List of French mountains by prominence

france.text: The climate of France is the statistical distribution of conditions in the Earth's atmosphere over the national territory, based on the averages and variability of relevant quantities over a given period, the standard reference period defined by the World Meteorological Organization being 30 years.
france.title: Climate of France

france.text: In the 19th century France built a new French colonial empire second only to the British Empire. It was humiliated in the Franco-Prussian War of 1870–71, which marked the rise of Germany to dominance in Europe.
france.title: Foreign relations of France

france.text: The military history of France encompasses an immense panorama of conflicts and struggles extending for more than 2,000 years across areas including modern France, Europe, and a variety of regions throughout the world.
france.title: Military history of France

france.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of France.
france.title: Postage stamps and postal history of France

france.text: In France, music reflects a diverse array of styles. In the field of classical music, France has produced several prominent romantic composers, while folk and popular music have seen the rise of the chanson and cabaret style.
france.title: Music of France

france.text: French cuisine is the cooking traditions and practices of France. In the 14th century, Guillaume Tirel, a court chef known as "Taillevent", wrote Le Viandier, one of the earliest recipe collections of medieval France.
france.title: French cuisine

france.text: There are eleven official public holidays in France, of which three are movable days which always fall on a weekday. The Alsace region and the Moselle department observe two additional days.
france.title: Public holidays in France

france.text: Religion in France is diverse, with the largest religious group being Christianity. A very significant part of the population is not religious, and significant minorities profess Islam and other religions.
france.title: Religion in France

france.text: French is the sole official language in France according to the second article of the French Constitution. French, a Gallo-Romance language, is spoken by nearly the entire population of France.
france.title: Languages of France

picture.credit: Self made based upon work by the authors shown a

france.text: The cinema of France comprises the film industry and its film productions, whether made within the nation of France or by French film production companies abroad.
france.title: Cinema of France

france.text: Sport in France plays an important role in French society, which is reflected in its popularity among the French people and the nation's strong sporting history.
france.title: Sport in France

france.text: French architecture consists of architectural styles that either originated in France or elsewhere and were developed within the territories of France.
france.title: French architecture

france.text: French literature generally speaking, is literature written in the French language, particularly by French citizens; it may also refer to literature written by people living in France who speak traditional languages of France other than French.
france.title: French literature

france.text: French art consists of the visual and plastic arts originating from the geographical area of France. Modern France was one of the main centre for the European art of the Upper Paleolithic, then left many megalithic monuments, and in the Iron Age many of the most impressive finds of early Celtic art.
france.title: French art

france.text: Transportation in France relies on one of the densest networks in the world with 146 km of road and 6.2 km of rail lines per 100 km2. It is built as a web with Paris at its center. Rail, road, air and water are all widely developed forms of transportation in France.
france.title: Transport in France

france.text: Tourism in France is a significant contributor to the country's gross domestic product. In 2023, France ranked as the world's sixth-largest travel and tourism market, with the sector contributing US$264.7 billion to GDP.
france.title: Tourism in France

france.text: Telecommunications in France are highly developed.
france.title: Telecommunications in France

france.text: France is the largest producer of agricultural products in Europe. Favorable agro-climatic conditions contribute to this status. The country ranks among the top five exporters of agricultural products.
france.title: Agriculture in France

france.text: Energy in France was generated from five primary sources: nuclear power, natural gas, liquid fuels, renewables and coal. In 2025, mainland France generated 547.5 TWh of electricity, of which 95.2% came from low-carbon sources.
france.title: Energy in France

france.text: Mining in France is based solely on the nature of the material, whether extracted from the surface or underground. These include fuels, metals and a few other minerals. The inventory of mining resources is relatively well known for surface and subsurface deposits.
france.title: Mining in France

french-polynesia.text: Politics of French Polynesia takes place in a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic French overseas collectivity, whereby the President of French Polynesia is the head of government, and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government.
french-polynesia.title: Politics of French Polynesia

french-polynesia.text: Demographic features of the population of French Polynesia include population density, ethnicity, religious affiliations and other aspects.
french-polynesia.title: Demographics of French Polynesia

french-polynesia.text: The University of French Polynesia is a French university located in Tahiti at Puna'auia, French Polynesia.
french-polynesia.title: University of French Polynesia

french-polynesia.text: The following is a list of mountains in French Polynesia.
french-polynesia.title: List of mountains in French Polynesia

picture.credit: Post of Tahiti. The original uploader was Tanjee

french-polynesia.text: This is a survey of the postal history and postage stamps of French Polynesia, formerly known as the French Oceania. The first postage stamps used in French Polynesia were the general stamps of the French Colonies from 1862.
french-polynesia.title: Postage stamps and postal history of French Polynesia

french-polynesia.text: The music of French Polynesia came to the forefront of the world music scene in 1992, with the release of The Tahitian Choir's recordings of unaccompanied vocal Christian music called himene tārava, recorded by French musicologist Pascal Nabet-Meyer.
french-polynesia.title: Music of French Polynesia

french-polynesia.text: This is a list of public holidays in French Polynesia.
french-polynesia.title: Public holidays in French Polynesia

french-polynesia.text: Transport in French Polynesia is dominated by air travel, with a total of 37 airports with paved runways and another 13 airports without paved runways.
french-polynesia.title: Transport in French Polynesia

french-polynesia.text: This article is about communications systems in French Polynesia. The Honotua fiber optic cable connected Tahiti to Hawaii in 2010, increasing Internet speeds to 20 gigabits per second from 500 megabits per second.
french-polynesia.title: Telecommunications in French Polynesia

gabon.text: The politics of Gabon takes place in a framework of a republic whereby the president of Gabon is head of state and in effect, also the head of government, since he appoints the prime minister and his cabinet.
gabon.title: Politics of Gabon

gabon.text: The Demographics of Gabon is the makeup of the population of Gabon. As of 2020, Gabon has a population of 2,225,287. Gabon's population is relatively young with 35.5% of its population under 15 years of age and only 4.3% of its population over 65 years old.
gabon.title: Demographics of Gabon

gabon.text: Education in Gabon is largely based on the French educational system.
gabon.title: Education in Gabon

gabon.text: This is a list of rivers in Gabon. This list is arranged by drainage basin, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
gabon.title: List of rivers of Gabon

gabon.text: Gabon is situated at the northwestern margin of the Congo Craton—a region of stable, ancient crust—and preserves very ancient rock units across 75% of the country, with overlying sedimentary units from the Cretaceous and other more recent periods.
gabon.title: Geology of Gabon

gabon.text: The wildlife of Gabon is composed of its flora and fauna. Gabon is a largely low-lying country with a warm, humid climate. Much of the country is still covered by tropical rainforest and there are also grasslands, savannas, large rivers and coastal lagoons.
gabon.title: Wildlife of Gabon

gabon.text: Gabon has followed a non-aligned policy, advocating dialogue in international affairs and recognizing both parts of divided countries. Since 1973, the number of countries establishing diplomatic relations with Gabon has doubled.
gabon.title: Foreign relations of Gabon

gabon.text: Gabon is a country in west central Africa sharing borders with the Gulf of Guinea to the west, Equatorial Guinea to the northwest, and Cameroon to the north, with the Republic of the Congo curving around the east and south. Its size is almost 270,000 km2 with an estimated population of 1,500,000.
gabon.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Gabon

gabon.text: Music of Gabon encompasses the traditional, ritual, popular and urban musics of the Gabonese Republic.
gabon.title: Music of Gabon

gabon.text: Gabonese cuisine comprises the cooking traditions, practices, foods and dishes associated with Gabon, a sovereign state on the west coast of Central Africa. French cuisine is prevalent as a notable influence, and in larger cities various French specialties are available.
gabon.title: Gabonese cuisine

gabon.text: This is a list of holidays in Gabon.
gabon.title: Public holidays in Gabon

gabon.text: Christianity is the predominant religion in Gabon, with significant minorities of the adherents of Islam and traditional faiths. Gabon is a secular state and the constitution ensures freedom of religion. Many people practice elements of both Christianity and traditional indigenous religious beliefs.
gabon.title: Religion in Gabon

gabon.text: French is the official language in Gabon, spoken natively in large metropolitan areas and in total by 320,000 people or 14% of the country. 32% of the people speak Fang as a mother tongue. French is the medium of instruction.
gabon.title: Languages of Gabon

gabon.text: The cinema of Gabon has had an uneven history. Though President Omar Bongo and his wife, Josephine Bongo, encouraged filmmaking in the 1970s, there was a 20-year hiatus until filmmaking started to grow again in the new millennium.
gabon.title: Cinema of Gabon

gabon.text: Gabonese literature, like many African literatures, began as an oral tradition.
gabon.title: Gabonese literature

gabon.text: Modes of transport in Gabon include rail, road, water and air. The one rail link, the Trans-Gabon Railway, connects the port of Owendo with the inland town of Franceville. While most of the country is connected by roads, not all areas are accessible.
gabon.title: Transport in Gabon

gabon.text: Tourism in Gabon is underdeveloped. Despite this, attractions include beaches, ocean and inland fishing facilities, the falls on the Ogooué River, and the Crystal Mountains. Tourists also come to see the famous hospital founded by Dr. Albert Schweitzer in Lambaréné.
gabon.title: Tourism in Gabon

gabon.text: Telecommunications in Gabon include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
gabon.title: Telecommunications in Gabon

gabon.text: Energy in Gabon comes from two main sources: solid biofuels and waste, and fossil fuels, particularly oil. Just under half of Gabon's share of power generation comes from renewables. The country is heavily reliant on oil exports, such as crude oil and petroleum.
gabon.title: Energy in Gabon

georgia.text: Politics in Georgia involve a parliamentary representative democratic republic with a multi-party system. The President of Georgia is the ceremonial head of state and the Prime Minister of Georgia is the head of government. The Prime Minister and the Government wield executive power.
georgia.title: Politics of Georgia (country)

georgia.text: The demographic features of the population of Georgia include population growth, population density, ethnicity, education level, health, economic status, religious affiliations, and other aspects of the population.
georgia.title: Demographics of Georgia (country)

georgia.text: Education in Georgia is free of charge and compulsory for eight years, from the age of 6 until the age of 14. Children in Georgia are legally required to have a basic primary education.
georgia.title: Education in Georgia (country)

georgia.text: Healthcare in Georgia is provided by a universal health care system under which the state funds medical treatment in a mainly privatized system of medical facilities.
georgia.title: Healthcare in Georgia (country)

georgia.text: The rivers of Georgia, a country in the Caucasus, are part of either the Black Sea or Caspian Sea Drainage basins. The most spectacular rivers include the Alazani, Aragvi, Enguri, Kura, and Rioni. Georgia has about 25,000 rivers, many of which power small hydroelectric stations.
georgia.title: List of rivers of Georgia (country)

georgia.text: The geology of Georgia is dominated by the Caucasus Mountains at the junction of the Eurasian Plate and the Afro-Arabian Plate, and rock units from the Mesozoic and Cenozoic are particularly prevalent.
georgia.title: Geology of Georgia (country)

georgia.text: This List of Mountains in Georgia names the highest mountains in Georgia, country in the western part of the Caucasus. Georgia has 2672 prominent peaks. The highest peak in the country is the Shkhara, at 5193 meters one of the country's three five-thousanders.
georgia.title: List of mountains in Georgia (country)

georgia.text: Georgia's location, nestled between the Black Sea, Russia, and Turkey, renders it strategically important. It is developing as the gateway from the Black Sea to the Caucasus and the larger Caspian region, but also serves as a buffer between Russia and Turkey.
georgia.title: Foreign relations of Georgia
