hong-kong.text: Energy in Hong Kong refers to the type of energy and its related infrastructure used in Hong Kong. Energy is crucial for the development of trade and industries in Hong Kong with its relatively small usable land.
hong-kong.title: Energy in Hong Kong

hong-kong.text: Mining in Hong Kong refers to mining activities in Hong Kong. Despite its small size, Hong Kong has a relatively large number of mineral deposits. Although some have been mined commercially, there are currently no commercial mining operations in Hong Kong.
hong-kong.title: Mining in Hong Kong

hungary.text: The politics of Hungary take place in a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic republic. The prime minister is the head of government of a pluriform multi-party system, while the president is the head of state and holds a largely ceremonial position.
hungary.title: Politics of Hungary

hungary.text: Demographic features of the population of Hungary include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects.
hungary.title: Demographics of Hungary

hungary.text: The educational system in Hungary is predominantly public, run by the Ministry of Human Resources. Preschool kindergarten education is compulsory and provided for all children between three and six years old, after which school attendance is also compulsory until age of sixteen.
hungary.title: Education in Hungary

hungary.text: Although death rates have decreased in Hungary since 1985, life expectancy remains low by European standards, particularly among Romani people. Almost half the deaths are caused by cardiovascular disease.
hungary.title: Health in Hungary

hungary.text: Some of the Rivers of Hungary include:
hungary.title: List of rivers of Hungary

hungary.text: Hungary is in the Pannonian Basin in Central Europe, is surrounded by the Carpathians, Alps and Dinarides, but for the most part dominated by lowlands. Sixty-eight percent of the country is lowlands below 200 meters altitude. Hilly terrain covers 30% of the country, while mountains cover only 2%.
hungary.title: Geology of Hungary

hungary.text: This list of mountains in Hungary is actually a series of sortable tables of major mountain peaks of Hungary. The summit of a mountain or hill may be measured or sorted in several ways. The topographic elevation of a summit measures the height of the summit above a geodetic sea level.
hungary.title: List of mountains in Hungary

hungary.text: The climate of Hungary is determined by its position. Hungary is in the eastern part of Central Europe, roughly equidistant from the Equator and the North Pole, more than 1,000 kilometres from both and about 1,000 kilometres from the Atlantic Ocean.
hungary.title: Climate of Hungary

hungary.text: Hungary wields considerable influence in Central and Eastern Europe and is a middle power in international affairs.
hungary.title: Foreign relations of Hungary

hungary.text: The military history of Hungary includes battles fought in the Carpathian Basin and the military history of the Hungarian people regardless of geography.
hungary.title: Military history of Hungary

hungary.text: The postal history of Hungary is strongly linked to the history of Hungary. While a messenger system was brought to the Carpathian Basin by Árpád as early as 895, modern mail delivery was first organized by the Habsburgs under the Austrian Empire.
hungary.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Hungary

hungary.text: Hungary has made many contributions to the fields of folk, popular and classical music. Hungarian folk music is a prominent part of the national identity and continues to play a major part in Hungarian music.
hungary.title: Music of Hungary

hungary.text: Hungarian cuisine is the cuisine characteristic of the nation of Hungary, and its primary ethnic group, Hungarians. Hungarian cuisine has been described as being the spiciest cuisine in Europe.
hungary.title: Hungarian cuisine

hungary.text: A number of public holidays and special events take place each year in Hungary.
hungary.title: Public holidays in Hungary

hungary.text: Religion in Hungary is varied, with Christianity being the largest religion.
hungary.title: Religion in Hungary

hungary.text: The languages spoken in Hungary include Hungarian, recognized minority languages, and other languages.
hungary.title: Languages of Hungary

hungary.text: Hungary has had a cinema industry since the beginning of the 20th century including Hungarians within and beyond the country's borders. Directors include István Szabó, Béla Tarr, and Miklós Jancsó.
hungary.title: Cinema of Hungary

hungary.text: The architecture of Hungary is understood as the architecture of the territory of Hungary, and in a wider sense the historical territory of the Kingdom of Hungary. Architecture in Hungary reflects historical influences from foreign occupation, notably by the Habsburg, Ottoman and Soviet empires.
hungary.title: Architecture of Hungary

hungary.text: Hungarian literature is the body of written works primarily produced in Hungarian, and may also include works written in other languages, either produced by Hungarians or having topics which are closely related to Hungarian culture.
hungary.title: Hungarian literature

hungary.text: Hungarian art stems from the period of the conquest of the Carpathian basin by the people of Árpád in the 9th century. Prince Árpád also organized earlier people settled in the area.
hungary.title: Hungarian art

hungary.text: Transport in Hungary relies on several main modes, including transport by road, rail, air and water.
hungary.title: Transport in Hungary

hungary.text: There is a long history of tourism in Hungary, and Hungary was the world's thirteenth most visited tourist destination country in 2002. Tourism increased by nearly 7 percent between 2004 and 2005. European visitors comprise more than 98 per cent of Hungary's tourists.
hungary.title: Tourism in Hungary

hungary.text: Telecommunications in Hungary include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
hungary.title: Telecommunications in Hungary

hungary.text: As of 2024, almost half of energy in Hungary is imported, with nuclear being the main domestic source.
hungary.title: Energy in Hungary

iceland.text: The politics of Iceland take place in the framework of a parliamentary representative democratic republic, whereby the president is the head of state, while the prime minister of Iceland serves as the head of government in a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government.
iceland.title: Politics of Iceland

iceland.text: The demographics of Iceland include population density, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population. As of 2026, the Icelandic population is 394,324. In 2026, 77,226 residents were immigrants.
iceland.title: Demographics of Iceland

iceland.text: The system of education in Iceland is divided in four levels: playschool, compulsory, upper secondary and higher, and is similar to that of other Nordic countries. Education is mandatory for children aged 6–16.
iceland.title: Education in Iceland

iceland.text: Iceland had the third-lowest crude mortality rate in Europe, at 355 per 100,000 population in 2015. It had the lowest rate of male smokers in Europe: 17%.
iceland.title: Health in Iceland

iceland.text: On an island like Iceland, the rivers are short in length. None of the rivers are important as a means of navigation due to the impracticality of settlements in the Highlands of Iceland where they originate.
iceland.title: List of rivers of Iceland

iceland.text: The geology of Iceland is unique and so of particular interest to geologists. Iceland lies on the divergent boundary between the Eurasian plate and the North American plate. It also lies above a hotspot, the Iceland plume.
iceland.title: Geology of Iceland

iceland.text: The wildlife of Iceland is the wild plant and animal life found on the island of Iceland, located in the north Atlantic Ocean just south of the Arctic Circle. The flora, fauna, and funga is limited by the geography and climate of the island.
iceland.title: Wildlife of Iceland

iceland.text: This is a list of mountains in Iceland
iceland.title: List of mountains in Iceland

iceland.text: Iceland has a subpolar oceanic climate near the southern coastal area and tundra inland in the highlands. The island lies in the path of the North Atlantic Current, which makes its climate more temperate than would be expected for its latitude just south of the Arctic Circle.
iceland.title: Climate of Iceland

iceland.text: Iceland took control of its foreign affairs in 1918 when it became a sovereign country, the Kingdom of Iceland, in a personal union with the King of Denmark. As a fully independent state, Iceland could have joined the League of Nations in 1920, but chose not to do so for cost reasons.
iceland.title: Foreign relations of Iceland

iceland.text: This is a brief overview of historical warfare and recent developments in Iceland. Iceland has never participated in a full-scale war or invasion and the constitution of Iceland has no mechanism to declare war.
iceland.title: Military history of Iceland

iceland.text: Regular mail service in Iceland was first established by a charter of 13 May 1776, and on 1 January 1873, Iceland issued its first postage stamps. The design was the same as for the Danish numeral issue of the time, denominated with values ranging from 2 to 16 skilling, and inscribed ÍSLAND.
iceland.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Iceland

iceland.text: The music of Iceland includes folk and pop traditions, as well as an active classical and contemporary music scene.
iceland.title: Music of Iceland

iceland.text: The cuisine of Iceland has a long history. Important parts of Icelandic cuisine are lamb, dairy, and fish, the latter because Iceland has traditionally been inhabited only near its coastline.
iceland.title: Icelandic cuisine

iceland.text: Public holidays in Iceland are established by the act of the Icelandic parliament. The public holidays are the religious holidays of the Church of Iceland and the First Day of Summer, May Day, the Icelandic National Day. In addition, Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve are holidays from 1 PM.
iceland.title: Public holidays in Iceland

iceland.text: Religion in Iceland has been predominantly Christianity since its adoption as the state religion by the Althing under the influence of Olaf Tryggvason, the king of Norway, in 999/1000 CE.
iceland.title: Religion in Iceland

iceland.text: Iceland has been a very isolated and linguistically homogeneous island historically, but has nevertheless been home to several languages. Although the Icelandic or Norse language prevails, northern trade routes brought German, English, Dutch, French and Basque to Iceland.
iceland.title: Languages of Iceland

iceland.text: Iceland has a notable cinema film industry, with many Icelandic actors and directors having gone on to receive international attention.
iceland.title: Cinema of Iceland

iceland.text: Sports in Iceland are very popular. Popular sports include football, handball, athletics, basketball, chess, golf, volleyball, tennis, skiing, snowboarding, ice hockey, swimming, rock climbing, mountain climbing, horseback riding, archery, strongman, powerlifting and crossfit.
iceland.title: Sport in Iceland

iceland.text: The architecture of Iceland draws from Scandinavian influences and traditionally was influenced by the lack of native trees on the island. As a result, grass- and turf-covered houses were developed.
iceland.title: Architecture of Iceland

iceland.text: Icelandic literature refers to literature written in Iceland or by Icelandic people. It is best known for the sagas written in medieval times, starting in the 13th century.
iceland.title: Icelandic literature

iceland.text: Icelandic art has been built on northern European traditions of the nineteenth century, but developed in distinct directions in the twentieth century, influenced in particular by the unique Icelandic landscape as well as by Icelandic mythology and culture.
iceland.title: Icelandic art

iceland.text: The modes of transport in Iceland are governed by the country's rugged terrain and sparse population. Domestically, the principal mode of transportation is by road, supplemented by air transport for longer distances.
iceland.title: Transport in Iceland

iceland.text: Tourism in Iceland has grown considerably in economic significance. In 2025, the tourism industry accounted for 8.8% of Iceland's GDP, while the country received just under 2.3 million foreign overnight visitors.
iceland.title: Tourism in Iceland

iceland.text: Telecommunications in Iceland are a diversified market. Iceland has a highly developed telecommunications sector with modern infrastructure. Multiple wholesale and retail providers operate in a competitive market.
iceland.title: Telecommunications in Iceland

iceland.text: For centuries Iceland's main industries were fishing, fish processing and agriculture. In the 19th century, 70–80% of Icelanders lived by farming, but there has been a steady decline over the years and now that figure is less than 5% of the total population.
iceland.title: Agriculture in Iceland

iceland.text: Iceland is a world leader in renewable energy. 100% of the electricity in Iceland's electricity grid is produced from renewable resources. In terms of total energy supply, 85% of the total primary energy supply in Iceland is derived from domestically produced renewable energy sources.
iceland.title: Energy in Iceland

india.text: The politics and government in the Republic of India work in adherence to the Constitution of India, which was adopted on November 26, 1949, by the Constituent Assembly of India, and took effect on January 26, 1950.
india.title: Politics of India

india.text: India is the most populous country in the world, comprising approximately one-sixth of the world population. According to the United Nations' World Population Dashboard, India's population reached slightly over 1.414 billion on 1 July 2021, surpassing that of China.
india.title: Demographics of India

india.text: Education in India is primarily managed through the state-run public education system, which falls under the command of the government at three levels: central, state, and local.
india.title: Education in India

india.text: India's population in 2024 as per World Bank is 1.45 billion. Being the world's most populous country and one of its fastest-growing economies, India experiences both challenges and opportunities in context of public health.
india.title: Health in India

india.text: With a land area of 3,287,263 km2 consisting of diverse ecosystems, India has many river systems and perennial streams. The rivers of India can be classified into four groups – Himalayan, Deccan, Coastal, and Inland drainage.
india.title: List of rivers of India

india.text: The geology of India is diverse. Different regions of the Indian subcontinent contain rocks belonging to different geologic periods, dating as far back as the Eoarchean Era. Some of the rocks are very deformed and altered.
india.title: Geology of India

india.text: India is one of the most biodiverse regions and is home to a large variety of wildlife. It is one of the 17 megadiverse countries and includes four of the world's 36 biodiversity hotspots – the Western Ghats, the Himalaya, the Nicobar Islands and the Indo-Burma hotspot.
india.title: Wildlife of India

india.text: The climate of India includes a wide range of weather conditions, influenced by its vast geographic scale and varied topography. Based on the Köppen system, India encompasses a diverse array of climatic subtypes.
india.title: Climate of India

india.text: India, officially the Republic of India, has full diplomatic relations with 201 states, including Palestine, the Holy See, Niue and the Cook Islands. The Ministry of External Affairs is the government agency responsible for the conduct of foreign relations of India.
india.title: Foreign relations of India

india.text: There were a number of predecessors to the contemporary Army of India: the sepoy regiments, native cavalry, irregular horse and Indian sapper and miner companies raised by the three British presidencies.
india.title: Military history of India

india.text: Indian postal systems for efficient military and governmental communications had developed long before the arrival of Europeans.
india.title: Postage stamps and postal history of India

india.text: Indian music encompasses numerous genres in multiple varieties and forms which include classical music, folk, rock, and pop. It has a history spanning several millennia and developed over several geo-locations spanning the subcontinent.
india.title: Music of India

india.text: Indian cuisine is not a single homogeneous entity, but consists of the regional cuisines native to the Indian subcontinent. Indian food has been influenced by religion, cultural choices and traditions. Agriculture spread to the Indus Valley Civilisation around 7000 BCE, bringing cereal cultivation.
india.title: Indian cuisine

india.text: Public Holidays in India, also known as Government Holidays, consist of a variety of cultural, nationalistic, and religious holidays that are legislated in India at the union or state levels.
india.title: Public holidays in India

picture.credit: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

india.text: Religion in India is characterised by a diversity of religious beliefs and practices.
india.title: Religion in India

india.text: Languages of India belong to several language families, the major ones being the Indo-Aryan languages spoken by 78.05% of Indians and the Dravidian languages spoken by 19.64% of Indians; both families together are sometimes known as Indic languages.
india.title: Languages of India

india.text: The cinema of India, consisting of motion pictures made by the Indian film industry, has had a large effect on world cinema since the second half of the 20th century.
india.title: Cinema of India

india.text: India has a history of sports dating back to the Vedic period, with Western sports having been imported during British rule. Cricket is the most popular sport in India, enjoyed across the country, but especially popular in the northern, western, and central regions.
india.title: Sport in India

india.text: Indian architecture is rooted in the history, culture, and religion of India.
india.title: Architecture of India

india.text: Indian literature refers to the literature produced on the Indian subcontinent until 1947 and in the Republic of India thereafter. The Eighth Schedule to the Constitution of India has 22 officially recognised languages.
india.title: Indian literature

india.text: Indian art consists of a variety of art forms, including painting, sculpture, pottery, and textile arts such as woven silk.
india.title: Indian art

india.text: Transport in India consists of transport by land, water and air. Road transport is the primary mode of transport for most Indian citizens, and India's road transport systems are among the most heavily used in the world.
india.title: Transport in India

india.text: Tourism in India is 4.6% of the country's gross domestic product. Unlike other sectors, tourism is not a priority sector for the Government of India.
india.title: Tourism in India

india.text: India's telecommunication network is the second largest in the world by number of telephone users with over 1,337.54 million subscribers as of April 2026.
india.title: Telecommunications in India

india.text: The history of agriculture in India dates back to the Neolithic period. India ranks second worldwide in farm output. As per the Indian Economic Survey 2025-26, agriculture and allied activities accounted for 46.1% of the Indian workforce and contributed 15.2% to the country's nominal GDP.
india.title: Agriculture in India

india.text: Since 2013, the total primary energy consumption in India has been the third greatest in the world after China and the United States.
india.title: Energy in India

india.text: The mining industry in India is a major economic activity which contributes significantly to the economy of India. The gross domestic product contribution of the mining industry varies from 2.2% to 2.5% only but going by the GDP of the total industrial sector, it contributes around 10% to 11%.
india.title: Mining in India

indonesia.text: The politics of Indonesia take place in the framework of a presidential representative democratic republic whereby the President of Indonesia is both head of state and head of government and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government.
indonesia.title: Politics of Indonesia

indonesia.text: Indonesia is a highly diverse country, both ethnically and linguistically. The country's population reached 270.20 million according to the 2020 national census, up from 237.64 million in 2010. As of mid-2025, the official estimate stood at 284.44 million, reflecting an annual growth rate of 1.11%.
indonesia.title: Demographics of Indonesia

indonesia.text: Education in Indonesia falls under the responsibility of the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, and Technology, and the Ministry of Religious Affairs. In Indonesia, all citizens must undertake twelve years of compulsory education.
indonesia.title: Education in Indonesia

indonesia.text: Health in Indonesia is affected by a number of factors. Indonesia has over 26,000 health care facilities; 2,000 hospitals, 9,000 community health centres and private clinics, 1,100 dentist clinics and 1,000 opticians. The country lacks doctors with only 0.4 doctors per 1,000 population.
indonesia.title: Health in Indonesia

picture.credit: Peter Fitzgerald, minor amendments by Joelf

indonesia.text: This is a list of rivers in Indonesia.
indonesia.title: List of rivers of Indonesia

indonesia.text: This is a brief summary of the geology of Indonesia. Indonesia is located between two major tectonic plates namely, the Australian Plate and the newly-separated Sunda Plate.
indonesia.title: Geology of Indonesia

indonesia.text: This is a list of all 270 mountains in or bordering Indonesia which have a topographic prominence of at least 1,000 m along with 115 less prominent peaks which are considered to have significant tourist interest, known as "spesials".
indonesia.title: List of mountains in Indonesia

indonesia.text: The climate of Indonesia is almost entirely tropical.
indonesia.title: Climate of Indonesia

indonesia.text: Since independence, Indonesian foreign relations have adhered to a "free and active" foreign policy, seeking to play a role in regional affairs commensurate with its size and location but avoiding involvement in conflicts among major powers.
indonesia.title: Foreign relations of Indonesia

indonesia.text: The military history of Indonesia includes the military history of the modern nation of Republic of Indonesia, as well as the military history of the states which preceded and formed it. It encompassed a kaleidoscope of conflicts spanning over a millennium.
indonesia.title: Military history of Indonesia

indonesia.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Indonesia. Indonesia is a country in Southeast Asia and Oceania, consisting of 17,508 islands. With a population of nearly 280 million people, it is the world's fourth most populated country.
indonesia.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Indonesia

indonesia.text: Indonesia is a country with many different tribes and ethnic groups, and its music is also highly diverse, coming in hundreds of different forms and styles. Every region has its own distinct culture and art, and as a result traditional music differs from area to area.
indonesia.title: Music of Indonesia

picture.credit: Zul Rosle from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia

indonesia.text: Indonesian cuisine is a collection of regional culinary traditions of the various ethnic groups that form the archipelagic nation of Indonesia.
indonesia.title: Indonesian cuisine

indonesia.text: The following table indicates declared Indonesian government national holidays. Cultural variants also provide opportunity for holidays tied to local events. Beside official holidays, there are the so-called "libur bersama" or "cuti bersama", or joint leave declared nationwide by the government.
indonesia.title: Public holidays in Indonesia

indonesia.text: Several different religions are practised in Indonesia, without an established state religion. The first principle of Indonesia's philosophical foundation, Pancasila, requires its citizens to state the belief in "the one and almighty God", sometimes called a "public religion".
indonesia.title: Religion in Indonesia

indonesia.text: Indonesia is home to over 700 living languages spoken across its extensive archipelago. This significant linguistic variety constitutes approximately 10% of the world’s total languages, positioning Indonesia as the second most linguistically diverse nation globally, following Papua New Guinea.
indonesia.title: Languages of Indonesia

indonesia.text: The cinema of Indonesia refers to films produced domestically in Indonesia.
indonesia.title: Cinema of Indonesia

indonesia.text: Sports in Indonesia are popular from both the participation and spectating aspect.
indonesia.title: Sports in Indonesia

indonesia.text: The architecture of Indonesia reflects the diversity of cultural, historical, and geographic influences that have shaped Indonesia as a whole. Invaders, colonizers, missionaries, merchants, and traders brought cultural changes that had a profound effect on building styles and techniques.
indonesia.title: Architecture of Indonesia

indonesia.text: Indonesian literature is a term grouping various genres of South-East Asian literature. Indonesian literature can refer to literature produced in the Indonesian archipelago.
indonesia.title: Indonesian literature

indonesia.text: Indonesian art takes many forms and is hard to define, as Indonesia is a sprawling archipelago nation of 17,000 islands with a long history that goes back to prehistoric times and is populated by over 600 ethnic groups who speak over 700 languages.
indonesia.title: Indonesian art

indonesia.text: Indonesia's transport system has been shaped over time by the economic resource base of an archipelago with thousands of islands, and the distribution of its more than 200 million people concentrated mainly on a single island, Java.
indonesia.title: Transport in Indonesia

indonesia.text: Tourism in Indonesia is an important component of the Indonesian economy, as well as a significant source of its foreign exchange revenues.
indonesia.title: Tourism in Indonesia

indonesia.text: Communications in Indonesia has a complex history due to the need to reach an extended archipelago of over 17,500 islands. The once important non-electronic communication methods of the past have given way to a considerable telecommunications infrastructure in contemporary Indonesia.
indonesia.title: Communications in Indonesia

indonesia.text: Agriculture in Indonesia is one of the key sectors within the Indonesian economy. In the last 50 years, the sector's share in national gross domestic product has decreased considerably, due to the rise of industrialisation and service sector.
indonesia.title: Agriculture in Indonesia

indonesia.text: In 2019, the total energy production in Indonesia is 450.79 million tonnes of oil equivalent, with a total primary energy supply of 231.14 million tonnes of oil equivalent and electricity final consumption of 263.32 terawatt-hours.
indonesia.title: Energy in Indonesia

iran.text: The politics of Iran takes place in the framework of a unitary Islamic theocracy which was formed following the overthrow of Iran's millennia-long monarchy by the 1979 Revolution.
iran.title: Politics of Iran

iran.text: Iran's population increased dramatically in the late 20th century, reaching about 80 million by 2016. As of 2026, Iran's population is over 87 million. In recent years, however, Iran's birth rate has dropped significantly.
iran.title: Demographics of Iran

iran.text: Education in Iran is centralized and divided into K-12 education plus higher education.
iran.title: Education in Iran

iran.text: As for many developing countries, health issues in Iran stem from a variety of reasons: namely, water and sanitation, diet and fitness, various addictions, mental fitness, communicable diseases, hygiene and the environment.
iran.title: Health in Iran

iran.text: This is a list of the rivers that flow wholly or partly in Iran, arranged geographically by river basin from west to east.
iran.title: List of rivers of Iran

iran.text: The main points that are discussed in the geology of Iran include the study of the geological and structural units or zones; stratigraphy; magmatism and igneous rocks; ophiolite series and ultramafic rocks; and orogenic events in Iran.
iran.title: Geology of Iran

iran.text: The wildlife of Iran include the fauna and flora of Iran. One of the most famous animals of Iran is the critically endangered Asiatic cheetah, which today survives only in Iran. Another notable species is the Iranian ground jay, the only bird endemic to Iran.
iran.title: Wildlife of Iran

iran.text: The highest mountains in Iran include Damavand, Alam-Kuh, Sabalan, Takht-e Soleyman, Azad Kuh, Zard-Kuh, and Shir Kuh. This is a list of mountains in the country of Iran. By clicking on the symbols at the head of the table the individual columns may be sorted.
iran.title: List of mountains in Iran

iran.text: Geography is an important factor in informing Iran's foreign policy. Following the 1979 Iranian Revolution, the newly formed Islamic Republic, under the leadership of Ayatollah Khomeini, dramatically reversed the pro-American foreign policy of the last Shah of Iran Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.
iran.title: Foreign relations of Iran

iran.text: The military history of Iran has been relatively well-documented, with thousands of years' worth of recorded history.
iran.title: Military history of Iran

iran.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Iran.
iran.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Iran

iran.text: The music of Iran encompasses music produced by Iranian artists. In addition to the traditional folk and classical genres, it also includes pop and internationally celebrated styles such as jazz, rock, and hip hop.
iran.title: Music of Iran

iran.text: Iranian cuisine comprises the culinary traditions of Iran.
iran.title: Iranian cuisine

iran.text: Iran uses three official calendar systems, including the Solar Hijri calendar as the main and national calendar, the Gregorian calendar for international events and Christian holidays, and the Lunar Hijri calendar for Islamic holidays.
iran.title: Public holidays in Iran

iran.text: Religion in Iran has been shaped by multiple religions and sects over the course of the country's history. Zoroastrianism was the main followed religion during the Achaemenid Empire, Parthian Empire, and Sasanian Empire.
iran.title: Religion in Iran

iran.text: Iran's ethnic diversity means that the languages of Iran come from a number of linguistic origins, although the primary language spoken and used is Persian.
iran.title: Languages of Iran

iran.text: The cinema of Iran, or of Persia, refers to the film industry in Iran. In particular, Iranian art films have garnered international recognition. Iranian films are usually written and spoken in the Persian language. Iran has been lauded as one of the best exporters of cinema in the 1990s.
iran.title: Cinema of Iran

iran.text: Many sports in Iran are both traditional and modern. Tehran, for example, was the first city in West Asia to host the Asian Games in 1974, and continues to host and participate in major international sporting events.
iran.title: Sport in Iran

iran.text: Iranian architecture or Persian architecture is the architecture of Iran and parts of the rest of West Asia, the Caucasus and Central Asia. Its history dates back to at least 5000 BC with characteristic examples distributed over a vast area from Turkey and Iraq to Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.
iran.title: Iranian architecture

iran.text: Literature in Iran encompasses a variety of literary traditions in the various languages used in Iran. Modern literatures of Iran include Persian literature, Azerbaijani literature, and Kurdish literature, among others.
iran.title: Literature in Iran

iran.text: Persian art or Iranian art has one of the richest art heritages in world history and has been strong in many media including architecture, painting, weaving, pottery, calligraphy, metalworking and sculpture.
iran.title: Persian art

iran.text: Transport in Iran is inexpensive because of the government's subsidization of the price of gasoline. The downside is a huge draw on government coffers, economic inefficiency because of highly wasteful consumption patterns, contraband with neighboring countries and air pollution.
iran.title: Transport in Iran

iran.text: Tourism in Iran is a major sector of the Iranian economy, contributing about 3% to the national GDP in 2023. Over 7 million tourists visited the country in 2024.
iran.title: Tourism in Iran

iran.text: Iran's telecommunications industry is almost entirely state-owned, dominated by the Telecommunication Company of Iran. Iran has a population of 80 million with some 56% of Iranians under the age of 25.
iran.title: Communications in Iran

iran.text: Agriculture in Iran is underdeveloped. While one-third of Iran's total surface area is suitable for farming, due to poor soil and inadequate water distribution, most of it is not cultivated.
iran.title: Agriculture in Iran

iran.text: Energy in Iran is characterized by vast reserves of fossil fuels, positioning the country as a global energy powerhouse.
iran.title: Energy in Iran

picture.credit: These maps and charts are scanned from "Atlas of

iran.text: Mining in Iran is still under development, yet the country is one of the most important mineral producers in the world, ranked among 15 major mineral-rich countries, holding some 68 types of minerals, 37 billion tonnes of proven reserves and more than 57 billion tonnes of potential reserves worth $770 billion in 2014.
iran.title: Mining in Iran

iraq.text: According to the constitution adopted in 2005, the Republic of Iraq is defined as a federal democratic parliamentary republic. Executive power is exercised by the Prime Minister of Iraq who heads the Council of Ministers.
iraq.title: Politics of Iraq

iraq.text: The Iraqi people are people originating from the country of Iraq. Iraqi Arabs are the largest ethnic group in Iraq, followed by Iraqi Kurds, then Iraqi Turkmen as the third largest ethnic group in the country. A minority of indigenous ethnic Assyrians also continue to exist in the country.
iraq.title: Demographics of Iraq

iraq.text: Education in Iraq is administered by the Ministry of Education. UNESCO reports that Iraq previously had one of the best educational performances in the Middle Eastern/West Asian region. In primary school, gross enrollment rate used to be 100%, and literacy levels were high.
iraq.title: Education in Iraq

iraq.text: Health in Iraq refers to the country's public healthcare system and the overall health of the country's population. Iraq belongs to WHO health region Eastern Mediterranean and classified as upper middle according to World Bank income classification 2013.
iraq.title: Health in Iraq

iraq.text: This is a list of rivers of Iraq.
iraq.title: List of rivers of Iraq

iraq.text: The geology of Iraq includes thick sequences of marine and continental sedimentary rocks over poorly understood basement rock, at the junction of the Arabian plate, the Anatolian plate, and the Iranian plate.
iraq.title: Geology of Iraq

iraq.text: The wildlife of Iraq includes its flora and fauna and their natural habitats. Iraq has multiple biomes from mountainous region in the north to the wet marshlands along the Euphrates river. The western part of the country is mainly desert and some semi-arid regions.
iraq.title: Wildlife of Iraq

picture.credit: U.S. Department of State from United States

iraq.text: The foreign relations of Iraq are the international relations maintained by the Republic of Iraq since its independence from Ottoman rule proclaimed in 1921.
iraq.title: Foreign relations of Iraq

iraq.text: The military history of Iraq, due to a rich archaeological record, is one of the longest in written human history.
iraq.title: Military history of Iraq

iraq.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Iraq. It includes special uses under the Ottoman Empire as well as occupation issues.
iraq.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Iraq

iraq.text: The music of Iraq spans numerous genres across many different cultures and ethnic groups, including Mesopotamian Arabic, Assyrian, Kurdish, and Turkmen, among others.
iraq.title: Music of Iraq

iraq.text: Iraqi cuisine is a Middle Eastern cuisine that has its origins in the ancient Near East culture of the Fertile Crescent. Tablets found in ancient ruins in Iraq show recipes prepared in the temples during religious festivals—the first cookbooks in the world.
iraq.title: Iraqi cuisine

iraq.text: This is a list of public holidays in Iraq.
iraq.title: Public holidays in Iraq

iraq.text: Religion in Iraq dates back to Ancient Mesopotamia, particularly Sumer, Akkad, Assyria, and Babylonia between c. 3500 BC and 400 AD. Iraqi society consists of a multi-ethnic and multi-religious population, with Islam having been the dominant faith for centuries.
iraq.title: Religion in Iraq

iraq.text: There are a number of languages spoken in Iraq, but the lingua franca -- Mesopotamian Arabic -- is by far the most widely spoken in the country.
iraq.title: Languages of Iraq

iraq.text: Iraq has one of the most significant and diverse film industries in the Middle East. The Iraqi cinema consists of film production notably in Arabic, Kurdish and Syriac languages.
iraq.title: Cinema of Iraq

iraq.text: There are a wide variety of sports played and followed in Iraq. Football is the most popular sport and hobby in Iraq. Football is a considerable uniting factor, following years of war and unrest.
iraq.title: Sport in Iraq

iraq.text: The architecture of Iraq encompasses the buildings of various architectural styles that exist in Iraq. Iraq is recognized by UNESCO as being the cradle of civilization.
iraq.title: Architecture of Iraq

iraq.text: Iraqi literature or Mesopotamian literature dates back to Sumerian times, which constitutes the earliest known corpus of recorded literature, including the religious writings and other traditional stories maintained by the Sumerian civilization and largely preserved by the later Akkadian and Babylonian empire.
iraq.title: Iraqi literature

iraq.text: Transport in Iraq consists of railways, highways, waterways, pipelines, ports and harbors, marines and airports.
iraq.title: Transport in Iraq

iraq.text: Tourism in Iraq refers to tourism in the Western Asian country of Iraq. Iraq was one of the main destinations for many years, however this changed dramatically due to conflicts. Tourism in Iraq has faced many challenges, however, in recent years there have been improvements.
iraq.title: Tourism in Iraq

iraq.text: Telecommunications in Iraq include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet as well as the postal system.
iraq.title: Telecommunications in Iraq

iraq.text: Energy in Iraq plays a crucial role in both the national economy and the global energy markets due to the country's vast oil reserves and significant status within the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries. Iraq holds abundant oil and gas resources and has strong solar PV potential.
iraq.title: Energy in Iraq

ireland.text: Ireland is a parliamentary, representative democratic republic and a member state of the European Union.
ireland.title: Politics of the Republic of Ireland

ireland.text: The demographics of the Republic of Ireland are characterized by a growing and gradually ageing population, with population growth driven by both natural increase and sustained net immigration, the latter becoming increasingly significant in recent decades.
ireland.title: Demographics of the Republic of Ireland

ireland.text: Education in the Republic of Ireland is a primary, secondary and higher education. In recent years, further education has grown immensely, and Ireland now has one of the highest percentages of higher education completion in the EU, at 55% of working age adults, and 63% of adults aged 25–34.
ireland.title: Education in the Republic of Ireland

ireland.text: Smoking, alcohol consumption and obesity in Ireland occur at rates higher than the OECD average. Life expectancy in the Republic of Ireland was 81.1 years for males at birth and 84.6 for females in 2025, considerably better than in Northern Ireland where the figures were 78.8 and 82.6 years.
ireland.title: Health in the Republic of Ireland

ireland.text: This is an alphabetical list of the main rivers on the island of Ireland. It includes rivers that flow through the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland. Rivers that flow through Northern Ireland are marked with an asterisk.
ireland.title: List of rivers of Ireland

ireland.text: The geology of Ireland consists of the study of the rock formations on the island of Ireland. It includes rocks from every age from Proterozoic to Holocene and a large variety of different rock types is represented.
ireland.title: Geology of Ireland

ireland.text: In these lists of mountains in Ireland, those within Northern Ireland, or on the Republic of Ireland – United Kingdom border, are marked with an asterisk, while the rest are within the Republic of Ireland.
ireland.title: Lists of mountains in Ireland

ireland.text: The climate of Ireland is mild, humid, and changeable, with abundant rainfall and a lack of temperature extremes. Ireland's climate is defined as a temperate oceanic climate, or Cfb on the Köppen climate classification system, a classification it shares with most of northwest Europe.
ireland.title: Climate of Ireland

ireland.text: The foreign relations of Ireland are substantially influenced by its membership of the European Union, although bilateral relations with the United States and United Kingdom are also important.
ireland.title: Foreign relations of Ireland

ireland.text: The military history of Ireland comprises thousands of years of armed actions in the territory encompassing the island of Ireland. Ireland was never invaded by the Roman Empire, and the island remained a warring collection of separate kingdoms throughout its early history.
ireland.title: Military history of Ireland

ireland.text: Irish music is music that has been created in various genres on the island of Ireland. The indigenous music of the island is termed Irish traditional music. It has remained vibrant through the 20th and into the 21st century, despite globalising cultural forces.
ireland.title: Music of Ireland

picture.credit: A Healthier Michigan from Detroit, United States

ireland.text: Irish cuisine encompasses the cooking styles, traditions and recipes associated with the island of Ireland. It has developed from antiquity through centuries of social and political change and the mixing of different cultures, predominantly with those from nearby Britain and other European regions.
ireland.title: Irish cuisine

ireland.text: Public holidays in Ireland are established in statute law, and there are ten public holidays observed each year. Public holidays in Ireland may commemorate a special day or other event, such as Saint Patrick's Day or Christmas Day. On public holidays, most businesses and schools close.
ireland.title: Public holidays in Ireland

ireland.text: The predominant religion in the Republic of Ireland is Christianity, with the largest denomination being the Catholic Church. The Constitution of Ireland says that the state may not endorse any particular religion and guarantees freedom of religion.
ireland.title: Religion in the Republic of Ireland

ireland.text: There are a number of languages used in Ireland, where Irish and English serve as the two official languages, though the diversity of spoken languages is expanding due to increasing immigration. Since the late 18th century, English has been the predominant first language, displacing Irish.
ireland.title: Languages of Ireland

ireland.text: The Irish film industry has grown somewhat from the late 20th century, due partly to the promotion of the sector by Fís Éireann/Screen Ireland and the introduction of heavy tax breaks.
ireland.title: Cinema of Ireland

ireland.text: Sport plays an important role in Irish society. The many sports played and followed in Ireland include Gaelic games, association football, horse racing, show jumping, greyhound racing, basketball, fishing, motorsport, boxing, tennis, hockey, golf, rowing, cricket, and rugby union.
ireland.title: Sport in Ireland

ireland.text: The architecture of Ireland is one of the most visible features in the Irish countryside – with remains from all eras since the Stone Age abounding. Ireland is famous for its ruined and intact Norman and Anglo-Irish castles, small whitewashed thatched cottages and Georgian urban buildings.
ireland.title: Architecture of Ireland

ireland.text: Irish literature is literature written in the Irish, Latin, English and Scots languages on the island of Ireland.
ireland.title: Irish literature

ireland.text: Irish art is art produced in the island of Ireland, and by artists from Ireland. The term normally includes Irish-born artists as well as expatriates settled in Ireland.
ireland.title: Irish art

ireland.text: Most of the transport system in Ireland is in public hands, either side of the Irish border. The Irish road network has evolved separately in the two jurisdictions into which Ireland is divided, while the Irish rail network was mostly created prior to the partition of Ireland.
ireland.title: Transport in Ireland

ireland.text: Tourism in the Republic of Ireland is one of the biggest contributors to the economy of Ireland, with 9.0 million people visiting the country in 2017, about 1.8 times Ireland's population.
ireland.title: Tourism in the Republic of Ireland

ireland.text: Telecommunications in Ireland operate in a regulated competitive market that provides customers with a wide array of advanced digital services.
ireland.title: Telecommunications in the Republic of Ireland

ireland.text: Agriculture in Ireland began during the neolithic era, when inhabitants of the island began to practice animal husbandry and farming grains. Principal crops grown during the neolithic era included barley and wheat.
ireland.title: Agriculture in Ireland

ireland.text: Ireland is a net energy importer and remains highly dependent on fossil fuels.
ireland.title: Energy in Ireland

isle-of-man.text: The government of the Isle of Man is a parliamentary representative democracy. The Monarch of the United Kingdom is also the head of state of the Isle of Man, and generally referred to as "The King, Lord of Mann".
isle-of-man.title: Politics of the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: Demographic features of the population of the Isle of Man include population density, ethnicity, level of education, health, economic status, and religious affiliations.
isle-of-man.title: Demographics of the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: Education in the Isle of Man is compulsory for children aged between 5 and 16.
isle-of-man.title: Education in the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: Life expectancy on the Isle of Man at birth was estimated at 81.3 years in 2017, 79.6 years for men and 83.2 years for women. The Infant mortality rate was 4 deaths per 1,000 live births. The birth rate in 2016 reached a 30-year low.
isle-of-man.title: Health in the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: This is a list of rivers of the Isle of Man. It is organised geographically, taken anti-clockwise, from Douglas. Tributaries are listed down the page in an upstream direction.
isle-of-man.title: List of rivers of the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: The geology of the Isle of Man consists primarily of a thick pile of sedimentary rocks dating from the Ordovician period, together with smaller areas of later sedimentary and extrusive igneous strata.
isle-of-man.title: Geology of the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: This is a list of the known wildlife of the Isle of Man. Each listing follows the following format: English name, binomial/trinomial scientific name with authorities for uncommon species, Manx name, status.
isle-of-man.title: Wildlife of the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: The Isle of Man is not part of the United Kingdom, but to a large extent its relations with other countries are handled by the United Kingdom.
isle-of-man.title: External relations of the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of the Isle of Man. The Isle of Man is a self-governing British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea between the islands of Great Britain and Ireland. The island is about 32 miles long and, at its widest, 14 miles wide.
isle-of-man.title: Postage stamps and postal history of the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: The music of the Isle of Man reflects Celtic, Norse and other influences, including those from its neighbours, Scotland, Ireland, England and Wales. The Isle of Man is a small island nation in the Irish Sea, between Great Britain and Ireland.
isle-of-man.title: Music of the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: This is a list of regular public holidays on the Isle of Man. For holidays that fall on a Saturday or Sunday a substitute holiday will be observed the next day that itself is not a holiday.
isle-of-man.title: Public holidays in the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: The main language of the Isle of Man is English, predominantly the Manx English dialect. Manx, the historical language of the island, is still maintained by a small speaker population. Both English and Manx are official languages in Tynwald.
isle-of-man.title: Languages of the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: For a small country, sport in the Isle of Man plays an important part in making the island known to the wider world. The principal international sporting event held on the island is the annual Isle of Man TT motorcycling event.
isle-of-man.title: Sport in the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: Literature in the Manx language is known from the 16th century. Early works were often religious in theme, including translations of the Book of Common Prayer, the Bible and Milton's Paradise Lost.
isle-of-man.title: Manx literature

isle-of-man.text: There are a number of transport services around the Isle of Man, mostly consisting of paved roads, public transport, rail services, sea ports and an airport.
isle-of-man.title: Transport in the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: The tourism industry of the Isle of Man has been an important element in the economy for over a century.
isle-of-man.title: Tourism in the Isle of Man

isle-of-man.text: The Isle of Man has an extensive communications infrastructure consisting of telephone cables, submarine cables, and an array of television and mobile phone transmitters and towers.
isle-of-man.title: Communications in the Isle of Man

israel.text: Politics in Israel are based on parliamentary democracy. The Prime Minister of Israel is the head of government and leader of a multi-party system. Politics in Israel is dominated by Zionist parties.
israel.title: Politics of Israel

israel.text: The demographics of Israel, monitored by the Israel Central Bureau of Statistics, encompass various attributes that define the nation's populace. Since its establishment in 1948, Israel has witnessed significant changes in its demographics.
israel.title: Demographics of Israel

israel.text: Education in Israel encompasses compulsory education, which spans from kindergarten through 12th grade, and higher education, which is characterized by a public university system and significant government subsidies.
israel.title: Education in Israel

israel.text: Health in Israel is advanced and efficient, compared to other developed counties, where Israel spends a relatively low proportion of their gross domestic product on health, which is 7.3%, compared to 9.3% in the OECD and 18% in the US.
israel.title: Health in Israel

israel.text: This is a list of rivers of Israel. This list is arranged by drainage basin, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name. Nahal and Wadi commonly translate to Stream, more seldom River. Both words, when used as common nouns, also signify ' valley'.
israel.title: List of rivers of Israel

israel.text: The geology of Israel includes igneous and metamorphic crystalline basement rocks from the Precambrian overlain by a lengthy sequence of sedimentary rocks extending up to the Pleistocene and overlain with alluvium, sand dunes and playa deposits.
israel.title: Geology of Israel

israel.text: The wildlife of Israel includes the flora and fauna of Israel, which is extremely diverse due to the country's location between the temperate and the tropical zones, bordering the Mediterranean Sea in the west and the desert in the east.
israel.title: Wildlife of Israel

israel.text: Foreign relations of Israel refers to diplomatic and trade relations between Israel and other countries around the world. Israel has diplomatic ties with 165 of the other 192 UN member states as of 12 December 2020.
israel.title: Foreign relations of Israel

israel.text: The history of the Israel Defense Forces intertwines in its early stages with history of the Haganah.
israel.title: History of the Israel Defense Forces

israel.text: The postage stamps and postal history of Israel is a survey of the postage stamps issued by the state of Israel, and its postal history, since independence was proclaimed on May 14, 1948. The first postage stamps were issued two days later on May 16, 1948.
israel.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Israel

israel.text: The music of Israel incorporates a variety of musical traditions. Since the First Aliyah of Jews to Palestine in the 1880s, local musical styles have developed alongside the adoption of international genres.
israel.title: Music of Israel

israel.text: Israeli cuisine primarily comprises dishes brought from the Jewish diaspora, and has more recently been defined by the development of a notable fusion cuisine characterized by the mixing of Jewish cuisine and Arab cuisine.
israel.title: Israeli cuisine

israel.text: For exact dates in the Gregorian calendar see Jewish and Israeli holidays 2000–2050. Public holidays in Israel are national holidays officially recognized by the Knesset, Israel's parliament.
israel.title: Public holidays in Israel

israel.text: Religion in Israel is manifested primarily in Judaism, the ethnic religion of the Jewish people. The State of Israel declares itself as a "Jewish and democratic state" and is the only country with a Jewish-majority population.
israel.title: Religion in Israel

israel.text: The Israeli population is linguistically and culturally diverse. Hebrew is the country's official language, and almost the entire population speaks it either as a first language or proficiently as a second language. Its standard form, known as Modern Hebrew, is the main medium of life in Israel.
israel.title: Languages of Israel

picture.credit: אלכס גל - IDF Spokesperson's Unit photographer

israel.text: Cinema of Israel comprises the film industry and its film productions, whether made within the State of Israel or by Israeli film production companies abroad. Most Israeli films are produced in Hebrew, but there are productions in other languages such as Arabic and English.
israel.title: Cinema of Israel

israel.text: Sport in Israel plays an important role in Israeli culture and is supported by the Ministry of Culture and Sport.
israel.title: Sport in Israel

israel.text: The architecture of Israel has been influenced by the different architectural styles of those who have inhabited the country over time, sometimes modified to suit the local climate and landscape.
israel.title: Architecture of Israel

israel.text: Israeli literature is literature written by Israelis. Most works classed as Israeli literature are written in the Hebrew language, although some Israeli authors write in Yiddish, English, Arabic and Russian.
israel.title: Israeli literature

israel.text: Visual arts in Israel or Israeli art refers to visual or plastic arts created by Israeli artists or Jewish painters in the Yishuv.
israel.title: Visual arts in Israel

israel.text: Transportation in Israel primarily consists of nationwide rail transport, bus services, cycling as well as private vehicles.
israel.title: Transport in Israel

israel.text: Tourism is a major economic sector and a significant source of income in Israel. Common tourist attractions include religious sites, beach resorts, natural sites, archaeological tourism, heritage tourism, adventure tourism, and ecotourism.
israel.title: Tourism in Israel

israel.text: Telecommunications in Israel are the most developed in the Middle East. Israel's system consists of coaxial cables, optical fibers, and microwave radio relay. Prior to the 1990s, Israel's telecommunication market was dominated by Bezeq, a government-owned corporation.
israel.title: Telecommunications in Israel

israel.text: Agriculture in Israel is a highly developed industry. Israel is an exporter of fresh produce and a leader in agricultural technologies. The southern half of Israel is desert and irrigation is required for growing crops. The northern half is more conducive to rain-fed agriculture.
israel.title: Agriculture in Israel

israel.text: Most energy in Israel comes from fossil fuels. The country's total primary energy demand is significantly higher than its total primary energy production, relying heavily on imports to meet its energy needs.
israel.title: Energy in Israel

italy.text: The politics of Italy are conducted through a parliamentary republic with a multi-party system.
italy.title: Politics of Italy

italy.text: The demography of Italy is monitored by the Italian National Institute of Statistics. At the beginning of 2024, Italy had an estimated population of 58.9 million. Its population density, at 195.7 inhabitants per square kilometre, is higher than both the EU and European average.
italy.title: Demographics of Italy

italy.text: Education in Italy is compulsory from 6 to 16 years of age, and is divided into five stages: kindergarten, primary school, lower secondary school, upper secondary school, and university.
italy.title: Education in Italy

italy.text: Italy is known for its generally very good health system, and the life expectancy is 80 for males and 85 for females, placing the country 5th in the world for life expectancy, and low infant mortality.
italy.title: Health in Italy

italy.text: This is a list of rivers which are at least partially located in Italy. They are organized according to the body of water they drain into, with the exceptions of Sicily and Sardinia, which are listed separately. At the bottom, all of the rivers are also listed alphabetically.
italy.title: List of rivers of Italy

italy.text: The geology of Italy includes mountain ranges such as the Alps and the Apennines formed from the uplift of igneous and primarily marine sedimentary rocks all formed since the Paleozoic.
italy.title: Geology of Italy

italy.text: This article contains a sortable table listing mountains of Italy. All mountain heights and prominences on the list are from the largest-scale maps available. In the list, only the exact location of the culminating point of the mountain is considered.
italy.title: List of mountains in Italy

italy.text: The climate of Italy is highly diverse. In most of the inland northern and central regions, the climate ranges from humid subtropical to humid continental and oceanic. The climate of the Po Valley geographical region is mostly humid subtropical, with cool winters and hot summers.
italy.title: Climate of Italy

italy.text: The foreign relations of the Italian Republic are the Italian government's external relations with the outside world. Located in Europe, Italy has been considered a major European power since its unification in 1860.
italy.title: Foreign relations of Italy

italy.text: This is an introduction to the postal and philatelic history of Italy. As Italy was not unified until 1861, its early postal history is tied to the various kingdoms and smaller realms that ruled in the peninsula.
italy.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Italy

picture.credit: Pirlouiiiit Pirlouiiiit, squared by Juan Pablo A

italy.text: In Italy, music has traditionally been one of the cultural markers of Italian national cultures and ethnic identity and holds an important position in society and in politics.
italy.title: Music of Italy

picture.credit: Various: ElfQrin (Valerio Capello) for File:Eq i

italy.text: Italian cuisine is a Mediterranean cuisine consisting of the ingredients, recipes and cooking techniques developed in Italy since Roman times, and later spread around the world together with waves of Italian diaspora.
italy.title: Italian cuisine

italy.text: Public holidays in Italy are established by the Italian parliament and, with the exception of city or community patronal days, apply nationwide. These include a mix of national, religious and local observances. In Italy, there are also State commemoration days, which are not public holidays.
italy.title: Public holidays in Italy

italy.text: Religion in Italy has been historically characterised by the dominance of the Catholic Church, the largest branch of Christianity, since the East–West Schism.
italy.title: Religion in Italy

picture.credit: Susana Freixeirominor changes by Xane Zeggi

italy.text: Italy is one of the most linguistically diverse areas in Europe. About 45.9% of the Italian population speak primarily Italian at home, while another 32.2% speak a local language alongside Italian.
italy.title: Languages of Italy

italy.text: The cinema of Italy comprises the films made within Italy or by Italian directors. Since its beginning, Italian cinema has influenced film movements worldwide.
italy.title: Cinema of Italy

italy.text: Sport in Italy has a long tradition. In several sports, both individual and team, Italy has good representation and many successes. The most popular sport in Italy is football.
italy.title: Sport in Italy

italy.text: Italy has a broad and diverse architectural style, which cannot be classified by period or region, due to Italy's division into various small states until 1861. This has created a diverse and eclectic range in architectural designs.
italy.title: Italian architecture

italy.text: Italian literature is written in the Italian language, particularly within Italy. It may also refer to literature written by Italians or in other languages spoken in Italy, often languages that are closely related to modern Italian, including regional varieties and vernacular dialects.
italy.title: Italian literature

italy.text: Since ancient times, the Italian peninsula has been home to diverse civilizations: the Greeks in the south, the Etruscans in the centre, and the Celts in the north. The numerous Rock Drawings in Valcamonica date back as far as 8,000 BC.
italy.title: Italian art

italy.text: Italy has a well developed transport infrastructure. The Italian rail network is extensive (16,723 km), especially in the north, and it includes a high-speed rail network that joins the major cities of Italy from Naples through northern cities such as Milan and Turin.
italy.title: Transport in Italy

italy.text: Tourism in Italy is one of the largest economic sectors of the country. With 88 million international tourists in 2025, Italy is the most visited country in international tourism arrivals.
italy.title: Tourism in Italy

italy.text: The most important telecommunications in Italy are telephone, radio, television and the Internet.
italy.title: Telecommunications in Italy

italy.text: Agriculture in Italy, one of the economic sectors of the country, has developed since the 5th millennium BC. In the 19th century, Italy transformed from a predominantly agricultural country to an industrial country.
italy.title: Agriculture in Italy

italy.text: Energy in Italy comes mostly from fossil fuels. Among the most used resources are petroleum, natural gas, coal and renewables. Italy has few energy resources, and most supplies are imported. An important share of its electricity is imported, mainly from Switzerland and France.
italy.title: Energy in Italy

ivory-coast.text: The politics of Ivory Coast takes place in a framework of a presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the President of Ivory Coast is both head of state and head of government, and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the President and the Government.
ivory-coast.title: Politics of Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Demographic features of the population of Ivory Coast include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
ivory-coast.title: Demographics of Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Education in Ivory Coast continues to face many challenges. Among sub-Saharan African countries, Ivory Coast has one of the highest literacy rates. According to The World Factbook - Central Intelligence Agency as of 2019, 89.9% of the population aged 15 and over were respectively literate.
ivory-coast.title: Education in Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Ivory Coast faces multiple health challenges, caused by factors including malaria, lack of access to medicine, and healthcare staffing shortages.
ivory-coast.title: Health in Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Four major river systems follow meandering courses from north to south, draining into the Gulf of Guinea. From west to east these are the Cavally, Sassandra, Bandama, and Comoé—all relatively untamed rivers navigable only short distances inland from the coast.
ivory-coast.title: List of rivers of Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: The geology of Ivory Coast is almost entirely extremely ancient metamorphic and igneous crystalline basement rock between 2.1 and more than 3.5 billion years old, comprising part of the stable continental crust of the West African Craton.
ivory-coast.title: Geology of Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: The wildlife of Ivory Coast consists of the flora and fauna of this nation in West Africa. The country has a long Atlantic coastline on the Gulf of Guinea and a range of habitat types.
ivory-coast.title: Wildlife of Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Throughout the Cold War, Ivory Coast's foreign policy was generally favorable toward the West. In particular, Félix Houphouët-Boigny kept relations with France that was among the closest between any African country and a former colonial power.
ivory-coast.title: Foreign relations of Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Côte d'Ivoire, or the Ivory Coast, is a country in West Africa established as a French colony in 1893, and becoming independent in 1960.
ivory-coast.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: The music of Ivory Coast includes music genres of many ethnic communities, often characterised by vocal polyphony especially among the Baoulé, talking drums especially among the Nzema people and by the characteristic polyrhythms found in rhythm in Sub-Saharan Africa.
ivory-coast.title: Music of Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Ivorian cuisine is the traditional cuisine of Côte d'Ivoire, and is based on tubers, grains, pig, chicken, seafood, fish, fresh fruits, vegetables and spices. It is very similar to that of neighboring countries in West Africa. Common staple foods include grains and tubers.
ivory-coast.title: Ivorian cuisine

ivory-coast.text: This is a list of public holidays in Ivory Coast.
ivory-coast.title: Public holidays in Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Religion in Ivory Coast is diverse, with no particular religion representing the majority of the population. According to the 2021 census, Islam is professed by 42.5% of the total population, while adherents of Christianity represented 39.8% of the population.
ivory-coast.title: Religion in Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Ivory Coast is a multilingual country with an estimated 69 languages currently spoken. The official language is French. This language is taught in schools and serves as a lingua franca in the country, along with Dioula.
ivory-coast.title: Languages of Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Ivory Coast invested remarkably in its transport system. Transport Infrastructures are much more developed than they are other West African countries despite a crisis that restrained their maintenance and development.
ivory-coast.title: Transport in Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: The Ivory Coast's tourism industry has developed significantly since the early 1970s. The country had 11,374 beds in 7,786 hotel rooms and a 70% occupancy rate in 1997. In 1998, there were 301,039 arriving tourists, including more than 73,000 from Germany, France, and United Kingdom.
ivory-coast.title: Tourism in Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Telecommunications in Ivory Coast include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
ivory-coast.title: Telecommunications in Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Agriculture was the foundation of the economy in Ivory Coast and its main source of growth.
ivory-coast.title: Agriculture in Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: Energy in Ivory Coast concerns the production and export of energy and electricity in the Ivory Coast. The country has a capacity of 2,200 megawatts energy production.
ivory-coast.title: Energy in Ivory Coast

ivory-coast.text: The mining sector of Ivory Coast contributes to 13% of the country's exports annually and accounts for 5% of the GDP. The industry has historically centered on the extraction of gold.
ivory-coast.title: Mining industry of Ivory Coast

jamaica.text: Politics in Jamaica takes place in the framework of a representative parliamentary democratic constitutional monarchy. The 1962 Constitution of Jamaica established a parliamentary system whose political and legal traditions closely follow those of the United Kingdom.
jamaica.title: Politics of Jamaica

jamaica.text: Jamaica is an island country in the Caribbean. The country had a population of 2,834,683 as of August 2026, having the fourth largest population in the region.It is #142 in global population among nations. Jamaica's annual population growth rate stood at 0.08% in 2022.
jamaica.title: Demographics of Jamaica

jamaica.text: Education in Jamaica is primarily modeled on the British education system. The Human Rights Measurement Initiative finds that Jamaica is fulfilling only 70.0% of what it should be fulfilling for the right to education based on the country's level of income.
jamaica.title: Education in Jamaica

jamaica.text: Jamaica’s health care has had a weak history, however has been improving and continuing to improve. Part of this is from the fact that close to half of the healthcare workers from the area are leaving for the better opportunities that are offered elsewhere.
jamaica.title: Health in Jamaica

jamaica.text: This is a list of rivers of Jamaica, arranged from west to east, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
jamaica.title: List of rivers of Jamaica

jamaica.text: The Geology of Jamaica is formed of rocks of Cretaceous to Neogene age. The basement consists of Cretaceous island arc and back-arc basin sequences that formed above a subduction zone.
jamaica.title: Geology of Jamaica

jamaica.text: Jamaica has diplomatic relations with many nations and is a member of the United Nations and the Organization of American States. Jamaica chairs the Working Group on smaller Economies. Jamaica is an active member of the Commonwealth of Nations and the Non-Aligned Movement.
jamaica.title: Foreign relations of Jamaica

jamaica.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Jamaica.
jamaica.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Jamaica

jamaica.text: The music of Jamaica includes Jamaican folk music and many popular genres, such as mento, ska, rocksteady, reggae, dub music, dancehall, reggae fusion and related styles. Reggae is especially popular through the fame of Bob Marley.
jamaica.title: Music of Jamaica

jamaica.text: Jamaican cuisine includes a mixture of cooking techniques, flavours and spices influenced by Amerindian, West African, Irish, English, French, Portuguese, Spanish, Indian, Chinese and Middle Eastern people who have inhabited the island.
jamaica.title: Jamaican cuisine

jamaica.text: The following is a list of Public holidays in Jamaica, which includes Christian holidays and secular holidays.
jamaica.title: Public holidays in Jamaica

jamaica.text: Christianity is the predominant religion in Jamaica. Jamaica's laws establish freedom of religion and prohibit religious discrimination. According to the census of 2011, 69% of the population were Christians of various denominations, while 21% stated they had no religion.
jamaica.title: Religion in Jamaica

jamaica.text: Despite Jamaica never having a very strong film industry, the island has produced notable films from the 1970s onwards. The most critically acclaimed film is The Harder They Come, by Perry Henzell, which received international acclaim.
jamaica.title: Cinema of Jamaica

jamaica.text: Athletics became the number one sport in Jamaica. The most popular sports in Jamaica are mostly imported from Britain. The most popular sports are athletics, cricket and association football; other popular sports include basketball, tennis and netball.
jamaica.title: Sport in Jamaica

jamaica.text: Jamaican literature is internationally renowned, with the island of Jamaica being the home or birthplace of many important authors. One of the most distinctive aspects of Jamaican literature is its use of the local dialect — a variation of English, the country's official language.
jamaica.title: Jamaican literature

jamaica.text: Jamaican art dates back to Jamaica's indigenous Taino Indians who created zemis, carvings of their gods, for ritual spiritual purposes.
jamaica.title: Jamaican art

jamaica.text: Transport in Jamaica consists of roadways, railways, ship and air transport, with roadways forming the backbone of the island's internal transport system.
jamaica.title: Transport in Jamaica

jamaica.text: Telecommunications in Jamaica include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephony, and Internet services. The sector is regulated by the Office of Utilities Regulation and the Spectrum Management Authority under the Ministry of Science, Energy and Technology.
jamaica.title: Telecommunications in Jamaica

japan.text: In Japan, politics are conducted in a framework of a dominant-party bicameral parliamentary representative democratic constitutional monarchy.
japan.title: Politics of Japan

japan.text: The demography of Japan is monitored by the National Institute of Population and Social Security Research and Statistics Bureau. In April 2025, Japan's population was roughly 123.4 million people, and peaked at 128.5 million people in 2010.
japan.title: Demographics of Japan

japan.text: Education in Japan is managed by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology of Japan. Education is compulsory at the elementary and lower secondary levels, for a total of nine years.
japan.title: Education in Japan

japan.text: The level of health in Japan is due to a number of factors including cultural habits, isolation, and a universal health care system.
japan.title: Health in Japan

japan.text: Rivers of Japan are characterized by their relatively short lengths and considerably steep gradients due to the narrow and mountainous topography of the country.
japan.title: List of rivers of Japan

picture.credit: Oghmoir Satellite picture from NASA, in public d

japan.text: The islands of Japan are primarily the result of several large ocean movements occurring over hundreds of millions of years from the mid-Silurian to the Pleistocene, as a result of the subduction of the Philippine Sea Plate beneath the continental Eurasian plate to the south, and subduction of the Pacific Plate under the North American Plate to the north.
japan.title: Geology of Japan

japan.text: The wildlife of Japan includes its flora, fauna, and natural habitats. The islands of Japan stretch a long distance from north to south and cover a wide range of climatic zones. This results in a high diversity of wildlife despite Japan's isolation from the mainland of Asia.
japan.title: Wildlife of Japan

japan.text: The following is a list of the mountains and hills of Japan, ordered by height.
japan.title: List of mountains and hills of Japan by height

japan.text: Most regions of Japan, such as Honshu, Shikoku, and Kyushu, belong to the temperate zone with humid subtropical climate characterized by four distinct seasons.
japan.title: Climate of Japan

japan.text: The foreign relations of Japan are handled by Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Japan maintains diplomatic relations with every United Nations member nations except for North Korea, in addition to UN observer states Holy See, as well as Kosovo, Cook Islands, and Niue.
japan.title: Foreign relations of Japan

japan.text: The recorded military history of Japan began in 2nd century during the Yayoi period. The Yamato tribal alliance fought amongst the Three Kingdoms of Korea, in the 5th century against Goguryeo and Silla and in 663 against Silla and Tang dynasty forces.
japan.title: Military history of Japan

japan.text: The story of Japan's postal system with its postage stamps and related postal history goes back over a century. The country's first modern postal service got started in 1871, with mail professionally travelling between Kyoto and Tokyo as well as the latter city and Osaka.
japan.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Japan

japan.text: In Japan, music includes a wide array of distinct genres, both traditional and modern. The word for "music" in Japanese is 音楽, combining the kanji 音 on with the kanji 楽 gaku.
japan.title: Music of Japan

picture.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Sixgimic as

japan.text: Japanese cuisine encompasses the regional and traditional foods of Japan, which have developed through centuries of political, economic, and social changes. The traditional cuisine of Japan is based on rice with miso soup and other dishes with an emphasis on seasonal ingredients.
japan.title: Japanese cuisine

japan.text: Public holidays in Japan were first established by the Public Holiday Law of 1948. It has since been amended 11 times to add additional holidays, the latest being in 2018, for a total of 16 recognized holidays.
japan.title: Public holidays in Japan

japan.text: Shinto and Buddhism, being practiced simultaneously, are two main religions in Japan. Syncretic combinations of both, known generally as shinbutsu-shūgō, are common; they represented Japan's dominant religion before the rise of State Shinto in the 19th century.
japan.title: Religion in Japan
