moldova.text: With few natural energy resources, Moldova imports almost all of its energy supplies.
moldova.title: Energy in Moldova

monaco.text: The politics of Monaco take place within the framework of a semi-constitutional monarchy, with the Prince of Monaco as head of state, with some powers devolved to several advisory and legislative bodies.
monaco.title: Politics of Monaco

monaco.text: This is a demography of the population of Monaco, including population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
monaco.title: Demographics of Monaco

monaco.text: Monaco has the third highest proportion of doctors for its population in Europe: 581 per 100,000 in 2015. Infant mortality rate: 1.7 deaths/1,000 live births Life expectancy at birth: total population: 89.8 years male: 86 years female: 93.7 years
monaco.title: Health in Monaco

monaco.text: The geology of Monaco is closely related to the end of the Western Alps, forming the small country's steep corniche coastline. During the last 2.5 million years of the Quaternary high sea levels between glaciations formed erosion terraces and left behind coastal sediment deposits.
monaco.title: Geology of Monaco

monaco.text: The Principality of Monaco is a sovereign and independent state, linked closely to France by the Treaty of July 1918, which was formally noted in Article 436 of the Treaty of Versailles of 1919.
monaco.title: Foreign relations of Monaco

monaco.text: The postal history of Monaco can be traced to the principality's first postmark in 1704.
monaco.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Monaco

monaco.text: Monaco is a sovereign city-state, country, and microstate on the French Riviera, along the Mediterranean coast. The country has long been under the control of the Grimaldi family, who have encouraged musical development.
monaco.title: Music of Monaco

monaco.text: Monégasque cuisine is the cuisine of the principality of Monaco. It is a Mediterranean cuisine shaped by the cooking style of Provence and the influences of nearby northern Italian and southern French cooking, in addition to Monaco's own culinary traditions.
monaco.title: Monégasque cuisine

monaco.text: This is a list of public holidays in Monaco.
monaco.title: Public holidays in Monaco

monaco.text: The official language of Monaco is French. Monégasque, a variety of Ligurian, is the national language of the Monégasque people. However, it is the primary language of very few people. There are several other languages spoken in addition to French and Monégasque, including Italian and English.
monaco.title: Languages of Monaco

monaco.text: Sport in Monaco form a significant role in the culture of Monaco. The biggest professional sports are association football, motorsports, basketball, and track and field. Other sports are also participated in by athletes and teams.
monaco.title: Sport in Monaco

monaco.text: Monaco is known for its wide range of architecture for a small country. The geography of Monaco, which consists of sharp hills and narrow coastline, influences the Monagasque architecture. The narrow roads have led to architectural construction being built into the hills in limited amounts of space.
monaco.title: Architecture of Monaco

monaco.text: Transport in Monaco is facilitated with road, air, rail, and water networks. Rail transport is operated by SNCF with only Monaco Monte Carlo station seeing passenger service and the total length of the line inside the Principality is 1.7 km.
monaco.title: Transport in Monaco

monaco.text: Energy in Monaco describes energy production, consumption and importation in the Principality of Monaco. Monaco has no domestic sources of fossil fuels and relies entirely on imports of electricity, gas and fuels from France.
monaco.title: Energy in Monaco

mongolia.text: The politics of Mongolia takes place in a framework of a parliamentary system with a multi-party representative democracy. Mongolia is described as a semi-presidential system. The government is headed by the Prime Minister of Mongolia, who is appointed by and accountable to the State Great Khural.
mongolia.title: Politics of Mongolia

mongolia.text: This article on the demographics of Mongolia include population density, ethnicity, religious affiliations, and other aspects of the population. All data are from the National Statistics Office of Mongolia, unless otherwise mentioned. The population at 2020 was around 3.3 million.
mongolia.title: Demographics of Mongolia

mongolia.text: Mongolia's education system has undergone colossal changes in the 20th century. The education reforms during communist times were a stark break with traditional education that was often religious and esoteric.
mongolia.title: Education in Mongolia

mongolia.text: Modern Mongolia inherited a relatively good healthcare system from its socialist period.
mongolia.title: Health in Mongolia

mongolia.text: This is a list of notable rivers of Mongolia, arranged geographically by river basin. The Mongolian words for river are gol and mörön, with the latter usually used for larger rivers.
mongolia.title: List of rivers of Mongolia

mongolia.text: The geology of Mongolia is made up a complicated array of microcontinents and island chains accreted together over the past half billion years, producing varied terrain and tectonics.
mongolia.title: Geology of Mongolia

mongolia.text: The wildlife of Mongolia consists of flora, fauna and funga found in the harsh habitats dictated by the diverse climatic conditions found throughout the country. In the north, there are salty marshes and fresh-water sources. The centre has desert steppes.
mongolia.title: Wildlife of Mongolia

mongolia.text: Mongolia has three major mountain ranges. The highest is the Altai Mountains, which stretch across the western and the southwestern regions of the country on a northwest to southeast axis.
mongolia.title: List of mountains in Mongolia

mongolia.text: Mongolia has diplomatic relations with all 192 UN states, the Holy See, the State of Palestine and the European Union. Its geopolitical position is defined by its geographical location, situated between Russia and China, relying on trade with both sides.
mongolia.title: Foreign relations of Mongolia

mongolia.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Mongolia. Mongolia is a landlocked country in East and Central Asia. It is bordered by Russia to the north and the People's Republic of China to the south, east and west. Ulaanbaatar is the capital and largest city.
mongolia.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Mongolia

picture.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Eric Pouhie

mongolia.text: Music is an integral part of Mongolian culture. Among the unique contributions of Mongolia to the world's musical culture are the long songs, overtone singing, and morin khuur, the horse-headed fiddle, and the pentatonic scale.
mongolia.title: Music of Mongolia

mongolia.text: Mongolian cuisine predominantly consists of dairy products, meat, and animal fats. The most common rural dish is cooked mutton. In the city, steamed dumplings filled with meat—"buuz"— are popular.
mongolia.title: Mongolian cuisine

mongolia.text: The following are the public holidays in Mongolia and other special days.
mongolia.title: Public holidays in Mongolia

mongolia.text: Religion in Mongolia has been traditionally dominated by the schools of Mongolian Buddhism and by Mongolian shamanism, the ethnic religion of the Mongols.
mongolia.title: Religion in Mongolia

mongolia.text: The cinema of Mongolia has been strongly influenced by the cinema of Russia, which differentiates it from cinematic developments in the rest of Asia.
mongolia.title: Cinema of Mongolia

mongolia.text: The architecture of Mongolia is largely based on traditional dwellings, such as the yurt and the tent. During the 16th and 17th centuries, lamaseries were built throughout the country as temples which were later enlarged to accommodate a growing number of worshipers.
mongolia.title: Architecture of Mongolia

mongolia.text: Mongolian literature is literature written in Mongolia and/or in the Mongolian language. It was greatly influenced by and evolved from its nomadic oral storytelling traditions, and it originated in the 13th century.
mongolia.title: Mongolian literature

mongolia.text: The culture of Mongolia has been shaped by the country's nomadic tradition and its position at the crossroads of various empires and civilizations.
mongolia.title: Culture of Mongolia

mongolia.text: Transportation in Mongolia comprises rail, road, air, and limited water transport systems that support movement across the country's vast and sparsely populated territory. Railways form the backbone of freight transport, while roads and buses provide domestic and urban connectivity.
mongolia.title: Transport in Mongolia

mongolia.text: Tourism in Mongolia is a relatively small component of the modern economy of Mongolia. Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, tourism was reported by the World Bank to be the third-largest economic sector after mining and agriculture, accounting 7.2% of the total GDP in 2019.
mongolia.title: Tourism in Mongolia

mongolia.text: Telecommunications in Mongolia face unique challenges.
mongolia.title: Telecommunications in Mongolia

mongolia.text: Agriculture in Mongolia constitutes over 10% of Mongolia's annual gross domestic product and employs one-third of the labor force. However, the high altitude, extreme fluctuation in temperature, long winters, and low precipitation provides limited potential for agricultural development.
mongolia.title: Agriculture in Mongolia

mongolia.text: Mongolia had a total primary energy supply of 6.66 Mtoe in 2019. Electricity consumption was 7.71 TWh. Mongolia is a big producer of coal, which is mostly exported.
mongolia.title: Energy in Mongolia

mongolia.text: Mining is important to the national economy of Mongolia. Mongolia is one of the 29 resource-rich developing countries identified by the International Monetary Fund and exploration of copper and coal deposits are generating substantial additional revenue.
mongolia.title: Mining in Mongolia

montenegro.text: The Politics of Montenegro takes place in a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic republic, whereby the Prime Minister of Montenegro is the head of government, and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government.
montenegro.title: Politics of Montenegro

montenegro.text: Demographic features of the population of Montenegro include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects.
montenegro.title: Demographics of Montenegro

montenegro.text: Education in Montenegro is regulated by the Ministry of Education and Science of Government of Montenegro. Education starts in either pre-schools or elementary schools. Children enroll in elementary schools at the age of 6 and elementary education lasts for nine years.
montenegro.title: Education in Montenegro

montenegro.text: Montenegro is a country with an area of 13,812 square kilometres and a population of 620,029, according to the 2011 census. The country is bordered by Croatia, the Adriatic Sea, Bosnia, Herzegovina, Serbia, Kosovo and Albania.
montenegro.title: Health in Montenegro

montenegro.text: This is a list of rivers in Montenegro.
montenegro.title: List of rivers of Montenegro

montenegro.text: The geology of Montenegro includes sedimentary and volcanic rocks from the Paleozoic through the Cenozoic, deposited atop poorly understood crystalline basement rock.
montenegro.title: Geology of Montenegro

montenegro.text: This is a list of mountains in Montenegro.
montenegro.title: List of mountains in Montenegro

montenegro.text: In a referendum on 21 May 2006, the people of Montenegro opted to leave the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro. This result was confirmed with a declaration of independence by the Montenegrin parliament on 3 June 2006.
montenegro.title: Foreign relations of Montenegro

montenegro.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Montenegro.
montenegro.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Montenegro

montenegro.text: Montenegrin cuisine is a result of Montenegro's geographic position and its long history and tradition.
montenegro.title: Montenegrin cuisine

montenegro.text: This is a list of public holidays in Montenegro.
montenegro.title: Public holidays in Montenegro

montenegro.text: Christianity is the most widely professed religion in Montenegro, representing 74.4% of the total population, with Eastern Orthodoxy as the largest denomination, which is adhered to by 71.1% of the population.
montenegro.title: Religion in Montenegro

montenegro.text: Languages of Montenegro are languages that are spoken in Montenegro. According to the Constitution of Montenegro that was adopted in 2007, Montenegro has only one official language, specified as Montenegrin, even though Serbian is used by 43% of the population and Montenegrin by 35% of population.
montenegro.title: Languages of Montenegro

montenegro.text: Sport in Montenegro revolves mostly around team sports, such as football, basketball, handball, and volleyball. Other sports involved are boxing, tennis, swimming, judo, karate, athletics, table tennis, and chess.
montenegro.title: Sport in Montenegro

montenegro.text: The architecture of Montenegro is a mixture of many influences, from Roman and Venetian to Ottoman and modern times.
montenegro.title: Architecture of Montenegro

montenegro.text: The culture of Montenegro is as pluralistic and diverse as its history and geographical position would suggest.
montenegro.title: Culture of Montenegro

montenegro.text: Montenegro is one of the fastest-growing tourist destinations. In 2007, over a million tourists visited Montenegro, making some 7.3 million overnight stays. This accounted for some €480 million in tourism revenue in 2007.
montenegro.title: Tourism in Montenegro

montenegro.text: Telecommunications in Montenegro includes radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
montenegro.title: Telecommunications in Montenegro

montserrat.text: Politics of Montserrat takes place in a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic dependency, whereby the Premier is the head of government, and of a multi-party system. Montserrat is an internally self-governing overseas territory of the United Kingdom.
montserrat.title: Politics of Montserrat

montserrat.text: The demographics of the population of Montserrat include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
montserrat.title: Demographics of Montserrat

montserrat.text: Education in Montserrat is compulsory for children between the ages of 5 and 14, and free up to the age of 17. The Government of Montserrat developed an Education in the Country Policy Plan for 1998–2002 in conjunction with the United Kingdom.
montserrat.title: Education in Montserrat

montserrat.text: This is a list of rivers of Montserrat. Rivers are listed in clockwise order, starting at the north end of the island. Farm River Lee River Paradise River Tar River Valley Hot River White River Belham River a corruption of Balham, a plantation on the south of the river, previously The River estate.
montserrat.title: List of rivers of Montserrat

montserrat.text: The geology of Montserrat formed from the Pliocene into recent times with five major and three parasitic volcanoes. For the most part, the volcanoes only erupted andesite, pyroclastic flows and dome lavas and the Montserrat series is dominantly calc-alkaline.
montserrat.title: Geology of Montserrat

montserrat.text: For information on the wildlife of Montserrat, see: List of birds of Montserrat List of mammals of Montserrat List of amphibians and reptiles of Montserrat
montserrat.title: Wildlife of Montserrat

montserrat.text: Montserrat is a British Overseas Territory in the Leeward Islands and has issued its own stamps since 1876.
montserrat.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Montserrat

montserrat.text: The music of Montserrat is influenced by Irish traditions, noticeable in the set dance-like Bam-chick-lay, and the presence of fife and drum ensembles similar to the bodhrán. Natives are also witness to the jumbie dance, the style of which is still strongly African.
montserrat.title: Music of Montserrat

montserrat.text: Montserrat's national dish is goat water, a goat meat stew (made from the meat of the male goat) and served with crispy bread rolls. It bears resemblance to the Irish stew and can be served with a variety of foods, such as bread, and rice.
montserrat.title: Cuisine of Montserrat

montserrat.text: This is a list of public holidays in Montserrat.
montserrat.title: Public holidays in Montserrat

montserrat.text: Railways: 0 km Highways: total: 269 km paved: 203 km unpaved: 66 km Waterways: none Ports and harbours: Plymouth, Little Bay, Carr's Bay Merchant marine: none Airports: One, Gerald's Airport, opened on 11 July 2005, replacing W.H. Bramble Airport which was destroyed by volcanic eruption in 1997.
montserrat.title: Transport in Montserrat

montserrat.text: Montserrat possesses a number of telecommunications systems, including mobile and main line telephone, radio and television. The country code for Montserrat in the Domain Name System of the Internet is ".ms". Telephony uses the area code 664.
montserrat.title: Telecommunications in Montserrat

montserrat.text: Agriculture in Montserrat, a British Overseas Territory, is a small industry that is heavily influenced by the volcanic activity of the Soufrière Hills.
montserrat.title: Agriculture in Montserrat

morocco.text: The politics of Morocco are conducted within the framework of a semi-constitutional monarchy, characterized by a parliamentary system and a multi-party structure. The prime minister is the head of government.
morocco.title: Politics of Morocco

morocco.text: Demographic features of the population of Morocco include population density, ethnicity, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population. All figures are from the Haut-Commissariat au Plan of Morocco or the United Nations Demographic Yearbooks, unless otherwise indicated.
morocco.title: Demographics of Morocco

morocco.text: The education system in Morocco comprises pre-school, primary, secondary and tertiary levels. School education is supervised by the Ministry of National Education, with considerable devolution to the regional level.
morocco.title: Education in Morocco

morocco.text: Morocco became an independent country in 1956. At that time there were only 400 private practitioners and 300 public health physicians in the entire country. By 1992, the government had thoroughly improved the healthcare service and quality.
morocco.title: Health in Morocco

morocco.text: This is a list of rivers in Morocco. This list is arranged north to south by drainage basin, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
morocco.title: List of rivers of Morocco

morocco.text: The geology of Morocco formed beginning up to two billion years ago, in the Paleoproterozoic and potentially even earlier. It was affected by the Pan-African orogeny, although the later Hercynian orogeny produced fewer changes and left the Maseta Domain, a large area of remnant Paleozoic massifs.
morocco.title: Geology of Morocco

morocco.text: The wildlife of Morocco is composed of its flora and fauna. The country has a wide range of terrains and climate types and a correspondingly large diversity of plants and animals. The coastal areas have a Mediterranean climate and vegetation while inland the Atlas Mountains is forested.
morocco.title: Wildlife of Morocco

morocco.text: The climate of Morocco can be divided into seven sub-zones, determined by the different influences affecting the country: oceanic, Mediterranean, mountain, continental, and desert influences.
morocco.title: Climate of Morocco

morocco.text: Morocco is a member of the United Nations and belongs to the African Union, Arab League, Arab Maghreb Union, Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the Non-Aligned Movement and the Community of Sahel-Saharan States.
morocco.title: Foreign relations of Morocco

morocco.text: The military history of Morocco covers a vast time period and complex events. It interacts with multiple military events in a vast area containing North Africa and the Iberian Peninsula.
morocco.title: Military history of Morocco

morocco.text: The postal history of Morocco is complex due to the country's political development in the 20th century. Mail was sent via post offices operated by the Sherifian post created by the Sultan, and by the European powers.
morocco.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Morocco

morocco.text: Moroccan music has varied greatly over the centuries as well as between geographic regions and social groups. It is influenced by musical styles including Arabic, Berber, Andalusi, Mediterranean, Saharan, West African, and others. Musical styles vary by geography.
morocco.title: Music of Morocco

morocco.text: Moroccan cuisine is the cuisine of Morocco, fueled by interactions and exchanges with many cultures and nations over the centuries. Moroccan cuisine is usually a mix of Arab, Berber, Andalusi, Mediterranean and African cuisines, with minimal European influences.
morocco.title: Moroccan cuisine

morocco.text: This is a list of holidays in Morocco.
morocco.title: Public holidays in Morocco

morocco.text: The main religion in Morocco is Sunni Islam, which is also the state religion of the country. Officially, 99% of the population are Muslim, and virtually all of those are Sunni. The second-largest religion in the country is Christianity, but most Christians in Morocco are foreigners.
morocco.title: Religion in Morocco

morocco.text: The official languages of Morocco are Modern Standard Arabic and Standard Moroccan Tamazight. Moroccan Arabic is the primary spoken vernacular and lingua franca, but a number of regional and foreign languages are also spoken.
morocco.title: Languages of Morocco

morocco.text: Cinema of Morocco refers to the film industry of Morocco. Aside from Arabic-language films, Moroccan cinema also produces Tamazight-language films. The first film in Morocco was shot by Louis Lumière in 1897. The first three Moroccan feature films were funded between 1968-1969.
morocco.title: Cinema of Morocco

morocco.text: Sports in Morocco refers to the sports played in the Kingdom of Morocco. As of 2007, Moroccan society participated in many sports, including handball, football, golf, tennis, basketball, and athletics.
morocco.title: Sport in Morocco

morocco.text: Moroccan architecture reflects Morocco's diverse geography and long history, marked by successive waves of settlers through both migration and military conquest.
morocco.title: Moroccan architecture

morocco.text: Moroccan literature are the written and oral works of Moroccan culture. These works have been produced and shared by people who lived in Morocco and the historical states that have existed partially or entirely within the geographical area of modern-day Morocco.
morocco.title: Moroccan literature

morocco.text: There are around 56,986 km of roads in Morocco. In addition to 1,808 km of highways. The Tangier–Casablanca high-speed rail link marks the first stage of the ONCF's high-speed rail master plan, pursuant to which over 1,500 km of new railway lines will be built by 2035.
morocco.title: Transport in Morocco

morocco.text: Tourism in Morocco is well developed, maintaining a strong tourist industry focused on the country's coast, culture, and history. The Moroccan government created a Ministry of Tourism in 1985.
morocco.title: Tourism in Morocco

morocco.text: Telecommunications in Morocco include fixed-line and mobile telephony, internet services and related infrastructure. The sector has undergone major transformation since the late 1990s, evolving from a state monopoly into a liberalised market with multiple operators.
morocco.title: Telecommunications in Morocco

morocco.text: Agriculture in Morocco employs 23.4% of the nation's workforce, making it one of the largest employers in the country. In the rainy sections of the northwest, barley, wheat, and other cereals can be raised without irrigation.
morocco.title: Agriculture in Morocco

morocco.text: Morocco's energy policy is defined and implemented by several public institutions, primarily the Ministry of Energy Transition and Sustainable Development, with the involvement of sectoral agencies such as the National Office of Hydrocarbons and Mines and the Office National de l'Électricité et de l'Eau potable, which are responsible respectively for hydrocarbons and electricity.
morocco.title: Energy policy of Morocco

picture.credit: Miguel González Novo from Melilla, España

morocco.text: The mining industry of Morocco is important to the national economy. Morocco is the world's largest producer of phosphate, and contains about 75% of the world's estimated reserves. Mining contributed up to 35% of exports and 5% of GDP in 2011.
morocco.title: Mining industry of Morocco

mozambique.text: Politics in Mozambique takes place in a framework of a semi-presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the President of Mozambique is head of state and head of government in a multi-party system.
mozambique.title: Politics of Mozambique

mozambique.text: The demographics of Mozambique describes the condition and overview of Mozambique's peoples. Demographic topics include basic education, health, and population statistics as well as identified racial and religious affiliations.
mozambique.title: Demographics of Mozambique

mozambique.text: Education in Mozambique is organized by three main stages: primary education, secondary education and higher education. Although having a national public education system, several educational programmes and initiatives in Mozambique are mainly funded and supported by the international community.
mozambique.title: Education in Mozambique

mozambique.text: Health in Mozambique has a complex history, influenced by the social, economic, and political changes that the country has experienced. Before the Mozambican Civil War, healthcare was heavily influenced by the Portuguese.
mozambique.title: Health in Mozambique

mozambique.text: This is a list of rivers in Mozambique. This list is arranged by drainage basin, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
mozambique.title: List of rivers of Mozambique

mozambique.text: The geology of Mozambique is primarily extremely old Precambrian metamorphic and igneous crystalline basement rock, formed in the Archean and Proterozoic, in some cases more than two billion years ago.
mozambique.title: Geology of Mozambique

mozambique.text: The wildlife of Mozambique consists of the flora and fauna of this country in southeastern Africa. Mozambique has a range of different habitat types and an ecologically rich and diverse wildlife. This includes 236 species of mammal, 740 species of bird and 5,692 species of vascular plant.
mozambique.title: Wildlife of Mozambique

mozambique.text: While alliances dating back to the Mozambican War of Independence remain relevant, Mozambique's foreign policy has become increasingly pragmatic. The twin pillars of the policy are maintenance of good relations with its neighbors and maintenance and expansion of ties to development partners.
mozambique.title: Foreign relations of Mozambique

mozambique.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Mozambique.
mozambique.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Mozambique

mozambique.text: The native folk music of Mozambique has been highly influenced by Portuguese colonisation and local language forms. The most popular style of modern dance music is marrabenta.
mozambique.title: Music of Mozambique

mozambique.text: The cuisine of Mozambique represents a mixture of indigenous foods and cooking practices, coupled with outside influences from Indian Ocean trade and Portuguese colonization.
mozambique.title: Mozambican cuisine

mozambique.text: This is a list of holidays in Mozambique This is a list of City-specific holidays in Mozambique
mozambique.title: Public holidays in Mozambique

mozambique.text: Christianity is the largest religion in Mozambique, with substantial minorities adhering to Islam or identifying with no religion. Mozambique is a secular state.
mozambique.title: Religion in Mozambique

mozambique.text: Mozambique is a multilingual country. A number of Bantu languages are indigenous to Mozambique. Portuguese, inherited from the colonial period, is the official language, and Mozambique is a full member of the Community of Portuguese Language Countries.
mozambique.title: Languages of Mozambique

mozambique.text: The cinema of Mozambique refers to the films and the film industry of Mozambique, which creates films in Portuguese.
mozambique.title: Cinema of Mozambique

mozambique.text: Mozambican literature refers to the body of written works produced in Mozambique or by Mozambican authors This literature has been shaped by the country's diverse cultures and tumultuous history, including colonialism, independence movements, and civil war.
mozambique.title: Mozambican literature

mozambique.text: Modes of transport in Mozambique include rail, road, water, and air. There are rail links serving principal cities and connecting the country with Malawi, Zimbabwe and South Africa. There are over 30,000 km of roads, but much of the network is unpaved.
mozambique.title: Transport in Mozambique

mozambique.text: The tourism assets of Mozambique include the country's natural environment, wildlife, and cultural heritage, which provide opportunities for beach, cultural, and eco-tourism.
mozambique.title: Tourism in Mozambique

mozambique.text: Telecommunications in Mozambique include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
mozambique.title: Telecommunications in Mozambique

mozambique.text: Mozambique has a variety of regional cropping patterns; agro-climatic zones range from arid and semi-arid to the sub-humid zones to the humid highlands.
mozambique.title: Agriculture in Mozambique

mozambique.text: Mozambique has abundant energy sources available for exploitation. As of 2021, the country was ranked first in energy potential of all the countries in the Southern African Power Pool, with an estimated energy capacity of 187,000 MW.
mozambique.title: Energy in Mozambique

mozambique.text: The mineral industry of Mozambique plays a significant role in the world's production of aluminium, beryllium, and tantalum. In 2006, Mozambique's share of the world's tantalum mine output amounted to 6%; beryllium, 5%; and aluminium, 2%.
mozambique.title: Mineral industry of Mozambique

myanmar.text: Myanmar operates de jure as a unitary assembly-independent republic under its 2008 constitution. On 1 February 2021, Myanmar's military overthrew the country's democratically elected government in a coup, causing ongoing anti-coup protests.
myanmar.title: Politics of Myanmar

myanmar.text: This is a demography of Myanmar including statistics such as population, ethnicity, language, education level, and religious affiliations.
myanmar.title: Demographics of Myanmar

myanmar.text: The educational system of Myanmar is operated by the Ministry of Education. Universities and professional institutes from Upper Burma and Lower Burma are run by two separate entities, each called the Department of Higher Education, with their headquarters in Yangon and Mandalay, respectively.
myanmar.title: Education in Myanmar

myanmar.text: The current population of Myanmar is 67.05 million. It was 27.27 million in 1970. The general state of healthcare in Myanmar is poor. The military government of 1962-2011 spent anywhere from 0.5% to 3% of the country's GDP on healthcare.
myanmar.title: Health in Myanmar

myanmar.text: This is a list of rivers in Myanmar. This list is arranged by drainage basin from east to west, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
myanmar.title: List of rivers of Myanmar

myanmar.text: The geology of Myanmar is shaped by dramatic, ongoing tectonic processes controlled by shifting tectonic components as the Indian Plate slides northwards and towards Southeast Asia. Myanmar spans across parts of three tectonic plates separated by north-trending faults.
myanmar.title: Geology of Myanmar

myanmar.text: The wildlife of Myanmar includes a diverse range of flora and fauna and natural habitats. As the largest country in Mainland Southeast Asia, Myanmar has numerous types of ecosystems, ranging from tropical rainforests to alpine tundra and mountains.
myanmar.title: Wildlife of Myanmar

myanmar.text: The following is a list of mountains in Myanmar. The elevations are in metres. For the names of the mountains in the Latin script the most common transcription has been adopted.
myanmar.title: List of mountains in Myanmar

myanmar.text: The climate of Myanmar varies depending on location and in the highlands, on elevation.
myanmar.title: Climate of Myanmar

myanmar.text: Myanmar has full diplomatic relations with 126 countries out of 192 United Nation Members States. The country has generally maintained warmer relations with near states and is a member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.
myanmar.title: Foreign relations of Myanmar

myanmar.text: The military history of Myanmar spans over a millennium, and is one of the main factors that have shaped the history of the country, and to a certain degree, the history of Southeast Asia.
myanmar.title: Military history of Myanmar

myanmar.text: The music of Myanmar shares many similarities with other musical styles in the region. Traditional music is melodic, having its own unique form of harmony, often composed with a 44, a 24 or a 816 time signature.
myanmar.title: Music of Myanmar

myanmar.text: Burmese cuisine encompasses the diverse regional culinary traditions of Myanmar, which have developed through longstanding agricultural practices, centuries of sociopolitical and economic change, and cross-cultural contact and trade with neighboring countries at the confluence of Southeast Asia, East Asia, and South Asia, such as modern-day nations of Thailand, China, and India, respectively.
myanmar.title: Burmese cuisine

myanmar.text: 16 distinct public holidays are observed in Myanmar.
myanmar.title: Public holidays in Myanmar

myanmar.text: Myanmar is a Buddhist majority country with a significant minority of Christians and other religious groups residing in the country. Buddhism is a part of Myanmar culture.
myanmar.title: Religion in Myanmar

myanmar.text: There are approximately a hundred languages spoken in Myanmar. Burmese, spoken by two-thirds of the population, is the official language.
myanmar.title: Languages of Myanmar

myanmar.text: The cinema of Myanmar dates to the 1910s. The person who created the first silent film was Ohn Maung.
myanmar.title: Cinema of Myanmar

myanmar.text: Myanmar has several sports, with some of them having come during British rule.
myanmar.title: Sport in Myanmar

myanmar.text: The architecture of Myanmar, in Southeast Asia, includes architectural styles which reflect the influence of neighboring and Western nations and modernization.
myanmar.title: Myanmar architecture

myanmar.text: The literature of Myanmar spans over a millennium. The Burmese language, unlike other Southeast Asian languages, adopted words primarily from Pāli rather than from Sanskrit. In addition, Burmese literature tends to reflect local folklore and culture.
myanmar.title: Burmese literature

myanmar.text: Art of Myanmar refers to visual art created in Myanmar. Ancient Burmese art was influenced by India and China, and was often religious in nature, ranging from Hindu sculptures in the Thaton Kingdom to Theravada Buddhist images in the Sri Ksetra Kingdom.
myanmar.title: Art of Myanmar

myanmar.text: Transport in Myanmar is characterised by a strong reliance on road transport for both passenger and freight movement. Other modes such as railways, inland waterways, and air transport play secondary roles.
myanmar.title: Transport in Myanmar

myanmar.text: Tourism in Myanmar is a developing sector. As of 2023, new tourist visa applications have resumed. Although Myanmar possesses tourist potential, much of the industry remains to be developed. The number of visitors to Burma is small compared to its neighbouring countries.
myanmar.title: Tourism in Myanmar

myanmar.text: Myanmar began liberalisation of its telecommunications market in 2013.
myanmar.title: Telecommunications in Myanmar

myanmar.text: Agriculture in Myanmar is the main industry in the country, accounting for 60 percent of the GDP and employing some 65 percent of the labour force. Burma was once Asia's largest exporter of rice, and rice remains the country's most crucial agricultural commodity.
myanmar.title: Agriculture in Myanmar

myanmar.text: Myanmar's energy sector is characterised by low per capita energy consumption and a limited electrification rate, with an estimated 65% of the population lacking access to the national grid as of 2019.
myanmar.title: Energy in Myanmar

namibia.text: Politics of Namibia takes place in a framework of a semi-presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the President of Namibia is both head of state and head of government, and of a pluriform multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by both the president and the government.
namibia.title: Politics of Namibia

namibia.text: This is a demography of the population of Namibia including population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
namibia.title: Demographics of Namibia

namibia.text: Education in Namibia is compulsory until the year a learner turns 18. There are approximately 1900 schools in Namibia of which 100 are privately owned.
namibia.title: Education in Namibia

namibia.text: The health status of Namibia has increased steadily since independence, and the government does have focus on health in the country and seeks to make health service upgrades.
namibia.title: Health in Namibia

namibia.text: This is a list of streams and rivers in Namibia, arranged geographically by drainage basin.
namibia.title: List of rivers of Namibia

picture.credit: David A. Foster und Ben D. Goscombe

namibia.text: The geology of Namibia encompasses rocks of Paleoproterozoic, Mesoproterozoic and Neoproterozoic and Paleozoic to Cenozoic age. About 46% of the countryʼs surface are bedrock exposure, while the remainder is covered by the young overburden sediments of the Kalahari and Namib deserts.
namibia.title: Geology of Namibia

namibia.text: The wildlife of Namibia is composed of its flora and fauna. Namibia's endangered species include the wild dog, black rhino, oribi and puku.
namibia.title: Wildlife of Namibia

namibia.text: Namibia follows a largely independent foreign policy, with strong affiliations with states that aided the independence struggle, including Nigeria, Libya, and Cuba. In Africa, Namibia has been involved in conflicts in neighbouring Angola as well as Democratic Republic of the Congo.
namibia.title: Foreign relations of Namibia

namibia.text: Namibia, formerly known as South West Africa and German South West Africa, has a long history of postal services, starting in 1814 with postal runners delivering messages among mission stations. The first stamps were printed during the German colonial period.
namibia.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Namibia

namibia.text: The music of Namibia includes a number of folk styles, as well as pop, rock, reggae, jazz, house and hip hop.
namibia.title: Music of Namibia

namibia.text: Namibian cuisine is the cuisine of Namibia. It is influenced by two primary cultural strands: cookery practised by indigenous people of Namibia such as the Himba, Herero and San groups; and settler cookery introduced during the colonial period by people of German, Afrikaner and British descent.
namibia.title: Namibian cuisine

namibia.text: The following table provides an overview of public holidays in Namibia. These are stipulated in the Public Holidays Act of 1990 of the Namibian National Assembly. When a public holiday fall on a Sunday, the following Monday is observed as a public holiday.
namibia.title: Public holidays in Namibia

namibia.text: Religion in Namibia is dominated by various branches of Christianity, with more than 90 percent of Namibian citizens identifying themselves as Christian. According to the government's survey, in 2013 up to two-thirds of the country was Protestant, including as much as 44% Lutheran.
namibia.title: Religion in Namibia

namibia.text: Namibia, despite its sparse population, is home to a wide diversity of languages, from multiple language families: Germanic, Bantu, and the various Khoisan families. Afrikaans, German, and English had equal status as official languages during the time Namibia was administered by South Africa.
namibia.title: Languages of Namibia

namibia.text: The Cinema of Namibia refers to cinema in the country of Namibia, which claimed its independence from South Africa in 1990.
namibia.title: Cinema of Namibia

namibia.text: The principal sports in Namibia are football, rugby union, cricket, golf and fishing. Boxing and athletics are also popular. The home stadium for all national teams is Independence Stadium in Windhoek, while Sam Nujoma Stadium in Katutura is also occasionally used.
namibia.title: Sport in Namibia

namibia.text: This article deals with the system of transport in Namibia, both public and private.
namibia.title: Transport in Namibia

namibia.text: Tourism in Namibia is a major industry, contributing N$7.2 billion to the country's gross domestic product. Annually, over one million travelers visit Namibia, with roughly one in three coming from South Africa, then Germany and finally the United Kingdom, Italy and France.
namibia.title: Tourism in Namibia

namibia.text: Telecommunications in Namibia include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
namibia.title: Telecommunications in Namibia

picture.credit: Tim Brunauer on behalf of Deutsche Gesellschaft

namibia.text: Agriculture in Namibia contributes around 5% of the national Gross Domestic Product though 25% to 40% of Namibians depend on subsistence agriculture and herding. Primary products included livestock and meat products, crop farming and forestry.
namibia.title: Agriculture in Namibia

namibia.text: Mining is the biggest contributor to Namibia's economy in terms of revenue. It accounts for 25% of the country's income. Its contribution to the gross domestic product is also very important and makes it one of the largest economic sectors of the country.
namibia.title: Mining in Namibia

nauru.text: The politics of Nauru, officially the Republic of Naoero, take place in a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic republic, whereby the President of Nauru is the head of government of the executive branch. Legislative power is vested in both the government and the parliament.
nauru.title: Politics of Nauru

nauru.text: The demographics of Nauru, an island country in the Pacific Ocean, are known through national censuses, which have been analysed by various statistical bureaus since the 1920s.
nauru.title: Demographics of Nauru

picture.credit: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

nauru.text: Education in Nauru is compulsory for children between the ages of 5 and 16. There are eleven schools in Nauru, including three primary schools and two secondary schools. There is an Able/Disable Centre for children with disabilities. Education at these schools is free.
nauru.title: Education in Nauru

nauru.text: In Nauru, health is challenged by obesity, limited lifespan and childhood health.
nauru.title: Health in Nauru

nauru.text: Nauru is positioned in the Nauru Basin of the Pacific Ocean, on a part of the Pacific Plate that formed at a mid oceanic ridge at 132 Ma. From mid Eocene to Oligocene times a submarine volcano built up over a hotspot, and formed a seamount composed of basalt.
nauru.title: Geology of Nauru

nauru.text: Nauru became a sovereign, independent republic on 31 January 1968, following the passage of the Nauru Independence Act 1967 by the Parliament of Australia and the end of its status as a United Nations Trust Territory.
nauru.title: Foreign relations of Nauru

nauru.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Nauru. The Republic of Nauru is an island country in Micronesia in the South Pacific. Its nearest neighbour is Banaba Island in Kiribati, 300 kilometres to the east.
nauru.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Nauru

nauru.text: The music of Nauru demonstrates its Micronesian heritage.
nauru.title: Music of Nauru

nauru.text: The cuisine of Nauru is the traditional cuisine of the island state on the Pacific Ocean. Nauru has the world's highest rate of obesity.
nauru.title: Nauruan cuisine

nauru.text: This is a list of holidays in Nauru, an island nation in Micronesia.
nauru.title: Public holidays in Nauru

nauru.text: Christianity is the largest religion in Nauru, with Nauru Congregational Church and Catholicism being the largest denominations, encompassing 34.3% and 33.9% of the population respectively as of the 2021 census.
nauru.title: Religion in Nauru

nauru.text: Transport in Nauru includes pedestrian, bicycle, automobile, train, and airplane. There is no harbour or port as of the 2020s, as the island is surrounded by a rocky coral reef, however an international port is currently under construction.
nauru.title: Transport in Nauru

nauru.text: Nauru is a small, isolated western Pacific island, which lacks many of the tourist facilities of some of its larger neighbours, such as Fiji, the Cook Islands, or even New Caledonia. Tourism does not make a significant contribution to the economy.
nauru.title: Tourism in Nauru

nauru.text: Nauru has one government-owned radio station and two television stations, one of which is government owned. The island has telephone service under country code 674. The island's Internet service is provided by CenPacNet and Digicel Nauru. The country's ccTLD is.nr.
nauru.title: Telecommunications in Nauru

nepal.text: The politics of Nepal functions within the framework of a parliamentary republic with a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the Prime Minister and their cabinet, while legislative power is vested in the Parliament.
nepal.title: Politics of Nepal

nepal.text: The current population of Nepal is 29,164,578 as per the 2021 census. The population growth rate is 0.92% per year. In the 2011 census, Nepal's population was approximately 26 million people with a population growth rate of 1.35% and a median age of 21.6 years.
nepal.title: Demographics of Nepal

nepal.text: Education in Nepal has been modeled on the Indian system, which is in turn based on that of the old British Raj. The National Examinations Board supervises all standardized tests, while the Ministry of Education and Sports is responsible for managing educational activities in Nepal.
nepal.title: Education in Nepal

nepal.text: Health care services in Nepal are provided by both public and private sectors and are generally regarded as failing to meet international standards. Prevalence of disease is significantly higher in Nepal than in other South Asian countries, especially in rural areas.
nepal.title: Health in Nepal

nepal.text: This is a list of rivers of Nepal, east to west. This list is arranged by drainage basin, indented to show the structure of confluences. Tributaries rising inside India are not shown. The basin is generally categorized into ten major basins as listed below.
nepal.title: List of rivers of Nepal

nepal.text: The geology of Nepal is dominated by the Himalaya, the highest, youngest, and one of the most geologically active mountain ranges on Earth. Himalaya is a type locality for the study of on-going continent-continent collision tectonics.
nepal.title: Geology of Nepal

nepal.text: Wildlife diversity is a notable feature of Nepal. Because of the variance in climate, from tropical to arctic, Nepal has a large variety of plants and animals. Wildlife tourism is a major source of tourism in the country.
nepal.title: Wildlife of Nepal

nepal.text: Almost all of Nepal is mountainous and it contains a large section of the Himalayas range peaks, including the highest mountain range in the world. Eight of the fourteen eight-thousanders are located in the country, either in whole or shared across a border with China or India.
nepal.title: List of mountains in Nepal

nepal.text: Though the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is the government agency responsible for conducting the foreign relations of Nepal, historically, it has been the Office of the Prime Minister that has exercised the authority to formulate the country's foreign policies.
nepal.title: Foreign relations of Nepal

nepal.text: The Nepalese Army or Gorkha Army is the armed military Land warfare force of Nepal and a major component of the Military of Nepal.
nepal.title: Military history of Nepal

nepal.text: Nepal has a long postal history. The modern form of postal service was started by the Rana Prime minister Ranaudip Singh in 1878. He established the first post office which was named Nepal Hulak Ghar. In 1881, the first postal stamp was issued.
nepal.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Nepal

nepal.text: Music of Nepal refers to the various musical genres played and listened to in Nepal. With more than fifty ethnic groups in Nepal, the country's music is highly diverse.
nepal.title: Music of Nepal

nepal.text: Nepali cuisine comprises a variety of cuisines based upon ethnicity, alluvial soil and climate relating to cultural diversity and geography of Nepal and neighboring regions of Sikkim and Gorkhaland. Dal-bhat-tarkari is eaten throughout Nepal.
nepal.title: Nepalese cuisine

nepal.text: Bikram Sambat is the official and the day to day calendar of Nepal while the Gregorian calendar is used for international events and holidays. Additionally, since 2023, Nepal Sambat dates are written alongside Bikram Sambat. Weekends in Nepal are different for each sector.
nepal.title: Public holidays in Nepal

nepal.text: Religion in Nepal encompasses a wide diversity of groups and beliefs.
nepal.title: Religion in Nepal

nepal.text: Languages of Nepal, referred to as Nepalese languages in the country's constitution, are the languages having at least an ancient history or origin inside the sovereign territory of Nepal, spoken by Nepalis.
nepal.title: Languages of Nepal

nepal.text: Nepali Cinema, also referred to as "Nepali Chalachitra" is the filmmaking industry in Nepal. This includes films in various languages of Nepal, most notably in the Nepali language but also in Newari, Maithili, Tamang, Bhojpuri and Tharu among others.
nepal.title: Cinema of Nepal

nepal.text: Sport in Nepal is an important part of Nepalese culture, encompassing both traditional Nepalese games and modern international disciplines. While Nepal has a long history of traditional sports, the contemporary era is dominated by cricket, football, and volleyball.
nepal.title: Sports in Nepal

nepal.text: Nepali architecture or Nepalese architecture is influenced by the architecture of India, Tibet and China. The pagoda architectural tradition figures prominently among Hindu temples in the country.
nepal.title: Architecture of Nepal

nepal.text: Nepali literature is the literature of Nepal. This is distinct from Nepali literature, which is the literature in only Nepali language. The major literary languages of Nepal are:
nepal.title: Literature of Nepal

nepal.text: Transportation in Nepal has developed under significant geographical constraints due to the country's mountainous terrain and landlocked position.
nepal.title: Transport in Nepal

nepal.text: Tourism is the largest source of foreign exchange revenue for Nepal. Tourism in Nepal contributes about 6.7% of the country's gross domestic product. In 2025, Nepal welcomed 11,58,4589 tourists, placing it 147th globally in terms of tourist numbers.
nepal.title: Tourism in Nepal

nepal.text: Nepal's telecommunication network has increased over the years significantly, with the number of telephone users reaching 40,789,198 as of 14 May 2019. Nepal Telecommunications Authority is the regulatory body of telecommunications in the country.
nepal.title: Telecommunications in Nepal

nepal.text: In Nepal, the economy is dominated by agriculture. In the late 1980s, it was the livelihood for more than 90% of the population. Although only approximately 20% of the total land area was cultivable. The agricultural sector has remained the backbone of the national economy.
nepal.title: Agriculture in Nepal

nepal.text: Nepal is a country enclosed by land, situated between China and India. It has a total area of 148,006.67 square kilometers and a population of 29.16 million. It has a small economy, with a GDP of $42 billion in 2024, amounting to about 1% of South Asia and 0.04% of the World's GDP.
nepal.title: Energy in Nepal

nepal.text: Nepal has been mining on a small scale for iron, copper, lead, zinc, cobalt, nickel and gold. Old mine pits, adits, smelting places and other remnants of mine processing are found all over Nepal. Some villages are named after mineral names, such as Taba Khani, Falam Khani, Shisa Khani or Sun Khani.
nepal.title: Mineral resources of Nepal

netherlands.text: The Kingdom of the Netherlands is a sovereign state with a parliamentary representative democracy. A constitutional monarchy, the country is organised as a decentralised unitary state. The Netherlands can be described as a consociational state.
netherlands.title: Politics of the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Demographic features of the population of the Netherlands include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the population, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
netherlands.title: Demographics of the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Education in the Netherlands is characterized by division: education is oriented toward the needs and background of the pupil. Education is divided over schools for different age groups, some of which are divided in streams for different educational levels.
netherlands.title: Education in the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Health in the Netherlands includes the leading causes of death, risk factors, mental health status, and health disparities of the population, as well as the impacts of climate change on health.
netherlands.title: Health in the Netherlands

netherlands.text: These are the main rivers of the Netherlands. All of the Netherlands is drained into the North Sea, partly via the IJsselmeer lake. In the list below, rivers that flow into the sea are sorted following the North Sea coast from the Belgian border near Knokke to the German border near Emden.
netherlands.title: List of rivers of the Netherlands

netherlands.text: The geology of the Netherlands describes the geological sequence of the Netherlands. Large parts of the Netherlands today are below sea level and have in the past been covered by the sea or flooded at regular intervals.
netherlands.title: Geology of the Netherlands

netherlands.text: The following is a list of mountains and hills in the Netherlands.
netherlands.title: List of mountains and hills in the Netherlands

netherlands.text: The foreign policy of the Netherlands is based on four basic commitments: to the Atlantic cooperation, to European integration, to international development and to international law.
netherlands.title: Foreign relations of the Netherlands

picture.credit: Claes Janszoon Visscher II / Joannes van Doetecu

netherlands.text: The Netherlands, as a nation state, dates to 1568, when the Dutch Revolt created the Dutch Empire.
netherlands.title: Military history of the Netherlands

netherlands.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of the Netherlands. The postal region of the Netherlands is located in North-West Europe and comprises the whole territory of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Europe and until 2010 the full territory of the country the Netherlands.
netherlands.title: Postage stamps and postal history of the Netherlands

netherlands.text: The Netherlands has multiple musical traditions. Contemporary Dutch popular music is heavily influenced by music styles that emerged in the 1950s, in the United Kingdom and United States. The style is sung in both Dutch and English.
netherlands.title: Music of the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Dutch cuisine is formed from the cooking traditions and practices of the Netherlands. The country's cuisine is shaped by its location on the fertile Rhine–Meuse–Scheldt delta at the North Sea, giving rise to fishing, farming, and overseas trade.
netherlands.title: Dutch cuisine

netherlands.text: The national holidays in the Netherlands are the following: While there are other holidays which are widely celebrated, these are not officially recognised national holidays. They are as follows: Saint Nicholas's Eve on 5 December is not a national holiday, it is widely celebrated.
netherlands.title: Public holidays in the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Religion in the Netherlands was dominated by Christianity between the 10th and 20th centuries. In the late 19th century, roughly 60% of the population was Calvinist and 35% was Catholic. Also, until The Holocaust, there was a noticeable Jewish minority.
netherlands.title: Religion in the Netherlands

netherlands.text: The predominant language of the Netherlands is Dutch, spoken and written by almost all people in the Netherlands. Dutch is also spoken and official in the Dutch Caribbean as well as the Flemish Community of Belgium and Suriname.
netherlands.title: Languages of the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Cinema of the Netherlands refers to the film industry based in the Netherlands. Because the Dutch film industry is relatively small, and there is little or no international market for Dutch films, almost all films rely on state funding.
netherlands.title: Cinema of the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Approximately 5 million of the 17 million people in the Netherlands are registered to one of the 35,000 sports clubs in the country. About two thirds of the population older than 15 years participates in sports weekly.
netherlands.title: Sport in the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Dutch architecture includes the history of architecture within the current territory of the Netherlands, thereby excluding Belgium, which is often included in the broader term "the Low Countries".
netherlands.title: Architecture of the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Dutch-language literature comprises all writings of literary merit written in the Dutch language, a product of the Netherlands, Belgium, Suriname, the Netherlands Antilles and of formerly Dutch-speaking regions, such as French Flanders, South Africa, and Indonesia.
netherlands.title: Dutch-language literature

netherlands.text: Dutch art describes the history of visual arts in the Netherlands, after the United Provinces separated from Flanders. Earlier painting in the area is covered in Early Netherlandish painting and Dutch and Flemish Renaissance painting.
netherlands.title: Dutch art

netherlands.text: The Netherlands is both a very densely populated and a highly developed country in which transport is a key factor of the economy. Correspondingly it has a very dense and modern infrastructure, facilitating transport with road, rail, air and water networks.
netherlands.title: Transport in the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Tourism in the Netherlands is a relatively small sector of the country's economy with a total contribution of 5.4% to gross domestic product and 9.6% to employment. In 2017 the Netherlands was visited by 17 million foreign tourists, making it the 20th most visited country in the world.
netherlands.title: Tourism in the Netherlands

netherlands.text: This article is intended to give an overview of telecommunications in the Netherlands.
netherlands.title: Telecommunications in the Netherlands

netherlands.text: Energy in the Netherlands describes energy and electricity production, consumption and import in the Netherlands. Electricity sector in the Netherlands is the main article of electricity in the Netherlands.
netherlands.title: Energy in the Netherlands

new-caledonia.text: New Caledonia is a French sui generis collectivity with a system of government based on parliamentarism and representative democracy. The President of the Government is the head of government, and there is a multi-party system, with Executive power being exercised by the government.
new-caledonia.title: Politics of New Caledonia

new-caledonia.text: Demographic features of the population of New Caledonia include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
new-caledonia.title: Demographics of New Caledonia

new-caledonia.text: A list of rivers of New Caledonia:
new-caledonia.title: List of rivers of New Caledonia

new-caledonia.text: The geology of New Caledonia includes all major rock types, which here range in age from ~290 million years old to recent. Their formation is driven by alternate plate collisions and rifting. The mantle-derived Eocene Peridotite Nappe is the most significant and widespread unit.
new-caledonia.title: Geology of New Caledonia

new-caledonia.text: The biodiversity of New Caledonia is of exceptional biological and paleoecological interest. It is frequently referred to as a biodiversity hotspot. The territory is a large South Pacific archipelago with a total land area of more than 18,000 square kilometres.
new-caledonia.title: Biodiversity of New Caledonia

new-caledonia.text: As a semi-autonomous overseas department of France, France is responsible for New Caledonia's defence, foreign relations, law and order, monetary policy and tertiary education.
new-caledonia.title: Foreign relations of New Caledonia

new-caledonia.text: The music of New Caledonia is rooted in the Melanesian tradition. The Pacific Tempo is an important music festival, held every three years in [England]; the biennial equinox is also an important celebration. Modern popular performers include OK!
new-caledonia.title: Music of New Caledonia

new-caledonia.text: This is a list of holidays in New Caledonia.
new-caledonia.title: Public holidays in New Caledonia

new-caledonia.text: In New Caledonia, a sui generis collectivity of France, French is the official and predominant language. The collectivity is also home to about thirty New Caledonian languages, which form a branch of the Southern Oceanic languages. They are spoken mainly by the indigenous Kanaks of the islands.
new-caledonia.title: Languages of New Caledonia

new-caledonia.text: Written New Caledonian literature is very recent. The New Caledonian Writers Association is an important advocacy group for literary activity in the islands. The Oceanian International Book Fair has been a relevant meeting point since 2003.
new-caledonia.title: New Caledonian literature

new-caledonia.text: The transportation networks in New Caledonia face several geographical constraints, including its insularity, climate, distance from Metropolitan France (approximately 17,000 km), the relatively large size of the main island, Grande Terre (with an area of 16,346 km2, it is the largest French island, twice the size of Corsica), and the presence of the Central Range spanning nearly its entire length.
new-caledonia.title: Transport in New Caledonia

new-caledonia.text: New Caledonia was "largely indifferent to tourists... as long as nickel mining remained economically dominant". After the Korean War and Vietnam War, world prices for nickel collapsed and aggressive marketing campaigns were initiated for the territory.
new-caledonia.title: Tourism in New Caledonia

new-zealand.text: The politics of New Zealand function within a framework of an independent, unitary, parliamentary democracy. The system of government is based on the Westminster system, and the legal system is modelled on the common law of England.
new-zealand.title: Politics of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: The demographics of New Zealand encompass the gender, ethnic, religious, geographic, and economic backgrounds of the 5.3 million people living in New Zealand. New Zealanders predominantly live in urban areas on the North Island.
new-zealand.title: Demographics of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: The education system in New Zealand implements a three-tier model which includes primary and intermediate schools, followed by secondary schools and by tertiary education at universities and polytechnics.
new-zealand.title: Education in New Zealand

new-zealand.text: New Zealand is a high income country, and this is reflected in the overall good health status of the population. However like other wealthy countries, New Zealand suffers from high rates of obesity and heart disease.
new-zealand.title: Health in New Zealand

new-zealand.text: This is a list of all waterways named as rivers in New Zealand.
new-zealand.title: List of rivers of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: The geology of New Zealand is noted for its volcanic activity, earthquakes and geothermal areas because of its position on the boundary of the Australian Plate and Pacific Plates.
new-zealand.title: Geology of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: The biodiversity of New Zealand, a large island country located in the south-western Pacific Ocean, is varied and distinctive. The species of New Zealand accumulated over many millions of years as lineages evolved in the local circumstances.
new-zealand.title: Biodiversity of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: The following are lists of mountains in New Zealand ordered by height. Names, heights, topographic prominence and isolation, and coordinates were extracted from the official Land Information New Zealand Topo50 topographic maps at the interactive topographic map of New Zealand site.
new-zealand.title: List of mountains of New Zealand by height

new-zealand.text: The climate of New Zealand is varied due to the country's diverse landscape. Most regions of New Zealand belong to the temperate zone with a maritime climate characterised by four distinct seasons. Winters are relatively mild and summers comparatively cool.
new-zealand.title: Climate of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: The foreign relations of New Zealand are oriented chiefly toward developed democratic nations and emerging Pacific Island economies. Until the late 20th century, New Zealand aligned itself strongly with the United Kingdom and had few bilateral relationships with other countries.
new-zealand.title: Foreign relations of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: The military history of New Zealand is an aspect of the history of New Zealand that spans several hundred years. Before European contact, Māori iwi engaged in intertribal warfare as the region reached its carrying capacity.
new-zealand.title: Military history of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: Postal services in New Zealand have existed since at least 1831, when the Postmaster-General of New South Wales deputed a Bay of Islands merchant to receive and return mail.
new-zealand.title: Postage stamps and postal history of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: The music of New Zealand has been influenced by a number of traditions, including Māori music, the music introduced by European settlers during the nineteenth century, and a variety of styles imported during the twentieth century, including blues, jazz, country, rock and roll, reggae, and hip-hop, with many of these genres given a unique New Zealand interpretation.
new-zealand.title: Music of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: The cuisine of New Zealand has historical influences from British cuisine and Māori culture. As an island nation with a primarily agricultural economy, New Zealand yields produce from land and sea.
new-zealand.title: New Zealand cuisine

new-zealand.text: Public holidays in New Zealand consist of a variety of cultural, national, and religious holidays that are legislated in New Zealand. Workers can get a maximum of 12 public holidays and a minimum of 20 annual leave days a year.
new-zealand.title: Public holidays in New Zealand

picture.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Gadfium ass

new-zealand.text: Religion in New Zealand is diverse. The country has no state religion and freedom of religion has been protected since the signing of the Treaty of Waitangi. New Zealand was predominantly Christian from the mid 1800s, but since 2000 has become post-Christian.
new-zealand.title: Religion in New Zealand

new-zealand.text: English is the predominant language and the primary official language of New Zealand. Almost the entire population speak it either as native speakers or proficiently as a second language.
new-zealand.title: Languages of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: The cinema of New Zealand refers to films made by New Zealand–based production companies in New Zealand or films made about New Zealand by filmmakers from other countries. New Zealand produces many films that are co-financed by overseas companies.
new-zealand.title: Cinema of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: Sport in New Zealand largely reflects the nation's British colonial heritage, with some of the most popular sports being rugby union, rugby league, cricket, football, footy, basketball, horse racing and netball, which are primarily played in Commonwealth countries.
new-zealand.title: Sport in New Zealand

new-zealand.text: Architecture of New Zealand is a built environment of regions, cities and towns of New Zealand, which is best known for its connection to the land between both islands, its use of local materials, and its incorporation of natural elements.
new-zealand.title: Architecture of New Zealand

new-zealand.text: New Zealand literature is literature, both oral and written, produced by the people of New Zealand. It often deals with New Zealand themes, people or places, is written predominantly in New Zealand English, and features Māori culture and the use of the Māori language.
new-zealand.title: New Zealand literature

new-zealand.text: New Zealand art consists of the visual and plastic arts originating from New Zealand and comes from different traditions: indigenous Māori art and that brought here including from early British and sometimes Irish settlers.
new-zealand.title: New Zealand art

picture.credit: Phillip Capper from Wellington, New Zealand

new-zealand.text: Transport in New Zealand consists of road, rail, water and air services, together with walking and cycling. Before Europeans arrived, Māori travelled on foot or by watercraft along rivers and coasts.
new-zealand.title: Transport in New Zealand

new-zealand.text: Tourism in New Zealand comprised an important sector of the national economy – tourism directly contributed NZ$16.2 billion of the country's GDP in the year ending March 2019. As of 2016 tourism supported 188,000 full-time-equivalent jobs.
new-zealand.title: Tourism in New Zealand

new-zealand.text: Telecommunications in New Zealand are fairly typical for an industrialised country. Fixed-line broadband and telephone services were largely provided through copper-based networks, but fibre-based services now represent the majority of connections.
new-zealand.title: Telecommunications in New Zealand

new-zealand.text: In New Zealand, agriculture is the largest sector of the tradable economy. The country exported NZ$46.4 billion worth of agricultural products in the 12 months to June 2019, 79.6% of the country's total exported goods.
new-zealand.title: Agriculture in New Zealand

new-zealand.text: Despite abundant natural resources and a relatively small population, New Zealand is a net importer of energy, in the form of petroleum products.
new-zealand.title: Energy in New Zealand

new-zealand.text: Mining in New Zealand began when the Māori quarried rock such as argillite in times prior to European colonisation. Mining by Europeans began in the latter half of the 19th century. New Zealand has abundant resources of coal, silver, iron ore, limestone, and gold.
new-zealand.title: Mining in New Zealand

nicaragua.text: Nicaragua operates nominally as a presidential republic in which the executive serves as both head of state and head of government, but since 2025 it has functioned as a formal co-presidency shared by Daniel Ortega and his wife Rosario Murillo, and as a de jure dictatorship since July 2026, when Ortega announced the country would no longer hold elections.
nicaragua.title: Politics of Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: According to the 2022 revision of the World Population Prospects, Nicaragua has a population of 6,850,540. According to Morera-Bernal the genetic genepool of nicaraguans ir 47% European ancestry, 37%, Indigenous ancestry and 17% African ancestry.
nicaragua.title: Demographics of Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: Education in Nicaragua is free for all Nicaraguans. Elementary education is free and compulsory although this is not strictly enforced. Many children are not able to attend if their families need to have them work.
nicaragua.title: Education in Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: Health in Nicaragua is influenced by several factors including public health policies, the availability of healthcare facilities, environmental influences, individual lifestyle choices, and socioeconomic circumstances. Nicaragua ranks as the second-least affluent nation in the Western Hemisphere.
nicaragua.title: Health in Nicaragua

picture.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Tabla assum

nicaragua.text: The majority of rivers in Nicaragua are located on the Caribbean coast and empty out into the Caribbean Sea. The Río San Juan is one of the most important rivers in Nicaragua, it borders Costa Rica and connects the Caribbean Sea to Lake Cocibolca.
nicaragua.title: List of rivers of Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: The geology of Nicaragua includes Paleozoic crystalline basement rocks, Mesozoic intrusive igneous rocks and sedimentary rocks spanning the Cretaceous to the Pleistocene.
nicaragua.title: Geology of Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: The fauna of Nicaragua is characterized by a very high level of biodiversity. Much of Nicaragua's wildlife lives in protected areas. There are currently 78 protected areas in Nicaragua, covering more than 22,000 square kilometers, or about 17% of its landmass.
nicaragua.title: Fauna of Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: Nicaragua pursues a subordinated foreign policy to Russia and China. A participant of the Central American Security Commission, Nicaragua also has taken a leading role in pressing for regional demilitarization and peaceful settlement of disputes within states in the region.
nicaragua.title: Foreign relations of Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Nicaragua.
nicaragua.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: The Music of Nicaragua contains a mixture of European, Indigenous, and African influences. Occasionally, it also rarely features Asian and Arab musical influences as well as from other countries of Hispanic and Latino origin.
nicaragua.title: Music of Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: Nicaraguan cuisine includes a mixture of Mesoamerican, Chibcha, Spanish, Caribbean, and African cuisine. Despite the blending and incorporation of pre-Columbian, Spanish and African influences, traditional cuisine differs from the western half of Nicaragua to the eastern half.
nicaragua.title: Nicaraguan cuisine

nicaragua.text: This is a list of public holidays in Nicaragua.
nicaragua.title: Public holidays in Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: Religion in Nicaragua is predominantly Christian and forms a significant part of the culture of the country as well as its constitution.
nicaragua.title: Religion in Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: The official language of Nicaragua is Spanish; however, Nicaraguans on the Caribbean coast speak indigenous languages and also English. The communities located on the Caribbean coast also have access to education in their native languages.
nicaragua.title: Languages of Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: Nicaraguan literature can be traced to pre-Columbian times with the myths and oral literature that formed the cosmogonic view of the world that indigenous people had. They told him that of these stories are still known in Nicaragua.
nicaragua.title: Nicaraguan literature

nicaragua.text: Transport in Nicaragua revolves around road, air and water transport modalities.
nicaragua.title: Transport in Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: Tourism in Nicaragua has grown considerably recently, and it is now the second largest industry in the nation. Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega has stated his intention to use tourism to combat poverty throughout the country.
nicaragua.title: Tourism in Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: Telecommunications in Nicaragua include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
nicaragua.title: Telecommunications in Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: Nicaragua produces coffee, cotton, bananas, sugar, and beef cattle.
nicaragua.title: Agriculture in Nicaragua

nicaragua.text: Nicaragua has the 2nd lowest electricity generation in Central America, ahead only of Belize. Nicaragua also possesses the lowest percentage of population with access to electricity.
nicaragua.title: Electricity sector in Nicaragua

niger.text: Politics of Niger takes place in a framework of a semi-presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the President of Niger is head of state and the Prime Minister of Niger head of government, and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government.
niger.title: Politics of Niger

niger.text: The demographic features of Nigeriens, the people of Niger, consist of population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations, and other aspects of the population.
niger.title: Demographics of Niger

niger.text: Education in Niger, as in other nations in the Sahelian region of Africa, faces challenges due to poverty and poor access to schools.
niger.title: Education in Niger

niger.text: Niger is a landlocked country located in West Africa and has Libya, Chad, Nigeria, Benin, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Algeria as its neighboring countries. Niger was French territory that got its independence in 1960 and its official language is French.
niger.title: Health in Niger

niger.text: This is a list of rivers in Niger. This list is arranged by drainage basin, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
niger.title: List of rivers of Niger

niger.text: The geology of Niger comprises very ancient igneous and metamorphic crystalline basement rocks in the west, more than 2.2 billion years old formed in the late Archean and Proterozoic eons of the Precambrian.
niger.title: Geology of Niger

niger.text: The wildlife of Niger is composed of its flora and fauna.
niger.title: Wildlife of Niger
