niger.text: Niger pursues a moderate foreign policy and maintains friendly relations with both East and West. It is a member state of the United Nations. Niger maintains a special relationship with France and enjoys close relations with its West African neighbours.
niger.title: Foreign relations of Niger

niger.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Niger, a former French colony that obtained independence in 1960. Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa named after the Niger River.
niger.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Niger

niger.text: The Music of Niger has developed from the musical traditions of a mix of ethnic groups: Hausa, the Zarma–Songhai, Tuareg, Fula, Kanuri, Toubou, Diffa Arabs and Gurma, as well as the Boudouma from Lake Chad.
niger.title: Music of Niger

niger.text: The cuisine of Niger draws on traditional African cuisines. Various spices are used and meals include grilled meat, seasonal vegetables, salads, and various sauces. Meals in Niger usually start with colorful salads made from seasonal vegetables. Moringa leaves are frequently used in salads.
niger.title: Cuisine of Niger

niger.text: The government and people of Niger observe twelve official public holidays. These include international commemorations, the commemoration of important dates in the history of Niger, and religious holidays. Both Christian and Muslim holidays are observed as official public holidays.
niger.title: Public holidays in Niger

niger.text: According to the 2012 census, Islam is the most followed religion in Niger and is practiced by 99% of the population. According to Pew, roughly 80% of Muslims are Sunni of Maliki school of jurisprudence, whilst 20% are non-denominational Muslims.
niger.title: Religion in Niger

niger.text: The national and official language of Niger is Hausa. French served as the country's official language until 2025 when it was replaced with Hausa as per the transitional charter introduced under Abdourahamane Tiani.
niger.title: Languages of Niger

niger.text: The Cinema of Niger began in the 1940s with the ethnographical documentary of French director Jean Rouch, before growing to become one of the most active national film cultures in Francophone Africa in the 1960s-70s with the work of filmmakers such as Oumarou Ganda, Moustapha Alassane and Gatta Abdourahamne.
niger.title: Cinema of Niger

niger.text: Transport in Niger primarily consists of roads, most of which are unpaved. The state runs one long distance coach service, while other long distance and local routes are run by private companies, using a variety of vehicles. Most Nigeriens do not own vehicles.
niger.title: Transport in Niger

niger.text: There is relatively limited tourism in Niger. Tourism in Niger is also centered on its natural features and historical sites, although the industry itself is relatively underdeveloped. Most of the tourism industry is in the north, where the city of Agadez allows access to the desert.
niger.title: Tourism in Niger

niger.text: Telecommunications in Niger include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
niger.title: Telecommunications in Niger

picture.credit: USDA:Global Crop Production Estimates and Assess

niger.text: Agriculture is the primary economic activity of a majority of Niger's 17 million citizens. The agricultural economy is based largely upon internal markets, subsistence agriculture, and the export of raw commodities: food stuffs and cattle to neighbors.
niger.title: Agriculture in Niger

niger.text: The mineral mining industry is a crucial piece of the economy of Niger. Exports of minerals consistently account for 40% of exports. Mineral commodities produced in Niger included cement, coal, gold, gypsum, limestone, salt, silver, tin, and uranium.
niger.title: Oil and mining industry of Niger

nigeria.text: The federal government of Nigeria is composed of three distinct arms: the executive, the legislative, and the judicial, whose powers are vested and bestowed upon by the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.
nigeria.title: Politics of Nigeria

nigeria.text: Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa and the sixth most populous in the world.
nigeria.title: Demographics of Nigeria

nigeria.text: Education in Nigeria is overseen by the Federal Ministry of Education. Responsibility for education is shared among the federal, state, and local governments. The education system is divided into kindergarten, primary education, secondary education, and tertiary education.
nigeria.title: Education in Nigeria

nigeria.text: In Nigeria, significant progress has been made in health improvement since 1950. However, lower respiratory infections, neonatal disorders, and HIV/AIDS remain the leading causes of death in the country.
nigeria.title: Health in Nigeria

nigeria.text: This is a list of rivers of Nigeria. This list is arranged by drainage basin and from west to east, with respective tributaries indented under each larger stream's name.
nigeria.title: List of rivers of Nigeria

nigeria.text: The geology of Nigeria formed beginning in the Archean and Proterozoic eons of the Precambrian. The country forms the Nigerian Province and more than half of its surface is igneous and metamorphic crystalline basement rock from the Precambrian.
nigeria.title: Geology of Nigeria

nigeria.text: The wildlife of Nigeria consists of the flora and fauna of this country in West Africa. Nigeria has a wide variety of habitats, ranging from mangrove swamps and tropical rainforest to savanna with scattered clumps of trees.
nigeria.title: Wildlife of Nigeria

nigeria.text: The climate of Nigeria is mostly tropical. Nigeria has three distinct climatic zones, two seasons, and an average temperature ranging between 21 °C and 35 °C. Two major elements determine the temperature in Nigeria: the climatic change towards the sun and the atmosphere's transparency.
nigeria.title: Climate of Nigeria

nigeria.text: The Armed Forces of Nigeria are the military forces of Nigeria. The forces consist of three service branches: the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Navy, and Nigerian Air Force.
nigeria.title: Nigerian Armed Forces

nigeria.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Nigeria.
nigeria.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Nigeria

nigeria.text: The music of Nigeria includes many kinds of folk and popular music. Little of the country's music history prior to European contact has been preserved, although bronze carvings dating back to the 16th and 17th centuries have been found depicting musicians and their instruments.
nigeria.title: Music of Nigeria

nigeria.text: Nigerian cuisine consists of dishes or food items from the hundreds of Native African ethnic groups that comprise Nigeria. Like other West African cuisines, it uses spices and herbs with palm oil or groundnut oil to create deeply flavored sauces and soups.
nigeria.title: Nigerian cuisine

nigeria.text: Nigeria has many public holidays declared by the government, as well as special days observed by the public.
nigeria.title: Public holidays in Nigeria

nigeria.text: Islam and Christianity are the two main religions practiced in Nigeria. The country is home to some of the world's largest Muslim and Christian populations, simultaneously.
nigeria.title: Religion in Nigeria

nigeria.text: There are over 520 native languages spoken in Nigeria. The two official languages are English and French.
nigeria.title: Languages of Nigeria

nigeria.text: Before Nigeria was amalgamated in 1914, the people of the Nri Kingdom were the most known for a traditional and cultural theatrical community acting performance. Village squares or market squares where their main stages are prior to most Iri Ji festivals. These acts were categorized precolonial.
nigeria.title: Cinema of Nigeria

nigeria.text: Football is largely considered Nigeria's national sport, and the country has its own professional football league. Basketball is the second sport of Nigeria.
nigeria.title: Sport in Nigeria

nigeria.text: Architecture of Nigeria was historically influenced by environmental conditions as well as social and cultural factors. The coming of missionaries and political changes brought about by colonialism precipitated a change in architectural style and utility of buildings.
nigeria.title: Architecture of Nigeria

nigeria.text: Nigerian literature is a literary writing in Nigeria often by her citizens. It encompasses writers in a number of languages spoken in Nigeria including Igbo, Urhobo, Yoruba, Hausa and Nupe. Things Fall Apart by Chinua Achebe is one of the milestones in African literature.
nigeria.title: Nigerian literature

nigeria.text: Nigeria's transport network has expanded in recent years to accommodate a growing population. The transport and storage sector was valued at N2.6trn in current basic prices in 2020, down from N3trn in 2019, according to the National Bureau of Statistics.
nigeria.title: Transport in Nigeria

nigeria.text: Tourism in Nigeria remains largely untapped, despite the dramatic devaluation of the country’s currency, the naira, in 2023, its numerous attractive sights and its hospitable people.
nigeria.title: Tourism in Nigeria

nigeria.text: Nigeria is Africa's largest ICT market, accounting for 82% of the continent's telecoms subscribers and 29% of internet usage. Globally, Nigeria ranks 11th in the absolute number of internet users and 7th in the absolute number of mobile phones.
nigeria.title: Telecommunications in Nigeria

nigeria.text: Agriculture is a major sector of the Nigerian economy, accounting for up to 35% of total employment in 2020. According to the FAO, agriculture remains the foundation of the Nigerian economy, providing livelihood for most Nigerians and generating millions of jobs.
nigeria.title: Agriculture in Nigeria

nigeria.text: In 2018, Nigeria's primary energy consumption was about 155 Mtoe. Most of the energy comes from traditional biomass and waste, which accounted for 73.5% of total primary consumption in 2018. The rest is from fossil fuels and hydropower.
nigeria.title: Energy in Nigeria

nigeria.text: The mining of minerals in Nigeria accounts for only 0.3% of its gross domestic product, due to the influence of its vast oil resources. The domestic mining industry is underdeveloped, leading to Nigeria having to import minerals that it could produce domestically, such as salt or iron ore.
nigeria.title: Mining industry of Nigeria

niue.text: The politics of Niue take place in a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic dependency, whereby the Prime Minister is the head of government, and of a non-partisan system. Niue is self-governing in free association with New Zealand and is fully responsible for internal affairs.
niue.title: Politics of Niue

niue.text: Niue maintains diplomatic relations with various other countries and multilateral organisations. Since 1974, Niue has been a self-governing state in free association with New Zealand. The King in right of New Zealand is the head of state of Niue, making Niue part of the Realm of New Zealand.
niue.title: Foreign relations of Niue

niue.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Niue. Niue is an island country in the South Pacific Ocean. It is commonly known as the "Rock of Polynesia", and inhabitants of the island call it "the Rock" for short.
niue.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Niue

niue.text: The music of Niue has a long history. Niue is a Polynesian island in the South Pacific. Though independent, it is in free association with New Zealand.
niue.title: Music of Niue

niue.text: Niue is an island in the Southern Pacific, mostly inhabited by Polynesians. The plantations are mostly filled with manioc, taro and breadfruit, but banana trees can be found.
niue.title: Niuean cuisine

niue.text: This is a list of holidays in Niue.
niue.title: Public holidays in Niue

niue.text: Niuean is a Polynesian language, belonging to the Malayo-Polynesian subgroup of the Austronesian languages. It is most closely related to Tongan and slightly more distantly to other Polynesian languages such as Māori, Samoan and Hawaiian.
niue.title: Niuean language

niue.text: Transport in Niue takes place on a road network, and via an airport and a sea port. A ring road around the island's coast is the major route, and roads cross the central plateau linking Alofi to the villages of Lakepa, Liku and Hakupu on the opposite coast.
niue.title: Transport in Niue

niue.text: Communications in Niue include postal, telephone, internet, press and radio.
niue.title: Communications in Niue

north-korea.text: The politics of North Korea takes place within the framework of the official state philosophy, Kimilsungism–Kimjongilism. Juche, a part of the philosophy, is the belief that true socialism is achieved only through self-reliance and a strong independent state.
north-korea.title: Politics of North Korea

north-korea.text: The demographics of North Korea are determined through national censuses and international estimates. The Central Bureau of Statistics of North Korea conducted the most recent census in 2008, where the population reached 24 million inhabitants.
north-korea.title: Demographics of North Korea

north-korea.text: Education in North Korea is universal and state-funded schooling by the government. As of 2021, UNESCO Institute for Statistics does not report any data for North Korea's literacy rates.
north-korea.title: Education in North Korea

picture.credit: Attribution to (Stephan) at Flickr and http://nk

north-korea.text: North Korea has a life expectancy of 74 years as of 2024. While North Korea is classified as a low-income country, the structure of North Korea's causes of death is unlike that of other low-income countries.
north-korea.title: Health in North Korea

north-korea.text: The geology of North Korea has been studied by the Central Geological Survey of Mineral Resources, rare international research, and by inference from South Korea's geology. The oldest rocks are Precambrian in age, with basement gneisses and metamorphic supergroups dating back over two billion years.
north-korea.title: Geology of North Korea

north-korea.text: The following is a list of mountains in Korea:
north-korea.title: List of mountains in Korea

north-korea.text: North Korea has diplomatic relations with 160 states. In the past, the country's foreign relations were marked by its conflict with South Korea and its historical ties to the Soviet Union.
north-korea.title: Foreign relations of North Korea

north-korea.text: Postage stamps are issued by the Korea Stamp Corporation. North Korea issues copious amounts of stamps. Since the 1970s, the country has outproduced South Korea in terms of issuance.
north-korea.title: Postage stamps and postal history of North Korea

north-korea.text: The music of North Korea includes a wide array of folk, popular, light instrumental, political, and classical performers.
north-korea.title: Music of North Korea

picture.credit: Stefan Krasowski from New York, NY, USA

north-korea.text: North Korean cuisine is the traditional culinary practices and dishes of North Korea. Its foundations are laid by the agricultural and nomadic traditions in southern Manchuria and the Korean Peninsula.
north-korea.title: North Korean cuisine

north-korea.text: This is a list of public holidays in North Korea, known as myŏngjŏl. See also the Korean calendar for a list of traditional holidays. As of 2017, the North Korean calendar has 71 official public holidays, including Sundays.
north-korea.title: Public holidays in North Korea

north-korea.text: There are no known official statistics of religions in North Korea. Officially, North Korea is an atheist state, although its constitution guarantees free exercise of religion, provided that religious practice does not introduce foreign forces, harm the state, or harm the existing social order.
north-korea.title: Religion in North Korea

picture.credit: Photo by John Pavelka. Mural: Mansudae Art Studi

north-korea.text: The cinema of North Korea began with the division of Korea and has been sustained since then by the ruling Kim dynasty. Kim Il Sung and his successor Kim Jong Il were both cinephiles and sought to produce propaganda films based on the Juche ideology.
north-korea.title: Cinema of North Korea

north-korea.text: Historically, North Korea's participation in international sporting events has been hindered by the relations with South Korea. Until the 1990s, North Korea used to host up to 14 international events every year, albeit in small scale.
north-korea.title: Sport in North Korea

picture.credit: Attribution to (Stephan) at Flickr and http://nk

north-korea.text: Reading is a popular pastime in North Korea, where literacy and books enjoy a high cultural standing, elevated by the regime's efforts to disseminate propaganda as texts. Because of this, writers are held in high prestige.
north-korea.title: North Korean literature

picture.credit: Department of Defense. Department of the Army. O

north-korea.text: Transport in North Korea is constrained by economic problems and government restrictions. Public transport predominates, and most of it is electrified.
north-korea.title: Transport in North Korea

north-korea.text: Tourism in North Korea is tightly controlled by the North Korean government.
north-korea.title: Tourism in North Korea

north-korea.text: Telecommunications in North Korea refers to the communication services available in North Korea. North Korea has not fully adopted mainstream Internet technology due to some restrictions on foreign interventions.
north-korea.title: Telecommunications in North Korea

north-korea.text: Farming in North Korea is concentrated in the flatlands of the four west coast provinces, where a longer growing season, level land, adequate rainfall, and good irrigated soil permit the most intensive cultivation of crops.
north-korea.title: Agriculture in North Korea

north-korea.text: Energy in North Korea describes energy and electricity production, consumption and import in North Korea. Primary energy use in North Korea was 224 TWh and 9 TWh per million people in 2009.
north-korea.title: Energy in North Korea

north-korea.text: Mining in North Korea is important to the country's economy. North Korea is naturally abundant in metals such as magnesite, zinc, tungsten, and iron; with magnesite resources of 6 billion tonnes, particularly in the North and South Hamgyong Provinces, as well as the Chagang Province.
north-korea.title: Mining in North Korea

north-macedonia.text: Politics in North Macedonia occur within the framework of a parliamentary representative democratic republic, whereby the Prime Minister is the head of government, and of a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government.
north-macedonia.title: Politics of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: Demographic features of the population of North Macedonia include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population.
north-macedonia.title: Demographics of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: The Constitution of North Macedonia mandates free and compulsory primary and secondary education in the Republic of North Macedonia, and the Law on Primary Education specifies that all children from 6 to 15 years of age attend school for a compulsory 9 years.
north-macedonia.title: Education in North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: Health in North Macedonia is improving. The life expectancy of North Macedonia in 2016 was 74 for men and 78 for women. In 2015 it was estimated that 11.44% of the population of North Macedonia had diabetes, costing about $403 per person per year.
north-macedonia.title: Health in North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: This is a list of rivers of North Macedonia.
north-macedonia.title: List of rivers of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: The geology of North Macedonia includes the study of rocks dating to the Precambrian and a wide array of volcanic, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks formed in the last 539 million years.
north-macedonia.title: Geology of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: Over 22,500 species of wildlife have been recorded in North Macedonia. Over 10,000 of these are insects, which include 3,000 beetle species and large numbers of Lepidoptera, flies, and Hymenoptera. Aside from insects, other large arthropod groups include Chelicerata and crustaceans.
north-macedonia.title: Wildlife of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: The following is a list of mountains in North Macedonia. North Macedonia is a predominantly mountainous country. The average elevation of the terrain is 850 meters. Approximately 80% of the country consists of hills and mountains.
north-macedonia.title: List of mountains in North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: The foreign relations of North Macedonia since its independence in 1991 have been characterized by the country's efforts to gain membership in international organizations such as NATO and the European Union and to gain international recognition under its previous constitutional name, overshadowed by a long-standing, dead-locked dispute with neighboring Greece.
north-macedonia.title: Foreign relations of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: The military history of North Macedonia spans from the beginning of World War II until the conflict with ethnic Albanian militants, such as the 2001 Macedonia conflict. The country also contributed troops in the war on terror.
north-macedonia.title: Military history of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of North Macedonia. The Republic of North Macedonia, until February 2019 the Republic of Macedonia, is a country located in the central Balkan Peninsula in Southeastern Europe.
north-macedonia.title: Postage stamps and postal history of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: The music of North Macedonia refers to all forms of music associated with North Macedonia and its people. It shares similarities with the music of neighbouring Balkan countries, yet it remains overall distinctive in its rhythm and sound.
north-macedonia.title: Music of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: Macedonian cuisine is the cuisine of North Macedonia. It is influenced by Ottoman and Balkan cuisines. The relatively warm climate of the country provides excellent growth conditions for a variety of vegetables, herbs and fruits.
north-macedonia.title: Macedonian cuisine

north-macedonia.text: Public holidays are observed in the Republic of North Macedonia for a number of reasons, including religious and national significance. They are generally accompanied by celebrations. The holidays are regulated by the 1998 Law on Holidays.
north-macedonia.title: Public holidays in North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: In North Macedonia, the most common religion is Orthodox Christianity, practiced mainly by Macedonians, Serbs, and Aromanians. The vast majority of the Eastern Orthodox in the country belong to the Macedonian Orthodox Church, which declared autocephaly from the Serbian Orthodox Church in 1967.
north-macedonia.title: Religion in North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: The official language of North Macedonia is Macedonian, while Albanian has co-official status. Macedonian is spoken by roughly two-thirds of the population natively, and as a second language by much of the rest of the population. Albanian is the largest minority language.
north-macedonia.title: Languages of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: Cinema of North Macedonia refers to film industry based in North Macedonia or any motion-picture made by Macedonians abroad. Janaki and Milton Manaki are considered the founding fathers. The first feature film produced by the country was Frosina and the most famous director is Milčo Mančevski.
north-macedonia.title: Cinema of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: The groups of people who have settled or controlled the territory of modern-day North Macedonia have influenced the country in many ways, one of the most visible being architecture.
north-macedonia.title: Architecture of North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: Macedonian literature begins with the Ohrid Literary School in the First Bulgarian Empire in 886. These first written works in the dialects of the Old Church Slavonic were religious. The school was established by St. Clement of Ohrid.
north-macedonia.title: Macedonian literature

north-macedonia.text: The following is a summary of the transport system of the Republic of North Macedonia.
north-macedonia.title: Transport in North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: Tourism in North Macedonia is a large factor of the nation's economy. The country's large abundance of natural and cultural attractions make it suitable for tourism. In 2019, North Macedonia received 1,184,963 tourist arrivals out of which 757,593 were foreign.
north-macedonia.title: Tourism in North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: Telecommunications in North Macedonia include radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, telegraph and the Internet.
north-macedonia.title: Telecommunications in North Macedonia

north-macedonia.text: Agriculture in North Macedonia provides a livelihood for a fifth of the country's population, where half live in a rural area. Industrialisation of the country was very delayed, due to the long Ottoman domination, and then destruction from World War I and Serbian occupation.
north-macedonia.title: Agriculture in North Macedonia

northern-mariana-islands.text: Politics of the Northern Mariana Islands takes place in a framework of a presidential representative democratic system, whereby the Governor is head of government, and of a pluriform multi-party system.
northern-mariana-islands.title: Politics of the Northern Mariana Islands

northern-mariana-islands.text: The demographics of the Northern Mariana Islands encompass the population characteristics of the Northern Mariana Islands, including population size and age structure, births and deaths, ethnic composition, languages, and religion.
northern-mariana-islands.title: Demographics of the Northern Mariana Islands

northern-mariana-islands.text: Education in the Northern Mariana Islands is linked to the United States Department of Education as the Northern Mariana Islands form part of the United States Commonwealth. This encompasses the sectors of pre-K, elementary schools, middle schools, high schools and college education.
northern-mariana-islands.title: Education in the Northern Mariana Islands

northern-mariana-islands.text: The geology of the Northern Mariana Islands began to form with undersea volcanic eruptions in the Eocene. Islands such as Saipan show a variety of rock types including volcanic rocks, breccia, tuff, conglomerate, sandstone, clay and extensive limestones.
northern-mariana-islands.title: Geology of the Northern Mariana Islands

northern-mariana-islands.text: The music of the Northern Mariana Islands is dominated by the folk music of the Chamorros, which remains an important part of the islands' culture, though elements of music left by American, German, Spanish and Japanese colonizers are also in evidence.
northern-mariana-islands.title: Music of the Northern Mariana Islands

norway.text: The politics of Norway takes place in the framework of a parliamentary, representative democratic constitutional monarchy. Executive power is exercised by the king, Council of State, and the cabinet, led by the prime minister.
norway.title: Politics of Norway

norway.text: Demographic features of the population of Norway, including Jan Mayen, and Svalbard, where the hospital is not equipped for births, and no burials are allowed because of permafrost, include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects.
norway.title: Demographics of Norway

norway.text: Education in Norway is mandatory for all children aged from 6 to 16. Schools are typically divided into two divisions: primary and lower secondary schooling. The majority of schools in Norway are municipal, where local governments fund and manage administration.
norway.title: Education in Norway

norway.text: Health in Norway, with its early history of poverty and infectious diseases along with famines and epidemics, was poor for most of the population at least into the 1800s. The country eventually changed from a peasant society to an industrial one and established a public health system in 1860.
norway.title: Health in Norway

norway.text: The geology of Norway encompasses the history of Earth that can be interpreted by rock types found in Norway, and the associated sedimentological history of soils and rock types. The Norwegian mountains were formed around 400 million years ago during the Caledonian orogeny.
norway.title: Geology of Norway

norway.text: The wildlife of Norway includes the diverse flora and fauna of Norway. The habitats include high mountains, tundras, rivers, lakes, wetlands, sea coast and some lower cultivated land in the south.
norway.title: Wildlife of Norway

norway.text: There are 291 peaks in Norway with elevations of over 2,000 metres above sea level and that have a topographic prominence of more than 10 m. The following list includes those 186 that have a topographic prominence of 50 m or more.
norway.title: List of mountains in Norway by height

norway.text: The climate of Norway is more temperate than expected for high latitudes.
norway.title: Climate of Norway

norway.text: The foreign relations of Norway are based on the country's membership in NATO and within the workings of the United Nations. Additionally, despite not being a member of the European Union, Norway takes a part in the integration of EU through its membership in the European Economic Area.
norway.title: Foreign relations of Norway

norway.text: The military history of Norway commences before the Viking Age with the internal wars fought between regional kings to obtain the supreme kingship of the whole of Norway.
norway.title: Military history of Norway

norway.text: The postal system of Norway dates from 1647, when Christian IV of Denmark–Norway granted a concession to a private company who established the Postvesenet. The Postvesenet primarily provided a way for various parts of the country to communicate with the central government in Christiania.
norway.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Norway

norway.text: Much has been learned about early music in Norway from physical artifacts found during archaeological digs. These include instruments such as the lur.
norway.title: Music of Norway

norway.text: Norwegian cuisine in its traditional form is based largely on the raw materials readily available in Norway. It differs in many respects from continental cuisine with a stronger focus on game and fish.
norway.title: Norwegian cuisine

norway.text: Public holidays in Norway are regulated by the Norwegian Annual Holiday Act, which was amended in 2014 to include workers employed in the mining and fishing industries, as well as all public and private sectors.
norway.title: Public holidays in Norway

norway.text: Religion in Norway is dominated by Lutheran Christianity, with 61.7% of the population belonging to the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Norway in 2024. The Catholic Church is the next largest Christian church at 3.1%. The growing group of unaffiliated made up 18.3% of the population in 2019.
norway.title: Religion in Norway

norway.text: Many languages are spoken, written and signed in Norway. In Norway, the indigenous languages, Norwegian and Sámi, have official status. Out of them, Norwegian is the most widely spoken language in Norway. English, a foreign language, is the second most widely spoken language in Norway.
norway.title: Languages of Norway

norway.text: Cinema in Norway has a long history, dating back to the beginning of the 20th century, and has an important stance in European cinema, contributing at least 30 feature-length films a year. There have been over 1,050 films made in Norway ever since cinema's first introduction to the country in 1907.
norway.title: Cinema of Norway

norway.text: The architecture of Norway has evolved in response to changing economic conditions, technological advances, demographic fluctuations and cultural shifts.
norway.title: Architecture of Norway

norway.text: Norwegian literature is literature composed in Norway or by Norwegian people. The history of Norwegian literature starts with the pagan Eddaic poems and skaldic verse of the 9th and 10th centuries with poets such as Bragi Boddason and Eyvindr Skáldaspillir.
norway.title: Norwegian literature

norway.text: For much of its history, Norwegian art is usually considered as part of the wider Nordic art of Scandinavia. It has, especially since about 1100 AD, been strongly influenced by wider trends in European art. After World War II, the influence of the United States strengthened substantially.
norway.title: Norwegian art

norway.text: Transport in Norway is highly influenced by Norway's low population density, narrow shape and rugged coastline. Norway has old water transport traditions, but road, rail and air transport have increased in importance during the 20th century.
norway.title: Transport in Norway

norway.text: As of 2019, Norway ranks 22nd in the World Economic Forum's Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Report. Tourism in Norway contributed 4.2% of the gross domestic product as reported in 2018. Every seven in a hundred people throughout the country work in the tourism industry.
norway.title: Tourism in Norway

norway.text: Telecommunications in Norway are relatively advanced. There are about as many cellular phone subscription as there are inhabitants in the country, while the number of fixed line telephone subscriptions is declining towards 800,000.
norway.title: Telecommunications in Norway

norway.text: Norway is a large energy producer, and one of the world's largest exporters of oil. Most of the electricity in the country is produced by hydroelectricity.
norway.title: Energy in Norway

norway.text: The Norwegian Directorate of Mining with the Commissioner of Mines at Svalbard is a Norwegian government agency responsible for administrating the extraction of mineral resources within the kingdom.
norway.title: Norwegian Directorate of Mining

oman.text: The Politics of Oman take place in the context of a unitary absolute monarchy, where the Sultan of Oman is both head of state and head of government. The Sultan is hereditary, who appoints a cabinet to assist him.
oman.title: Politics of Oman

oman.text: Demographics of the population of Oman include population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects.
oman.title: Demographics of Oman

oman.text: Education in Oman is provided free of charge up to end of secondary education, though attendance is not mandatory at any level. In 1970 there were only three formal schools with 900 students in the whole state.
oman.title: Education in Oman

oman.text: Life expectancy at birth in 2013 was 74 for men and 79 for women.
oman.title: Health in Oman

oman.text: This is a list of wadis in Oman arranged by drainage basin.
oman.title: List of wadis of Oman

oman.text: The geology of Oman includes varied landscapes which are a blend of its geological history, and its climate over the past few million years. Rock outcrops in the Hajar, Huqf and Dhofar Mountains are a point of interest for international geologists.
oman.title: Geology of Oman

oman.text: The wildlife of Oman is the flora and fauna of this country in the southeastern corner of the Arabian Peninsula, with coasts on the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.
oman.title: Wildlife of Oman

oman.text: Although much of the country has a desert or semi-desert and relatively flat territory, Oman has mountains that include the Hajar Mountains, located in the northeast of Oman and the far northeast of the United Arab Emirates.
oman.title: List of mountains in Oman

oman.text: When Sultan Qaboos bin Said Al Said assumed power in 1970, Oman had limited contacts with the outside world, including neighbouring Arab states. A special treaty relationship permitted the United Kingdom close involvement in Oman's civil and military affairs.
oman.title: Foreign relations of Oman

oman.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Muscat and Oman, including the present day Sultanate of Oman.
oman.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Muscat and Oman

oman.text: The Music of Oman has been strongly affected by the country's coastal location with a diverse mix of outside influences and its own traditional Eastern, Southern Arabian, and overall Khaleeji Gulf musical tradition.
oman.title: Music of Oman

oman.text: Omani cuisine is part of the Khaleeji cuisine and is influenced by Arab, Indian, Iranian, Asian, Greek, and African cuisine, reflecting Oman's position as a vast trading empire at the intersection of traditional spice trade routes.
oman.title: Omani cuisine

oman.text: The following is a list of public holidays in Oman. National Day - November 20th: Celebrates the date of the founding of the Al Bu Said dynasty, which has ruled Oman since 1744.
oman.title: Public holidays in Oman

oman.text: The government of Oman does not keep statistics on religious affiliation. According to the CIA World Factbook, as of 2020, Muslims are in the majority at 85.9%, with Christians at 6.4%, Hindu at 5.7%, and other religious affiliations and unaffiliated at 2%.
oman.title: Religion in Oman

oman.text: The cinema of Oman is very small. There is only one Omani film, Al-Boom, as of 2007. Partly inspired by Samuel Beckett's Waiting For Godot, Al-Boom deals with the challenges facing a small fishing community.
oman.title: Cinema of Oman

oman.text: This article is about transport in Oman.
oman.title: Transport in Oman

oman.text: Oman is a country on the Arabian Peninsula. Tourism in Oman grew considerably during the 2000s, and a 2013 report predicted that it would become one of the largest industries in the nation.
oman.title: Tourism in Oman

oman.text: Oman Telecommunication Company has a monopoly in the landline telephone and internet access markets. Its arm Omanmobile offers mobile services. The Omani government owns 70% of Omantel after 30% was listed for the public in 2005.
oman.title: Telecommunications in Oman

oman.text: Agriculture in Oman has been important for centuries. The government's economic development policy emphasizes the expansion of such non-oil sectors as agriculture, fishing, industry, and mining in its bid to diversify the economy and diminish its dependence on oil exports.
oman.title: Agriculture in Oman

oman.text: Energy use in Oman was 381 TWh in 2020, almost double the consumption in 2010.
oman.title: Energy in Oman

pakistan.text: The Politics of Pakistan takes place within the framework established by the constitution. The country is a federal parliamentary republic in which provincial governments enjoy a high degree of autonomy and residuary powers.
pakistan.title: Politics of Pakistan

pakistan.text: Pakistan had a population of 247,541,947 according to the final results of the 2023 Pakistani census.
pakistan.title: Demographics of Pakistan

pakistan.text: Education in Pakistan is administered by the Federal Ministry of Education and the provincial governments.
pakistan.title: Education in Pakistan

pakistan.text: Pakistan is the fifth most populous country in the world with population approaching 225 million. It is a developing country struggling in many domains due to which the health system has suffered a lot.
pakistan.title: Health in Pakistan

pakistan.text: This is a list of rivers wholly or partly in Pakistan, organised geographically by river basin, from west to east. Tributaries are listed from the mouth to the source. The longest and the largest river in Pakistan is the Indus River.
pakistan.title: List of rivers of Pakistan

pakistan.text: The geology of Pakistan encompasses the varied landscapes that make up the land constituting modern-day Pakistan, which are a blend of its geological history, and its climate over the past few million years.
pakistan.title: Geology of Pakistan

pakistan.text: The wildlife of Pakistan comprises a diverse flora and fauna across a wide range of habitats, from sea level to high-elevation areas in the mountains, including 195 mammal species, 668 bird species, and more than 5,000 species of invertebrates.
pakistan.title: Wildlife of Pakistan

pakistan.text: Pakistan is home to 108 peaks above 7,000 metres and 4555[1] above 6,000 m. There is no count of the peaks above 5,000 and 4,000 m. Five of the 14 highest independent peaks in the world are in Pakistan.
pakistan.title: List of mountains in Pakistan

pakistan.text: Pakistan's climate varies from a continental type of climate in the north, a mountainous dry climate in the west, a wet climate in the East an arid climate in the Thar Desert, to a tropical climate in the southeast, characterized by extreme variations in temperature, both seasonally and daily, because it is located on a great landmass barely north of the Tropic of Cancer.
pakistan.title: Climate of Pakistan

pakistan.text: The Islamic Republic of Pakistan emerged as an independent country through the partition of India in August 1947 and was admitted as a United Nations member state in September 1947.
pakistan.title: Foreign relations of Pakistan

pakistan.text: The military history of Pakistan covers the development, organization, and operations of the Pakistan Armed Forces from the country's creation in 1947 to the present day.
pakistan.title: Military history of Pakistan

pakistan.text: Postage stamps of Pakistan are those issued since Pakistan's independence in 1947. Pakistan Post has issued more than 600 sets and singles totalling more than 1300 stamps.
pakistan.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Pakistan

pakistan.text: The Music of Pakistan includes South Asian, Central Asian, Middle Eastern and contemporary Western influences. The genre has adapted and evolved over time in response to shifting cultural norms and global influences. It has been shaped by Persian, Arab and Turkish traditions among others.
pakistan.title: Music of Pakistan

pakistan.text: Pakistani cuisine encompasses the traditional and regional foods of Pakistan and its diaspora, Central and West Asia. Pakistan's ethnic and cultural diversity, diverse climates, geographical environments, and availability of different produce lead to diverse regional cuisines.
pakistan.title: Pakistani cuisine

pakistan.text: Holidays in Pakistan are celebrated according to the Islamic or Gregorian calendars for religious and civil purposes, respectively.
pakistan.title: Public holidays in Pakistan

pakistan.text: The official religion of Pakistan is Islam, as enshrined by article 2 of the Constitution, and is practiced by an overwhelming majority of 96.35% of the Pakistani population. The remaining 3.65% are followers of Hinduism, Christianity, Ahmadiyya, Sikhism and Zoroastrianism.
pakistan.title: Religion in Pakistan

pakistan.text: Pakistan is a multilingual country with over 70 languages spoken as first languages. The majority of Pakistan's languages belong to the Indo-Iranian group of the Indo-European language family.
pakistan.title: Languages of Pakistan

pakistan.text: The film industry of Pakistan, consisting of motion pictures, has had a large effect on Pakistani society and culture since the nation's independence. The film industry in Pakistan is centred in three main cities: Lahore, Karachi and Peshawar.
pakistan.title: Cinema of Pakistan

pakistan.text: Sport in Pakistan is a significant part of Pakistani culture. Cricket is the most popular sport in Pakistan. Football has also gained popularity in recent years, and is the second most popular sport in the country.
pakistan.title: Sport in Pakistan

pakistan.text: Pakistani architecture is intertwined with the architecture of the broader Indian subcontinent. Major historical architectural styles include Hindu temple, Buddhist, Jain, Indo-Islamic, Mughal and Indo-Saracenic architecture, all of which have many regional varieties.
pakistan.title: Pakistani architecture

pakistan.text: Pakistani literature is a distinct literature that gradually came to be defined after Pakistan gained nationhood status in 1947, emerging out of literary traditions of the Indian subcontinent.
pakistan.title: Pakistani literature

pakistan.text: Pakistani art has a long tradition and history. It consists of a variety of art forms, including painting, sculpture, calligraphy, pottery, and textile arts such as woven silk.
pakistan.title: Pakistani art

pakistan.text: Transport in Pakistan is extensive and varied. In the early 21st century new national highways and motorways were built, which improved trade and logistics within the country. Pakistan's rail network was also expanded. Airports and seaports have been built with foreign and domestic funding.
pakistan.title: Transport in Pakistan

pakistan.text: Tourism in Pakistan is a growing industry. Pakistan was a stop along the Hippie trail from the mid-1950s to the late 1970s. In 2010, Lonely Planet termed Pakistan "tourism's 'next big thing'".
pakistan.title: Tourism in Pakistan

pakistan.text: Telecommunications in Pakistan describes the overall environment for the mobile telecommunications, telephone, and Internet markets in Pakistan.
pakistan.title: Telecommunications in Pakistan

pakistan.text: Agriculture is considered the backbone of Pakistan's economy, which relies heavily on its major crops. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization, agriculture contributes approximately 23% of GDP and employs 37.4% of the national labour force.
pakistan.title: Agriculture in Pakistan

pakistan.text: The energy policy of Pakistan is formulated and determined by the federal, provincial, and local institutional entities in Pakistan, which address the issues of energy production, distribution, and consumption of energy, such as gas mileage and petroleum standards.
pakistan.title: Energy policy of Pakistan

pakistan.text: Mining is an important industry in Pakistan. Pakistan has deposits of several minerals including coal, copper, gold, chromite, mineral salt, bauxite and several other minerals. There are also a variety of precious and semi-precious minerals that are also mined.
pakistan.title: Mining in Pakistan

palau.text: The politics of Palau take place in a presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the President of Palau is both head of state and head of government.
palau.title: Politics of Palau

palau.text: Demographic features of the population of Palau include population density, ethnicity, education level, the health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations and other aspects. About 70% of the Palauan population lives in the city of Koror on Koror Island.
palau.title: Demographics of Palau

palau.text: This is a list of the rivers of Palau, all of which are located on Babeldaob. They are listed in clockwise order, starting at the north end of the island. Alternate names are given in parentheses.
palau.title: List of rivers of Palau

palau.text: For information on the wildlife of Palau, see: List of birds of Palau List of mammals of Palau
palau.title: Wildlife of Palau

palau.text: Palau gained its independence October 1, 1994 with the entry into force of the Compact of Free Association with the United States. Palau was the last Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands territories to gain its independence.
palau.title: Foreign relations of Palau

palau.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Palau. The Republic of Palau is an island nation in the Pacific Ocean, 500 miles east of the Philippines and 2,000 miles south of Tokyo, forming the westernmost part of the Caroline Islands.
palau.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Palau

palau.text: The music of Palau finds its heritage in Micronesia, but it has been supplemented with influences from the United States and Western Europe, as well as Japan.
palau.title: Music of Palau

palau.text: This is a list of holidays in Palau.
palau.title: Public holidays in Palau

palau.text: Christianity is the dominant religion in Palau, practiced by around 72.8% of the total population, according to the 2022 census. Freedom of religion is enshrined in Palau's constitution.
palau.title: Religion in Palau

panama.text: The politics of Panama take place in a framework of a presidential representative democratic republic with a multi-party system, whereby the President of Panama is both head of state and head of the government of Panama. Executive power is exercised by the president.
panama.title: Politics of Panama

panama.text: This is a demography of the population of Panama including population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations, and other aspects of the population.
panama.title: Demographics of Panama

panama.text: Education in Panama is compulsory for the first six years of primary education and the first three years of secondary school. However, a high proportion of students complete an additional 3 years in secondary school, for a total of 6 years in secondary school.
panama.title: Education in Panama

panama.text: Even though Panama has one of the fastest growing economies in the western hemisphere, an estimated 500,000 people are in extreme poverty. Panama has major socioeconomic and health inequalities between the country's urban and rural populations.
panama.title: Health in Panama

panama.text: This is a list of rivers in Panama.
panama.title: List of rivers of Panama

panama.text: The geology of Panama includes the complex tectonic interplay between the Pacific, Cocos and Nazca plates, the Caribbean Plate and the Panama Microplate.
panama.title: Geology of Panama

panama.text: Panama's foreign relations are conventional in outlook, with Panama being especially aligned with United States since the 1989 US invasion to topple the regime of General Manuel Noriega.
panama.title: Foreign relations of Panama

panama.text: Panama was formerly a department of Colombia and used overprints of Colombian stamps from 1878 until it gained independence in 1903.
panama.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Panama

panama.text: Panama is a Central American country, inhabited mostly by mestizos.
panama.title: Music of Panama

panama.text: Panamanian cuisine is a mix of Spanish, Indigenous, and African techniques, dishes, and ingredients, reflecting its diverse population. Since Panama is a land bridge between two continents, it has a large variety of tropical fruits, vegetables and herbs that are used in native cooking.
panama.title: Panamanian cuisine

panama.text: The predominant religion in Panama is Christianity, with Catholic Church being its largest denomination. Before the arrival of Spanish missionaries, the various ethnic groups residing in the territory of modern-day Panama practiced a multitude of faiths.
panama.title: Religion in Panama

panama.text: Panamanian literature comprises the whole of literary works written in Panama. The first literature relating to Panama can be dated to 1535, with a modern literary movement appearing from the mid-19th century onwards
panama.title: Panamanian literature

panama.text: Transport in Panama covers a vast network of routes predominantly traversed by cargo trucks and buses. The country's railway system, known as the Panama Canal Railway, facilitates the transportation of both passengers and goods.
panama.title: Transport in Panama

panama.text: Tourism in Panama represents one of Panama‘s main activities. The main areas of tourism in the country focus on business tourism, beaches, health and trade. Most of the tourists come from the United States, Canada, Europe, Central America, and South America.
panama.title: Tourism in Panama

panama.text: Telecommunications in Panama includes radio, television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
panama.title: Telecommunications in Panama

panama.text: Agriculture in Panama is an important sector of the Panamanian economy. Major agricultural products include bananas, cocoa beans, coffee, coconuts, timber, beef, chicken, shrimp, corn, potatoes, rice, soybeans, and sugar cane. In 2009 agriculture and fisheries made up 7.4% of Panama's GDP.
panama.title: Agriculture in Panama

panama.text: The mineral-mining industry of Panama accounted for about 1% of the country's GDP in 2006. This does not include any manufacturing of mineral commodities, such as cement or petroleum refinery products.
panama.title: Mineral industry of Panama

papua-new-guinea.text: The politics of Papua New Guinea takes place in a framework of a parliamentary representative democratic multi-party system, whereby the prime minister is the head of government.
papua-new-guinea.title: Politics of Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: The indigenous population of Papua New Guinea is one of the most heterogeneous in the world. Papua New Guinea has several thousand separate communities, most with only a few hundred people.
papua-new-guinea.title: Demographics of Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: Education in Papua New Guinea is managed through nineteen provinces and two district organisational units. It is tuition-free and attendance is not compulsory.
papua-new-guinea.title: Education in Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: Life expectancy in Papua New Guinea at birth was 64 years for men in 2016 and 68 for women, markedly lower than neighbouring countries: Indonesia, 67 and 71; Australia, 81 and 85.
papua-new-guinea.title: Health in Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: This is a list of rivers of Papua New Guinea.
papua-new-guinea.title: List of rivers of Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: Papua New Guinea's foreign policy reflects close ties with Australia and other traditional allies and cooperative relations with neighboring countries. Its views on international political and economic issues are generally moderate.
papua-new-guinea.title: Foreign relations of Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: The postage stamps and postal history of Papua New Guinea originated in the two colonial administrations on the eastern part of the island of New Guinea and continued until their eventual merger, followed by independence in 1975.
papua-new-guinea.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: The music of Papua New Guinea has a long history.
papua-new-guinea.title: Music of Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: The cuisine of Papua New Guinea comprises the traditional varied foods found in the eastern part of the New Guinea island.
papua-new-guinea.title: Papua New Guinean cuisine

papua-new-guinea.text: This is a list of holidays in Papua New Guinea.
papua-new-guinea.title: Public holidays in Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: Religion in Papua New Guinea is dominated by various branches of Christianity, with traditional animism and ancestor worship often occurring less openly as another layer underneath or more openly side by side with Christianity. The Catholic Church has a plurality of the population.
papua-new-guinea.title: Religion in Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: Papua New Guinea, a sovereign state in Oceania, is the most linguistically diverse country in the world. Ethnologue, among other sources, state that there are 840 living languages spoken in the country, although estimates vary due to the distinction between a language and a dialect.
papua-new-guinea.title: Languages of Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: Sport in Papua New Guinea is an important part of the national culture. Rugby league is the most popular sport in Papua New Guinea. Other popular sports include most football codes cricket, volleyball, softball, netball, and basketball.
papua-new-guinea.title: Sport in Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: Papua New Guinean literature is diverse. The emergence of written literature is comparatively recent in Papua New Guinea. It was given its first major stimulus with the setting up of creative writing courses by Ulli Beier at the University of Papua New Guinea.
papua-new-guinea.title: Papua New Guinean literature

papua-new-guinea.text: Papua New Guinean art refers to visual art created in Papua New Guinea or by Papua New Guinean artists.
papua-new-guinea.title: Papua New Guinean art

papua-new-guinea.text: Transport in Papua New Guinea is mainly based around roads and air travel. It is in many cases heavily limited by the mountainous terrain and copious amount of rainfall and frequent severe weather occurring in many locations, such as Lae.
papua-new-guinea.title: Transport in Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: Tourism in Papua New Guinea is a fledgling industry but there are attractions for the potential visitor which include culture, markets, festivals, diving, surfing, hiking, fishing and the unique flora and fauna.
papua-new-guinea.title: Tourism in Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: Communications in Papua New Guinea refers to the media in the country which are regulated by the Media Council of Papua New Guinea such as newspapers, radio, television, and the Internet.
papua-new-guinea.title: Communications in Papua New Guinea

papua-new-guinea.text: Agriculture in Papua New Guinea has more than a 7,000 years old history, and developed out of pre-agricultural plant/food collecting and cultivation traditions of local hunter-gatherers.
papua-new-guinea.title: Agriculture in Papua New Guinea

picture.credit: The original uploader was Dr. Blofeld at English

papua-new-guinea.text: Mining in Papua New Guinea is an important part of the Papua New Guinean economy.
papua-new-guinea.title: Mining in Papua New Guinea

paraguay.text: Politics of Paraguay takes place in a framework of a presidential representative democratic republic. The National Constitution mandates a separation of powers in three branches. Executive power is exercised solely by the President.
paraguay.title: Politics of Paraguay

paraguay.text: Paraguay's population is distributed unevenly through the country. The vast majority of the people live in the eastern region, most within 160 kilometres of Asunción, the capital and largest city, which borders on Argentina to the south and west.
paraguay.title: Demographics of Paraguay

paraguay.text: During Alfredo Stroessner Mattiauda’s presidency, education initiatives took a backseat to economic concerns and the task of controlling political adversaries, and teacher salaries fell to extremely low levels. The constitution of 1992 attempted to remedy the long neglect of education.
paraguay.title: Education in Paraguay

paraguay.text: In terms of major health indicators, health in Paraguay ranks near the median among South American countries. In 2003 Paraguay had a child mortality rate of 59 deaths per 2000 children, ranking it behind Argentina, Colombia, and Uruguay but ahead of Brazil and Bolivia.
paraguay.title: Health in Paraguay

paraguay.text: This is a list of rivers in Paraguay.
paraguay.title: List of rivers of Paraguay

paraguay.text: The country of Paraguay lies geologically at the borderzone between several cratons. Due to thick Cenozoic sediment cover and regolith development few outcrops are available in Paraguay.
paraguay.title: Geology of Paraguay

paraguay.text: The climate of Paraguay consists of a subtropical climate in the Paranaense region, and tropical and semi-arid climates in the Chaco. The Paranaense region has a humid climate, with abundant rainfall throughout the year and only moderate seasonal changes in temperature.
paraguay.title: Climate of Paraguay

paraguay.text: Paraguayan foreign policy has concentrated on maintaining good relations with its neighbors, and it has been an active proponent of regional co-operation. It is a member of the United Nations and has served one term in the UN Security Council in 1967–1969.
paraguay.title: Foreign relations of Paraguay

paraguay.text: Paraguay gained independence from Spain in 1811.
paraguay.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Paraguay

paraguay.text: The music of Paraguay includes a variety of traditional, popular, and classical musical styles. The most famous forms of traditional music include Paraguayan polka and Guarania.
paraguay.title: Music of Paraguay

paraguay.text: Paraguayan cuisine is the set of dishes and culinary techniques of Paraguay. It has a marked influence of the Guaraní people combined with the Spanish cuisine and other marked influences coming from the immigration received by bordering countries such as Italian cuisine and German cuisine.
paraguay.title: Paraguayan cuisine

paraguay.text: The following are national holidays in Paraguay
paraguay.title: Public holidays in Paraguay

paraguay.text: Christianity is the predominant religion in Paraguay, with Catholicism being its largest denomination. Before the arrival of Spanish missionaries, the people residing in the territory of modern-day Paraguay practiced a variety of religions.
paraguay.title: Religion in Paraguay

paraguay.text: The Republic of Paraguay is a mostly bilingual country, as the majority of the population uses Spanish and Guaraní. The Constitution of Paraguay of 1992 declares it as a multicultural and bilingual country, establishing Spanish and Guaraní as official languages.
paraguay.title: Languages of Paraguay

paraguay.text: The cinema of Paraguay has historically been small.
paraguay.title: Cinema of Paraguay

paraguay.text: Sport in Paraguay is an important part of national culture. Association football is the most popular sport, while basketball is also very popular. Other sports such as padel, volleyball, futsal, swimming and tennis are popular as well.
paraguay.title: Sport in Paraguay

paraguay.text: The development of a distinct architectural style in Paraguay is relatively recent. This is due partially to the European influence following the colonization of the country in 1537.
paraguay.title: Paraguayan architecture

paraguay.text: Paraguay's transportation system ranges from adequate to poor, largely depending on the region of the country. The country has a network of roads, railroads, rivers, and airports, but significant infrastructure and regulation improvements are needed.
paraguay.title: Transport in Paraguay

paraguay.text: Tourism in Paraguay employs only 9,500 people, according to data from 2010. Paraguay was the least visited country of South America after Guyana and Suriname, with only 610,000 international tourists for the period 2013–2014.
paraguay.title: Tourism in Paraguay

paraguay.text: Telecommunications in Paraguay are meager. Paraguay has the lowest fixed-line telephone density in South America, with 5.6 lines per 100 residents, compared with 8.7 per 100 in Bolivia, 21.9 in Brazil, and 24.9 in Argentina.
paraguay.title: Telecommunications in Paraguay

paraguay.text: Throughout its history, agriculture in Paraguay has been the mainstay of the economy. This trend has continued today and in the late 1980s the agricultural sector generally accounted for 48 percent of the nation's employment, 23 percent of GDP, and 98 percent of export earnings.
paraguay.title: Agriculture in Paraguay

paraguay.text: Energy in Paraguay is primarily sourced from hydropower, with pivotal projects like the Itaipu Dam, one of the world's largest hydroelectric facilities.
paraguay.title: Energy in Paraguay

paraguay.text: The mineral industry of Paraguay includes the production of cement, iron and steel, and petroleum derivatives. Paraguay has no known natural gas or oil reserves. To meet its crude oil and petroleum products demand, Paraguay relies completely on imports of approximately 25,400 barrels per day.
paraguay.title: Mineral industry of Paraguay

people-s-republic-of-china.text: In the People's Republic of China, politics functions within the parameters of a unitary socialist state, in which the ruling Chinese Communist Party enacts its policies through people's congresses.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Politics of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The People's Republic of China is the second most-populous country in the world with a population exceeding 1.4 billion, only surpassed by India. China was the world's most populous country until it was surpassed by India in 2023.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Demographics of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Education in the People's Republic of China is primarily managed by the state-run public education system, which falls under the Ministry of Education. By law, education in the People's Republic of China is led by the Chinese Communist Party and adheres to its ideology.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Education in China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Health in the People's Republic of China encompasses the country's health status, health-care system, major public health issues, and health policy.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Health in China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Rivers that flow through China are as follows. The list is organized according to the body of water into which each river empties, beginning with the Sea of Okhotsk in the northeast, moving clockwise on a map and ending with the Arctic Ocean.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: List of rivers of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The geology of China consists of three Precambrian cratons surrounded by a number of orogenic belts. The modern tectonic environment is dominated by the continued collision of India with the rest of Asia starting 40–50 million years ago.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Geology of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: China's vast and diverse landscape is home to a profound variety and abundance of wildlife. As of one of 17 megadiverse countries in the world, China has, according to one measure, 7,516 species of vertebrates including 4,936 fish, 1,269 bird, 562 mammal, 403 reptile and 346 amphibian species.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Wildlife of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The following is an incomplete list of mountains in the People's Republic of China, sorted in alphabetical order.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: List of mountains in China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Owing to tremendous differences in latitude, longitude, and altitude, the climate of China is extremely diverse. It ranges from tropical or subtropical in the far south to subarctic in the far north, and alpine in the higher elevations of the Tibetan Plateau. Each region has dominant weather events.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Climate of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The People's Republic of China, has full diplomatic relations with 180 out of the other 192 United Nations member states, the Cook Islands, Niue, and Palestine. As of 2024, the country has the most diplomatic missions of any state.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Foreign relations of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The recorded military history of China extends from about 2200 BC to the present day. This history can be divided into the military history of China before 1912, when a revolution overthrew the imperial state, and the period of the Republic of China Army and the People's Liberation Army.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Military history of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The history of the postage stamps and postal history of China is complicated by the gradual decay of Imperial China and the years of civil war and Japanese occupation in the 1930s and 1940s. In modern times, postal delivery is handled by China Post.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Postage stamps and postal history of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The music of China consists of many distinct traditions, often specifically originating with one of the country's various ethnic groups. It is produced within the country, involving people of Chinese origin, the use of traditional Chinese instruments, Chinese music theory, or the languages of China.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Music of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Chinese cuisine comprises cuisines originating from China, that varies with the country's large population and geographic diversity, as well as from Chinese people from other parts of the world.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Chinese cuisine

people-s-republic-of-china.text: There are currently seven official public holidays in the People's Republic of China. Each year's holidays are announced about one month before the start of the year by the General Office of the State Council.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Public holidays in China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Religion in China is diverse and most Chinese people are either non-religious or practice a combination of Buddhism and Taoism with a Confucian worldview, which is collectively termed Chinese folk religion. Freedom of religion is substantially curtailed in China.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Religion in China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: There are several hundred languages in the People's Republic of China. The predominant language is Standard Chinese, which is based on the Beijing dialect, but there are hundreds of related Chinese languages, collectively known as Hanyu, that are spoken by 92% of the population.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Languages of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The cinema of China is the filmmaking and film industry of mainland China, one of three distinct historical threads of Chinese-language cinema together with the cinema of Hong Kong and the cinema of Taiwan.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Cinema of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Sports in the People's Republic of China consists of a variety of competitive sports. Traditional Chinese culture regards physical fitness as an important characteristic. China has its own national quadrennial multi-sport event similar to the Olympic Games called the National Games.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Sport in China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Chinese architecture is the embodiment of an architectural style that has developed over millennia in China and has influenced architecture throughout East Asia. Since its emergence during the early ancient era, the structural principles of its architecture have remained largely unchanged.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Chinese architecture

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The history of Chinese literature extends thousands of years, and begins with the earliest recorded inscriptions, court archives, building to the major works of philosophy and history written during the Axial Age.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Chinese literature

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Chinese art is visual art that originated in or is practiced in China, Greater China or by Chinese artists. Art created by Chinese residing outside of China can also be considered a part of Chinese art when it is based on or draws on Chinese culture, heritage, and history.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Chinese art

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Transport in China has experienced major growth and expansion in recent years. Although China's transport system comprises a vast network of transport nodes across its huge territory, the nodes tend to concentrate in the more economically developed coastal areas and inland cities along major rivers.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Transport in China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Tourism in China is a growing industry that is becoming a significant part of the Chinese economy. The rate of tourism has accelerated over the last few decades since the beginning of reform and opening up.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Tourism in China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The People's Republic of China possesses a diversified communications system that links all parts of the country by Internet, telephone, telegraph, radio, and television.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Telecommunications in China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: Agriculture has been a cornerstone of the People's Republic of China and its predecessors' economy and culture for millennia, supporting one of the world's largest populations and driving economic development.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Agriculture in China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: The People's Republic of China is both the world's largest energy consumer and the largest industrial country. China is currently the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gases, and coal in China is a major cause of global warming.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Energy policy of China

people-s-republic-of-china.text: As of 2022, more than 200 types of minerals are actively explored or mined in the People's Republic of China. These resources are widely but not evenly distributed throughout the country.
people-s-republic-of-china.title: Mining industry of China

peru.text: The politics of the Republic of Peru takes place in a framework of a unitary semi-presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the President of Peru is both head of state and head of government, and of a pluriform multi-party system.
peru.title: Politics of Peru

peru.text: This is a demography of the population of Peru including population density, ethnicity, religious affiliations and other aspects of the population. Peru is a multiethnic country, which means that it is home to people of many different historical backgrounds.
peru.title: Demographics of Peru

peru.text: Education in Peru is under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Education, which oversees formulating, implementing and supervising the national educational policy. According to the Constitution of Peru, education is compulsory and free in public schools for the initial, primary and secondary levels.
peru.title: Education in Peru

peru.text: Health in Peru has changed drastically from pre-colonial times to the modern era. When European conquistadors invaded Peru, they brought with them diseases against which the Inca population had no acquired immunity.
peru.title: Health in Peru

peru.text: This is a list of rivers of Peru, that are at least partially in Peru. The Peruvian government has published guidelines for the preparation of river flow studies in April 2015.
peru.title: List of rivers of Peru

peru.text: The geology of Peru includes ancient Proterozoic rocks, Paleozoic and Mesozoic volcanic and sedimentary rocks, and numerous basins and the Andes Mountains formed in the Cenozoic.
peru.title: Geology of Peru

peru.text: Peru has some of the greatest biodiversity in the world. It belongs to the select group of mega diverse countries because of the presence of the Andes, Amazon rainforest, and the Pacific Ocean. It has the fourth-most tropical forests of any country and the ninth-most forest area.
peru.title: Wildlife of Peru

peru.text: Climate of Peru describes the diverse climates of this large South American country with an area of 1,285,216 km2. Peru is located entirely in the tropics but features desert and mountain climates as well as tropical rainforests.
peru.title: Climate of Peru

peru.text: The foreign relations of Peru are managed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. As an important first-tier state in South America, Peru has been a member of the United Nations since 1945, and Peruvian Javier Pérez de Cuéllar served as UN Secretary General from 1981 to 1991.
peru.title: Foreign relations of Peru

picture.credit: Pacific Steam Navigation Company, Perkins Bacon;

peru.text: In Pre-Columbian times, the Inca Empire relied on messengers named chasquis for official communications; the chasquis used a special stone-paved road named Capac Ñan, and quipus, cotton or camelid fiber strings, collecting data with a special pattern of knots and colors.
peru.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Peru

peru.text: Peruvian music is an amalgamation of sounds and styles drawing on Peru's Andean, Spanish, and African roots.
peru.title: Music of Peru

peru.text: Peruvian cuisine refers to the culinary and gastronomical traditions of Peru, which originated in the pre-Columbian indigenous populations in its three main geographical regions along the Pacific coast, the Andes and the Amazonian areas.
peru.title: Peruvian cuisine

peru.text: The following is a list of public holidays in Peru.
peru.title: Public holidays in Peru

peru.text: Christianity is the most widely professed religion in Peru, with Catholicism being its largest denomination. Religion in Peru is traditionally related to religious syncretism originating from Catholicism with the ancient Inca religion after the Spanish Conquest.
peru.title: Religion in Peru

peru.text: Peru has many languages in use, with its official languages being Spanish, Quechua and Aymara. Spanish was introduced by conquistadors in the 1500s; it began being taught in the time of José Pardo instead of the country's Native languages, especially the languages in the Andes.
peru.title: Languages of Peru

peru.text: While the Peruvian film industry has not been nearly as prolific as that of some other Latin American countries, such as Mexico or Argentina, some Peruvian movies produced enjoyed regional success.
peru.title: Cinema of Peru

peru.text: Sports in Peru are popular and widespread.
peru.title: Sport in Peru

peru.text: Peruvian architecture is the architecture carried out during any time in what is now Peru, and by Peruvian architects worldwide. Its diversity and long history spans from ancient Peru, the Inca Empire, Colonial Peru to the present day.
peru.title: Architecture of Peru

peru.text: The term Peruvian literature not only refers to literature produced in the independent Republic of Peru, but also to literature produced in the Viceroyalty of Peru during the country's colonial period, and to oral artistic forms created by diverse ethnic groups that existed in the area during the prehispanic period, such as the Quechua, the Aymara and the Chanka South American native groups.
peru.title: Peruvian literature

peru.text: Peruvian art has its origin in the Andean civilizations. These civilizations rose in the territory of modern Peru before the arrival of the Spanish.
peru.title: Peruvian art

peru.text: This article describes the transport in Peru.
peru.title: Transport in Peru

peru.text: Since the 2000s, Tourism in Peru has made up the nation's third largest industry, behind fishing and mining.
peru.title: Tourism in Peru

peru.text: Telecommunications in Peru include radio and television, fixed and mobile telephones, and the Internet.
peru.title: Telecommunications in Peru

peru.text: The agricultural history of Peru includes agriculture, cultivation of plants and herbs and general changes in the history of farming in Peru or its historical regions.
peru.title: Agricultural history of Peru

peru.text: The electricity sector in Peru has experienced large improvements in the past 15 years. Access to electricity has increased from 45% in 1990 to 96.4% in 2018, while service quality and efficiency of service provision improved.
peru.title: Electricity sector in Peru

peru.text: The mineral industry of Peru has played an important role in the nation's history and been integral to the country's economic growth for several decades.
peru.title: Mineral industry of Peru
