south-africa.text: This is a list of rivers in South Africa. It is quite common to find the Afrikaans word -rivier as part of the name. Another common suffix is "-kamma", from the Khoisan term for "river". The Zulu / Xhosa word amanzi also forms part of some river names.
south-africa.title: List of rivers of South Africa

south-africa.text: The geology of South Africa is highly varied including cratons, greenstone belts, large impact craters as well as orogenic belts. The geology of the country is the base for a large mining sector that extracts gold, diamonds, iron and coal from world-class deposits.
south-africa.title: Geology of South Africa

south-africa.text: The wildlife of South Africa consists of the flora and fauna of this country in Southern Africa. The country has a range of different habitat types and an ecologically rich and diverse wildlife, vascular plants being particularly abundant, many of them endemic to the country.
south-africa.title: Wildlife of South Africa

south-africa.text: List of Mountains in South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini is a general list of mountains in South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini with elevation.
south-africa.title: List of mountains in South Africa

south-africa.text: The climate of South Africa is determined by South Africa's geographic situation between 22°S and 35°S, in the Southern Hemisphere's subtropical zone, and its location between two oceans, Atlantic and the Indian.
south-africa.title: Climate of South Africa

south-africa.text: The foreign relations of South Africa have spanned from the country's time as a dominion of the British Empire to its isolationist policies under apartheid to its position as a responsible international actor taking a key role in Africa, particularly southern Africa.
south-africa.title: Foreign relations of South Africa

south-africa.text: The military history of South Africa chronicles a vast time period and complex events from the dawn of history until the present time. It covers civil wars and wars of aggression and of self-defense both within South Africa and against it.
south-africa.title: Military history of South Africa

south-africa.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of South Africa. The Republic of South Africa, previously The Union of South Africa, is a country located at the southern tip of Africa, with a coastline on the Atlantic and Indian Oceans.
south-africa.title: Postage stamps and postal history of South Africa

south-africa.text: The music of South Africa exhibits a culturally varied musical heritage in conjunction with the multi-ethnic populace.
south-africa.title: Music of South Africa

south-africa.text: South African cuisine draws from the culinary traditions of the various communities that inhabit the country.
south-africa.title: South African cuisine

south-africa.text: A list of current public holidays in South Africa: In gold, the National Day The Public Holidays Act states that whenever a public holiday falls on a Sunday, the Monday following it will be a public holiday.
south-africa.title: Public holidays in South Africa

south-africa.text: Religion in South Africa is dominated by various branches of Christianity, which collectively represent over 85% of the country's total population. South Africa is a secular state with a diverse religious population. Its constitution guarantees freedom of religion.
south-africa.title: Religion in South Africa

south-africa.text: South Africa is a linguistically diverse country and has twelve official languages: Ndebele, Sepedi, Sotho, South African Sign Language, Swazi, Tsonga, Tswana, Venda, Afrikaans, Xhosa, Zulu, and English, which is the primary language used in parliamentary and state discourse, though all official languages are equal in legal status.
south-africa.title: Languages of South Africa

south-africa.text: The cinema of South Africa refers to the films and film industry of South Africa. Films have been made in English and Afrikaans. Many foreign films have been produced about South Africa, including many involving race relations.
south-africa.title: Cinema of South Africa

south-africa.text: Sport has a significant role in South African culture. The three most popular mainstream sports in the country—cricket, football and rugby union—reflect the country's early British colonial influence.
south-africa.title: Sport in South Africa

south-africa.text: South African literature is the literature of South Africa, which has 11 national languages: Afrikaans, English, Zulu, Xhosa, Sotho, Pedi, Tswana, Venda, Swazi, Tsonga and Ndebele.
south-africa.title: South African literature

south-africa.text: South African art is the visual art produced by the people inhabiting the territory occupied by the modern country of South Africa. The oldest art objects in the world were discovered in a South African cave.
south-africa.title: South African art

south-africa.text: South Africa has a diverse and extensive transport system that includes road, rail, air, and maritime infrastructure. The country has the most developed road network in Africa, and the 10th-largest in the world, at approximately 750,000 kilometers.
south-africa.title: Transport in South Africa

south-africa.text: South Africa is a major global tourist destination, with the tourism industry accounting for 5.8% of the country's GDP as of May 2026, according to Statistics South Africa. In 2025, South Africa's international passenger arrivals reached a record 10.5 million people.
south-africa.title: Tourism in South Africa

south-africa.text: Telecommunications infrastructure in South Africa is advanced and widespread, comprising a combination of mobile, satellite, and fiber optic internet. Services are provided by many competing players in the private market, as well as by the South African Government through multiple public programs.
south-africa.title: Telecommunications in South Africa

south-africa.text: Agriculture in South Africa contributes around 5% of formal employment, relatively low compared to other parts of Africa, and the number is still decreasing, as well as providing work for casual laborers and contributing around 2.8 percent of GDP for the nation.
south-africa.title: Agriculture in South Africa

south-africa.text: South Africa has a large energy sector, being the largest economy in Africa. The country consumed 227 TWh of electricity in 2018. The vast majority of South Africa's electricity is produced from coal, with the fuel responsible for 88% of production in 2017.
south-africa.title: Energy in South Africa

south-africa.text: Mining in South Africa was once the main driving force behind the history and development of Africa's most advanced and richest economy.
south-africa.title: Mining industry of South Africa

south-korea.text: The politics of South Korea take place in the framework of a presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the president is the head of state, and of a multi-party system.
south-korea.title: Politics of South Korea

south-korea.text: Demographic features of South Korea's population include population density, ethnicity, education level, health, economic status, religious affiliations, and other aspects of the population.
south-korea.title: Demographics of South Korea

south-korea.text: Education in South Korea is provided by both public schools and private schools with government funding available for both. South Korea is known for its high academic performance in reading, mathematics, and science, consistently ranking above the OECD average.
south-korea.title: Education in South Korea

south-korea.text: Life expectancy has been rising rapidly and South Korea ranked 3rd in the world for life expectancy.
south-korea.title: Health in South Korea

south-korea.text: The geology of South Korea includes rocks dating to the Archean and two large massifs of metamorphic rock as the crystalline basement, overlain by thick sedimentary sequences, younger metamorphic rocks and volcanic deposits.
south-korea.title: Geology of South Korea

south-korea.text: The wildlife of South Korea includes 8,271 plant species, 18,117 animal species and 3,528 species of fungi and others. 30,000 species are known to inhabit South Korea, among an estimated 100,000+ in all.
south-korea.title: Wildlife of South Korea

south-korea.text: The following is the mountains in South Korea by height.
south-korea.title: List of mountains in South Korea

south-korea.text: South Korea maintains diplomatic relations with every United Nations member state except for North Korea. The country is a member of the United Nations, WTO, OECD/DAC, ASEAN Plus Three, East Asia Summit, and G-20.
south-korea.title: Foreign relations of South Korea

south-korea.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of South Korea. In 1945, Korea was liberated from Empire of Japan's colonial rule at the end of World War II, but soon divided into North and South Korea. South Korea began to issue its own stamps from 1946.
south-korea.title: Postage stamps and postal history of South Korea

south-korea.text: The music of South Korea has evolved over the course of the decades since the end of the Korean War, and has its roots in the music of the Korean people, who have inhabited the Korean Peninsula for over a millennium.
south-korea.title: Music of South Korea

picture.credit: Korea.net / Korean Culture and Information Servi

south-korea.text: South Korea is a country in East Asia constituting the southern part of the Korean Peninsula. It is bordered to the north by North Korea, and the two countries are separated by the Korean Demilitarized Zone. Some dishes are shared by the two Koreas.
south-korea.title: South Korean cuisine

south-korea.text: Public holidays in South Korea each belong to one or more of three categories: National day National flag raising day Public holiday: on these days, the general working population gets a day off, and employers are legally required to pay their employees. Each category has a different legal basis.
south-korea.title: Public holidays in South Korea

south-korea.text: A majority of South Koreans are irreligious. Christianity and Buddhism are the dominant confessions among those who affiliate with a formal religion.
south-korea.title: Religion in South Korea

south-korea.text: South Korean films have been heavily influenced by such events and forces as the Korea under Japanese rule, the Korean War, government censorship, the business sector, globalization, and the democratization of South Korea.
south-korea.title: Cinema of South Korea

south-korea.text: South Korea has traditional sports of its own, as well as sports imported from other cultures and countries. Football and baseball have traditionally been regarded as the most popular sports in Korea.
south-korea.title: Sport in South Korea

south-korea.text: South Korean architecture refers to any architecture in South Korea, which includes architecture from Neolithic–7th century, three-kingdoms of Korea, Goryeo, Joseon, Japanese occupation, Korean War, and modern architecture.
south-korea.title: Architecture of South Korea

south-korea.text: See also Culture of South Korea, Korean literature until 1945, and North Korean literature South Korean literature is literature written or produced in South Korea following the division of Korea into North and South in 1945. South Korean literature is primarily written in Korean.
south-korea.title: South Korean literature

south-korea.text: Transportation in South Korea is provided by extensive networks of railways, highways, bus routes, ferry services and air routes that traverse the country.
south-korea.title: Transport in South Korea

south-korea.text: Tourism in South Korea and its industry caters to both foreign and domestic tourists. The country has 16 World Heritage Sites, including Changdeokgung Palace, Namhansanseong and Hwaseong Fortress. Seoul is the principal tourist destination for visitors.
south-korea.title: Tourism in South Korea

south-korea.text: In South Korea, telecommunications services improved dramatically in the 1980s with the assistance of foreign partners and as a result of the development of the electronics industry.
south-korea.title: Telecommunications in South Korea

south-korea.text: Agriculture in South Korea is a sector of the economy of South Korea. Korean agriculture is the basic industry of the Korean economy, consisting of farming, animal husbandry, forestry and fishing.
south-korea.title: Agriculture in South Korea

south-korea.text: South Korea is a major energy importer, importing nearly all of its oil needs and ranking as the third-largest importer of liquefied natural gas in the world in 2024.
south-korea.title: Energy in South Korea

south-sudan.text: The politics of South Sudan concern the system of government in the Republic of South Sudan, a country in East Africa, and the people, organizations, and events involved in it. As a region, the Republic of South Sudan gained autonomy in 2005 with former rebel leader Dr.
south-sudan.title: Politics of South Sudan

south-sudan.text: South Sudan is home to around 60 indigenous ethnic groups and 80 linguistic partitions among a 2021 population of around 11 million.
south-sudan.title: Demographics of South Sudan

south-sudan.text: Education in South Sudan is modelled after the educational system of the Republic of Sudan. Primary education consists of eight years, followed by four years of secondary education, and then four years of university instruction; the 8 + 4 + 4 system, in place since 1990.
south-sudan.title: Education in South Sudan

south-sudan.text: South Sudan has one of the weakest health systems in the world, marked by a severely degraded public health system, shortages of qualified health workers, and restricted access to care.
south-sudan.title: Health in South Sudan

south-sudan.text: This is a list of streams and rivers in South Sudan, arranged geographically by drainage basin. There is an alphabetic list at the end of this article. The list may not be comprehensive.
south-sudan.title: List of rivers of South Sudan

south-sudan.text: The geology of South Sudan is founded on Precambrian igneous and metamorphic rocks, that cover 40 percent of the country's surface and underlie other rock units.
south-sudan.title: Geology of South Sudan

south-sudan.text: The wildlife of South Sudan refers to the natural flora and fauna of South Sudan. South Sudan includes the Sudd, one of the world's largest wetlands. According to the American biologist and conservationist, J.
south-sudan.title: Wildlife of South Sudan

south-sudan.text: The Republic of South Sudan established relations with sovereign states and international organizations following independence on 9 July 2011, including the African Union and United Nations. South Sudan's former ruling country of Sudan was the first state in the world to recognize South Sudan.
south-sudan.title: Foreign relations of South Sudan

south-sudan.text: The Republic of South Sudan became independent on 9 July 2011 from Sudan and issued its first stamps on 13 July 2011. Only almost three months later, on 4 October 2011, did South Sudan become a member of the Universal Postal Union. Before independence, South Sudan used stamps issued by Sudan.
south-sudan.title: Postage stamps and postal history of South Sudan

south-sudan.text: South Sudanese cuisine is based on grains. It uses yams, potatoes, vegetables, legumes, meat, okra and fruit as well. Meat is boiled, grilled or dried. South Sudanese cuisine was influenced by Arab cuisine.
south-sudan.title: South Sudanese cuisine

south-sudan.text: This is a list of public holidays in South Sudan.
south-sudan.title: Public holidays in South Sudan

south-sudan.text: Christianity is the most widely professed religion in South Sudan, with significant minorities of the adherents of traditional faiths and Islam. President Salva Kiir, a Catholic, while speaking at St.
south-sudan.title: Religion in South Sudan

south-sudan.text: South Sudan is a multilingual country, with over 60 indigenous languages spoken. The official language of the country is English which was introduced in the region during the colonial era. Some of the indigenous languages with the most speakers include Dinka, Nuer, Shilluk, Bari, and Zande.
south-sudan.title: Languages of South Sudan

south-sudan.text: Cinema is a newly developing industry in South Sudan.
south-sudan.title: Cinema of South Sudan

south-sudan.text: Sports in South Sudan are still not widely recognized internationally. Many traditional and modern games and sports are popular in South Sudan, particularly wrestling and mock battles.
south-sudan.title: Sport in South Sudan

south-sudan.text: Despite high potential for tourism, especially ecotourism, tourism in South Sudan remains a small industry. The country is home to the world's second largest animal migration, six national parks, and 10 game reserves.
south-sudan.title: Tourism in South Sudan

south-sudan.text: Telecommunications in South Sudan includes fixed and mobile telephony, the Internet, radio, and television. Despite this progress, South Sudan remains one of the least connected countries globally, with limited infrastructure, high costs, and significant rural–urban disparities in access.
south-sudan.title: Telecommunications in South Sudan

south-sudan.text: South Sudan is one of the African countries known as an important oil producer, whereas, South Sudan also has mineral resources like copper, gold, diamonds, limestone among others. Government is promoting investment particularly in exploration and also developing the mining projects in South Sudan.
south-sudan.title: Mining industry of South Sudan

spain.text: The politics of Spain takes place under the framework established by the Constitution of 1978. Spain is established as a social and democratic sovereign country wherein the national sovereignty is vested in the people, from which the powers of the state emanate.
spain.title: Politics of Spain

spain.text: As of 1 October 2026, Spain had a total population of 49,935,642. Spain's population surpassed 49 million inhabitants for the first time in 2025.
spain.title: Demographics of Spain

spain.text: Education in Spain is compulsory and free for all children aged between 6 and 16 years and is supported by the national government together with the governments of each of the country's 17 autonomous communities. In Spain, primary school and secondary school are considered basic education.
spain.title: Education in Spain

spain.text: In 2012, life expectancy at birth in Spain reached 82.5 years, one of the highest among OECD countries and more than two years higher than the OECD average. Only Japan, Iceland and Switzerland had a higher life expectancy than Spain in 2012.
spain.title: Health in Spain

spain.text: This is an incomplete list of rivers that are at least partially in Spain. The rivers flowing into the sea are sorted along the coast. Rivers flowing into other rivers are listed by the rivers they flow into.
spain.title: List of rivers of Spain

spain.text: The wildlife of Spain includes the diverse flora and fauna of Spain.
spain.title: Wildlife of Spain

spain.text: This is a list of Spanish mountains with their elevation taken from the Instituto Nacional de Estadística de España data. Where available is also reported the mountains' prominence.
spain.title: List of mountains in Spain

spain.text: The climate of Spain is highly diverse and varies considerably across the country's various regions. In fact, Spain is sometimes described as the most climatically diverse country in Europe and has 13 different Köppen climates.
spain.title: Climate of Spain

spain.text: The foreign relations of Spain could be constructed upon the foreign relations of the Hispanic Crown. The personal union of Castile and Aragon that ensued with the joint rule of the Catholic Monarchs was followed by the annexation of the Kingdom of Granada and the Kingdom of Navarre.
spain.title: Foreign relations of Spain

spain.text: The military history of Spain, from the period of the Carthaginian conquests over the Phoenicians to the former Afghan War spans a period of more than 2200 years, and includes the history of battles fought in the territory of modern Spain, as well as her former and current overseas possessions and territories, and the military history of the people of Spain, regardless of geography.
spain.title: Military history of Spain

spain.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Spain. A royal decree of 12 September 1861 established the Fábrica del Sello as the exclusive printer of Spanish stamps.
spain.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Spain

spain.text: The musical traditions of Spain have played an important role in the development of both western classical and Latin American music. Spanish music includes many different traditional styles from across the country, among which flamenco and classical guitar are probably the best-known abroad.
spain.title: Music of Spain

spain.text: Spanish cuisine consists of the traditions and practices of Spanish cooking. It features considerable regional diversity, with significant differences in different parts of the country.
spain.title: Spanish cuisine

spain.text: Public holidays celebrated in Spain include a mix of religious, national and regional observances.
spain.title: Public holidays in Spain

spain.text: Christianity is the most widely professed religion in Spain, with Catholicism being its main denomination, along with high levels of secularization as of 2026. Spain is a secular state and freedom of religion is guaranteed by the Spanish Constitution.
spain.title: Religion in Spain

spain.text: The majority of the languages of Spain belong to the Romance language family. The official national language is Spanish.
spain.title: Languages of Spain

spain.text: The cinema of Spain, or Spanish cinema, comprises the film industry and its film productions, whether made within Spain or by Spanish film production companies abroad. The most important spanish directors are Luis Buñuel, Carlos Saura and Pedro Almodóvar.
spain.title: Cinema of Spain

spain.text: Sport in Spain has been highly successful through the late 20th century and early 21st century, in a wide variety of disciplines. The most popular and high profile sport in Spain is football.
spain.title: Sport in Spain

spain.text: Spanish architecture refers to architecture in any area of what is now Spain, and by Spanish architects worldwide, influencing mainly areas of what was once part of the Spanish Empire.
spain.title: Spanish architecture

spain.text: Spanish literature is literature written in the Spanish language within the territory that presently constitutes the Kingdom of Spain.
spain.title: Spanish literature

spain.text: Spanish art has been an important contributor to Western art and Spain has produced many famous and influential artists including Velázquez, Goya and Picasso.
spain.title: Spanish art

spain.text: Transport in Spain is characterised by a network of roads, railways, trams, air routes, and ports. Its geographic location makes it an important link between Europe, Africa, and the Americas.
spain.title: Transport in Spain

spain.text: Tourism in Spain is a major component of the national economy. In 2024, domestic and international tourism combined accounted for 12.6% of Spain’s GDP. The characteristic tourism branches generated more than 2.7 million jobs, representing 12.3% of total employment.
spain.title: Tourism in Spain

spain.text: Telecommunications in Spain is accomplished through the transmission of information by various types of technologies within Spain.
spain.title: Telecommunications in Spain

spain.text: Agriculture in Spain is important to the national economy. The primary sector activities accounting for agriculture, husbandry, fishing and silviculture represented a 2.7% of the Spanish GDP in 2017, with an additional 2.5% represented by the agrofood industry.
spain.title: Agriculture in Spain

spain.text: Primary energy consumption in Spain in 2020 was mainly composed of fossil fuel sources. The largest sources are petroleum, natural gas and coal. The remaining 26.3% is accounted for by nuclear energy and various renewable energy sources.
spain.title: Energy in Spain

sri-lanka.text: Sri Lanka is a unitary multi-party semi-presidential representative democratic republic, whereby the President of Sri Lanka is both head of state and head of government. Executive power is exercised by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Cabinet of Ministers.
sri-lanka.title: Politics of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: Sri Lanka is an island in the Indian Ocean, formerly known as Ceylon and also by many other names. It is about the size of Ireland. It is about 28 kilometres off the south-eastern coast of India with a population of about 22 million.
sri-lanka.title: Demographics of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: Education in Sri Lanka has a long history that dates back two millennia.
sri-lanka.title: Education in Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: Sri Lanka scores higher than the regional average in healthcare having a high life expectancy and a lower maternal and infant death rate than its neighbors. In 2018 life expectancy was 72.1 for men and 78.5 for women ranking the country 70th in the world.
sri-lanka.title: Health in Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: The following table lists most rivers of Sri Lanka. Since Sri Lanka is a trilingual country, some rivers may have a Sinhala name, while other have an English or a Tamil name.
sri-lanka.title: List of rivers of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: More than 90% of Sri Lanka's surface lies on Precambrian strata, some of it dating back 2 billion years.
sri-lanka.title: Geology of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: The wildlife of Sri Lanka includes its flora and fauna and their natural habitats. Sri Lanka has one of the highest rates of biological endemism.
sri-lanka.title: Wildlife of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: The following page lists the mountain peaks of Sri Lanka. The following list comprises mountains that have been thoroughly explored, with their altitudes measured by expert hikers in Sri Lanka.
sri-lanka.title: List of mountains of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: Foreign relations of Sri Lanka refers to the diplomatic and commercial relations between Sri Lanka and other countries. Sri Lanka has stressed its principle of "friendship towards all, enmity towards none" in its diplomacy.
sri-lanka.title: Foreign relations of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: This is a survey of the postage stamps and postal history of Sri Lanka, formerly known as Ceylon. Sri Lanka is an island country in South Asia, located about 31 km off the southern coast of India.
sri-lanka.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: The music of Sri Lanka has its roots in five primary influences: ancient folk rituals, Hindu religious traditions, Buddhist religious traditions, the legacy of European colonisation, and the commercial and historical influence of nearby Indian culture—specifically, Kollywood cinema and Bollywood cinema.
sri-lanka.title: Music of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: Sri Lankan cuisine is known for its particular combinations of herbs, spices, fish, vegetables, rices, and fruits. The cuisine is highly centred around many varieties of rice, as well as coconut which is a ubiquitous plant throughout the country.
sri-lanka.title: Sri Lankan cuisine

sri-lanka.text: Sri Lanka is officially a Buddhist country, however Sri Lankans practice a variety of religions. As of the 2024 census, 69.8% of Sri Lankans were Buddhists, 12.6% were Hindus, 10.7% were Muslims, 7.6% were Christians.
sri-lanka.title: Religion in Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: The main languages spoken in Sri Lanka are Sinhala and Tamil. Several languages are spoken in Sri Lanka within the Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, and Austronesian families. Sri Lanka accords official status to Sinhala and Tamil, with English as a recognised language.
sri-lanka.title: Languages of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: Sri Lankan cinema encompasses the Sri Lankan film industry. It is a fledgling industry that has struggled to find a footing since its inauguration in 1947 with Kadawunu Poronduwa produced by S. M. Nayagam of Chitra Kala Movietone.
sri-lanka.title: Cinema of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: Sport in Sri Lanka is a significant part of Sri Lankan culture. Popular sports include cricket, rugby union, water sports, badminton, athletics sports, football, basketball and tennis.
sri-lanka.title: Sport in Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: The architecture of Sri Lanka displays a rich variety of architectural forms and styles. Buddhism has had a significant influence on Sri Lankan architecture, since it was introduced to the island in the 3rd century BCE.
sri-lanka.title: Architecture of Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: Sri Lankan literature is the literary tradition of Sri Lanka. The largest part of Sri Lankan literature was written in the Sinhala language, but there is a considerable number of works in other languages used in Sri Lanka over the millennia.
sri-lanka.title: Sri Lankan literature

sri-lanka.text: Visual arts in Sri Lanka refers to a variety of visual art forms, including as painting, drawing, sculpture architecture and other visual arts from the ancient time to modern Sri Lanka.
sri-lanka.title: Sri Lankan art

sri-lanka.text: Transport in Sri Lanka is based on its road network, which is centred on the country's commercial capital Colombo. A rail network handles a portion of Sri Lanka's transport needs.
sri-lanka.title: Transport in Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: Sri Lanka is a popular tourist destination. Tourism is a key industry that attracts international tourists yearly. Foreigners visit Sri Lanka to see nature, wildlife, historical monuments, and indigenous culture.
sri-lanka.title: Tourism in Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: Telecommunications in Sri Lanka commenced in 1858 after the first telegraphic circuit between Colombo and Galle was commenced. The sector continues to grow in the modern times.
sri-lanka.title: Telecommunications in Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: The primary form of agriculture in Sri Lanka is rice production. Rice is cultivated during Maha and Yala seasons. Tea is cultivated in the central highlands and is a major source of foreign exchange. Vegetables, fruits and oilseed crops are also cultivated in the country.
sri-lanka.title: Agriculture in Sri Lanka

sri-lanka.text: The electricity sector in Sri Lanka has a national grid which is primarily powered by hydroelectric power and thermal power, with sources such as photovoltaics and wind power in early stages of deployment.
sri-lanka.title: Electricity sector in Sri Lanka

sudan.text: The politics of Sudan takes place in the context of a civil war between two factions of the country's military dictatorship. Sudan has usually been ruled by the military, interspersed with short periods of democratic parliamentary rule.
sudan.title: Politics of Sudan

sudan.text: The demographics of Sudan include the Sudanese people and their characteristics, Sudan, including population density, ethnicity, education level, health, economic status, religious affiliations, and other aspects of the population. In Sudan's 1993 census, the population was calculated at 30 million.
sudan.title: Demographics of Sudan

sudan.text: Education in Sudan is free and compulsory for children aged 6 to 13 years. Primary education up to the 2019/2020 academic year consists of eight years, followed by three years of secondary education.
sudan.title: Education in Sudan

sudan.text: Sudan, a country of about 52 million people, faces severe public health challenges shaped by decades of conflict, economic instability, and underfunded health services. Sudan has a predominantly young population, with a median age of 18.5 years.
sudan.title: Health in Sudan

sudan.text: This is a list of streams and rivers in Sudan, arranged geographically by drainage basin. There is an alphabetic list at the end of this article.
sudan.title: List of rivers of Sudan

sudan.text: The geology of Sudan formed primarily in the Precambrian, as igneous and metamorphic crystalline basement rock. Ancient terranes and inliers were intruded with granites, granitoids, and volcanic rocks.
sudan.title: Geology of Sudan

sudan.text: The wildlife of Sudan is composed of its flora and fauna. A variety of climate types in Sudan results in a wide range of habitats and the range of wildlife is diverse. Some 287 species of mammal have been recorded in the country and some 634 species of bird.
sudan.title: Wildlife of Sudan

sudan.text: The foreign relations of Sudan are generally in line with the Muslim Arab world, but are also based on Sudan's economic ties with the People's Republic of China and Russia.
sudan.title: Foreign relations of Sudan

sudan.text: The military history of Sudan, includes wars, fighting, the rise of states of power, and the resistance of forces along the Nile, the Red Sea coast, the Sahel and the southern frontiers.
sudan.title: Military history of Sudan

sudan.text: Sudan was governed by the United Kingdom and Egypt from 1898. Independence was proclaimed on 1 January, 1956, and independent Sudan became a member of the Universal Postal Union on 27 July 1956.
sudan.title: Postage stamps and postal history of Sudan

sudan.text: The rich and varied music of Sudan has traditional, rural, northeastern African roots and also shows Arabic, Western or other African influences, especially on the popular urban music from the early 20th century onwards.
sudan.title: Music of Sudan

sudan.text: Sudanese cuisine is greatly affected by the historical cross-cultural influences of Arab, Nubian, Egyptian, Turkish, Greek, and Levantine cuisine in Sudan. Many Sudanese foods have been around for thousands of years.
sudan.title: Sudanese cuisine

sudan.text: This is a list of holidays in Sudan. The following public holidays are the same every year: January 1: Independence Day January 7: Coptic Christmas December 25: Christmas Day Variable Coptic Easter The Prophet's Birthday Eid al-Fitr Islamic New Year Eid al-Adha
sudan.title: Public holidays in Sudan

sudan.text: The predominant religion in Sudan is Islam, practised by around 97% of the total population. Christianity is the second largest religion in the country, accounting for around 2.2% of the population. A minority of Sudanese adhere to indigenous beliefs, primarily in the Nuba Mountains.
sudan.title: Religion in Sudan

sudan.text: Sudan is a multilingual country dominated by Sudanese Arabic. In the 2005 constitution of the Republic of Sudan, the official languages of Sudan are Literary Arabic and English.
sudan.title: Languages of Sudan

sudan.text: Cinema of Sudan refers to both the history and present of the making or screening of films in cinemas or film festivals, as well as to the persons involved in this form of audiovisual culture of the Sudan and its history from the late nineteenth century onwards.
sudan.title: Cinema of Sudan

sudan.text: The architecture of Sudan mirrors the geographical, ethnic and cultural diversity of the country and its historical periods.
sudan.title: Architecture of Sudan

sudan.text: Sudanese literature consists of both oral as well as written works of fiction and nonfiction that were created during the cultural history of today's Republic of the Sudan.
sudan.title: Sudanese literature

sudan.text: Transport in Sudan during the early 1990s included an extensive railroad system that served the more important populated areas except in the far south, a meager road network, a natural inland waterway—the Nile River and its tributaries—and a national airline that provided both international and domestic service.
sudan.title: Transport in Sudan

sudan.text: Tourism in Sudan is a minor contributor to the country's economy. As of 2019, travel and tourism contributed about 2.4% of Sudan’s gross domestic product. Sudan is infrequently visited compared to other African countries, and long-running internal conflict has damaged the country's tourism industry.
sudan.title: Tourism in Sudan

sudan.text: Telecommunications in Sudan includes fixed and mobile telephones, the Internet, radio, and television. Approximately 12 million out of 45 million people in Sudan use the Internet, mainly on smartphones and mobile computers.
sudan.title: Telecommunications in Sudan

sudan.text: Agriculture in Sudan plays an important role in that country's economy. Agriculture and livestock raising are the main sources of livelihood for most of the Sudanese population.
sudan.title: Agriculture in Sudan

sudan.text: Energy in Sudan describes energy and electricity production, consumption and imports in Sudan. The chief sources of energy in 2010 were wood and charcoal, hydroelectric power, and oil. Sudan is a net energy exporter. Primary energy use in Sudan was 179 TWh and 4 TWh per million persons in 2008.
sudan.title: Energy in Sudan

sudan.text: The mining industry of Sudan is mostly driven by extraction fuel minerals, including gold. Prior to becoming independent in 2011 as South Sudan, petroleum extraction in the autonomous region of Southern Sudan accounted for a substantial contribution to the country's economy.
sudan.title: Mining industry of Sudan

suriname.text: Politics of Suriname take place in a framework of a representative democratic assembly independent presidential system, and in a multi-party system. Executive power is exercised by the government. The executive power is dependent on the Parliament in theory.
suriname.title: Politics of Suriname

suriname.text: This is a demography of the population of Suriname, including population density, ethnicity, education level, health of the populace, economic status, religious affiliations, and other aspects of the population. Most Surinamese people live in the narrow, northern coastal plain.
suriname.title: Demographics of Suriname

suriname.text: The education in Suriname was initially set up in analogy to the Dutch education system. In terms of structure, the education system is now a mixture of school types that were common in the Netherlands before, during and after the Mammoetwet.
suriname.title: Education in Suriname

suriname.text: The Human Rights Measurement Initiative finds that Suriname is fulfilling 78.4% of what it should be fulfilling for the right to health based on its level of income. When looking at the right to health with respect to children, Suriname achieves 94.0% of what is expected based on its current income.
suriname.title: Health in Suriname
